Reviewed/ Written by EricThePinkCat

Иногда всё, чего достаточно для успеха — простота и честность. A Game About Digging A Hole™ — это игра, которая честно и без обмана делает ровно то, что обещает в названии. Буквально. Ты копаешь яму. Долго. Методично. С нарастающим интересом и, как ни странно, удовольствием. Она ощущается как лихорадочный сон во время болезни, и её прохождение — именно в период болезни — стало для меня действительно аутентичным опытом.

9,5 часов для полного стопроцентного прохождения и все ради того, чтобы выкопать каждый кусочек на заднем дворе только что купленного дома в поисках обещанного сокровища как раз в то самое время, когда мне меньше всего хотелось сложных решений, напряженных диалогов и необходимости постоянно поддерживать фокус внимания. Это сработало почти идеально, и в итоге я просто отключила свою больную голову и осталась на уровне самых базовых ощущений. И выкопала, черт возьми, эту яму. Даже несколько раз...

Ты начинаешь с очень жалкого инструмента. Ковыряешь землю хаотично, медленно и неловко. В твоих карманах едва помещаются три камня, которые ты нашел, даже толком не успев вскрыть самый первый слой грунта. Энергия заканчивается быстро, ты вынужден часто возвращаться в гараж, продавать ресурсы и восполнять энергию. И постоянно кажется, будто если прямо сейчас купить улучшение, то не хватит на покупку энергии в следующий раз (хотя на самом деле всегда хватает). 

Шаг за шагом ты превращаешься в что-то вроде божества лопаты и гравитации: за спиной появляется реактивный ранец, а лопата становится настоящим буром, которым ты уже не вкапываешься, а вгрызаешься в пространство, превращая хаотичную почву в аккуратную, почти эстетичную дыру куда-то к центру Земли. И все это копание в куче грязи почему-то приносит какое-то по-настоящему первобытное удовольствие. 

Игровая петля максимально прозрачна: выкопал — собрал ресурсы — поднялся наверх — продал ресурсы — купил улучшения — снова зарылся в землю. Возвращение на поверхность — короткий вздох перед очередным погружением. И чем глубже уходишь, тем более неохотно возвращаешься, когда в очередной раз заканчивается энергия или место в инвентаре. Но если энергия вдруг все же закончится, то все ресурсы пропадут, поэтому возвращаться приходится. 

Не обойтись и без шероховатостей, конечно, особенно если увлечься получением всех достижений. Например, охота за спидранерским достижением — та еще задача. Учитывая тот факт, что в этой игре можно, например, упасть с высоты птичьего полета и чудом не разбиться, а можно прыгнуть с высоты одного метра и каким-то образом потерять половину шкалы здоровья. А еще тот факт, что сообщение о том, что энергия на исходе появляется посреди экрана в момент, когда энергии остается еще половина шкалы, и иногда ты так сильно привыкаешь к этой мозолящей глаза строке, что не замечаешь, как энергия действительно заканчивается. А еще тот факт, что разбиваемые одной лишь только взрывчаткой каменные и лавовые глыбы генерируются в яме случайным образом при каждом запуске новой игры, так что тебе может просто неудачно повезти, и все неломаемые камни будут именно на выбранном пути вниз, причем когда ты еще не можешь позволить себе взрывчатку. И тогда спидран придется начинать заново. Хорошо, что все эти проблемы касаются только тех, кто добровольно занимается мазохизмом в целях получения всех достижений. В случае же стандартного игрового опыта эти проблемы практически не заметны и ни на что не влияют. 

Интересно, что первое прохождение игры сделано как бы для удовольствия, чтобы расслабиться и не выбивать никаких достижений. На самом деле в начале это даже сбило меня с толку и я подумала, что над достижениями придется танцевать с бубном, чтобы все заработало. Но в действительности все достигнутые в первой игре достижения выдаются ретроспективно по началу новой игры, а прогресс по еще не достигнутым можно отследить прямо в гараже на полке с наградами. 

Ну и все же приятно, что в игре есть незамысловатый сюжет, который пусть и мелькает где-то на периферии, но все же оправдывает процесс и в конце концов приводит игрока к очень даже интересному [spoiler]плот-твисту[/spoiler]. Без сюжета оправдывать почти десяток часов, проведенных даже не в майнкрафте, было бы как-то совсем грустно. 

В общем, A Game About Digging A Hole™ просто подвернулась мне под руку в самое подходящее время. И если вы тоже болеете, или просто не знаете, чем себя занять под какой-нибудь неторопливый стрим, то вы попали по адресу — получение удовольствия от простого и почти медитативного труда почти гарантировано.

[b]🕳️ A Game About Digging a Hole – mała gra, duża satysfakcja 🕳️[/b]

[i]Na pierwszy rzut oka wygląda jak prosty, żartobliwy projekt, ale A Game About Digging a Hole potrafi wciągnąć bardziej, niż można się spodziewać. To minimalistyczna, spokojna gra, która opiera się na jednym pomyśle… i wykorzystuje go naprawdę dobrze.[/i]

[b]⛏️ Gameplay – prostota, która uzależnia ⛏️[/b]
[i]Kopiesz. Coraz głębiej. Bez zbędnych tutoriali i bez presji czasu. Mechanika jest bardzo prosta, ale satysfakcja z odkrywania kolejnych warstw ziemi i ulepszania możliwości sprawia, że „jeszcze jeden metr” szybko zamienia się w dłuższą sesję.[/i]

[b]⌛ Długość rozgrywki ⌛[/b]
[i]Ukończenie gry zajmuje około 3 godziny, co idealnie pasuje do jej formy. To tytuł w sam raz na jeden wieczór, bez zbędnego przeciągania zabawy.[/i]

[b]🧠 Zaskakujące zakończenie 🧠[/b]
[i]Choć przez większość czasu gra wydaje się czysto mechaniczna, jej finał potrafi naprawdę zaskoczyć i sprawia, że cała podróż w dół nabiera nowego znaczenia.[/i]

[b]💬 Podsumowanie 💬[/b]
[i]A Game About Digging a Hole to niewielka, pomysłowa produkcja, która oferuje około 3 godziny przyjemnej, relaksującej rozgrywki i serwuje zaskakujący finał.[/i]

[h3]There's something primally satisfying about digging a really freakin' big hole, and this game satisfies that with flying colors . Despite a few minor shortcomings, it's definitely a pretty great price for some hours of indie digging fun.[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
[h1]I Can Dig It[/h1]
I had seen various people on YouTube play this game, and every time I always thought about how I'd approach digging the hole™️. I could picture myself digging this elegant spiral staircase down to the core of the earth, or whatever lies at the bottom of this random, shockingly easy to excavate patch of land in the back of my house. It was what originally compelled me to pick the game up. And, true to it's name, there's not a whole lot else going on with this one.

The progression systems in place are pretty solid. Starting with a pitiful trowel and working your way up to the dirt vaccuum 9000-inator is a great incrementation on the formula that felt good to move through even upon replaying the game. The other upgrades the game has, inventory, battery, and jetpack, are also substantial enough to feel useful, though they lack the immediacy and punch of digging a bigger perfect sphere of dirt out like the shovel upgrade path has. I found myself excited to get a new shovel upgrade, and really I considered the other upgrades as just the means to get to the next shovel upgrade more than anything. I don't necessarily think that there's anything wrong with this, but maybe some more visual and auditory aspects to the other upgrades could've made them a bit more impactful.


[h1]The Elephant* in the Room[/h1]
So, lite spoilers for the end-game, which I do think are kind of cute in their own way, this game does actually tell a simple story. It's got this game jam-level premise that I kind of love and hate with these sorts of indie games. You know, the kinds of stories that are so unambiguous and straightforward, the kind that are describable with just one sentence to the point they're almost painfully trite. I think I can give this game a pass, as it's clearly just about digging the hole, so we'll chalk it up as a "bowser kidnaps peach" kind of story wrapper; The story isn't anything to write home about, but having absolutely NO story would've been worse.

What happens in this one that you eventually [spoiler]fall into a cave, all your tools and abilities get disabled, and the game suddenly transitions into a stealth game where you're dodging *giant killer moles with glowing red eyes. The tone shift reminds me of another indie game: Budget Cuts. In its twelfth hour, it's suddenly very dark, the ambience is different, and it becomes a diet horror game out of nowhere. This one isn't nearly as egregious, as it's pretty obvious this was meant to be a funny conclusion to the game, and I think it mostly sticks the landing. [/spoiler]I do think that there was a lot of possibilities that were left on the table, though, even with keeping the same premise, and I think that the lack of a genuinely entertaining story is going to hold this one back from being an indie classic.

On the other hand, added content may have ballooned this game into something it was never trying to be. It's short runtime, about 6-8 hours for 100% completion, is just the absolute perfect length for it's experience. I don't know if adding 4 hours to that for dialogue, secrets, lore, or what have you, would've made the game better. The game definitely played it safe, and I think that was the smart choice. Doesn't mean I can't yearn for a more elaborate hole.


[h1]Quality of Life-ish[/h1]
Indie games inherently come with some jank, and one with it's free-form digging innevitably wasn't going to be the exception, but I feel like just 5% more time and budget to the user experience might've made it truly painless. The biggest one for me is that you can't just quit to the main menu. Normally not an issue, but especially irksome as 100%-ing the game requires a lot of restarts if you attempt to get the speedrunner achievement.

Speaking of the speedrunner achievement, I feel as though any game that has that kind of achievement should go through the effort of giving you an option for an on-screen display of your time, if nothing else to let you know which menus pause the timer, if any, and to help you know where your current time is at if you decide to save and quit. Going for the speedrunner achievement was also where a lot of the minor things started to add up. Fall damage being finicky, collision being irritating at times, energy management becoming more of a challenge than I'd have liked.

Energy, while we're at it, is one of the things that barely scraped by without me becoming furious at this game. The joke is that everything you have is battery powered, and the batteries explode when they run out, leading to the loss of all the ores you've gathered. Casually, I'm fine with this, but once again going for the speedrunner achievement leads to a handful of ocassions where, because you're digging far further down than you would otherwise, the low battery warning isn't sufficient to get you out of the hole with your jetpack (which is a normal thing to dig a hole with). Coupled with getting caught on random dirt geometry as you try to get out quickly, and you're set up to lose a run. Having the jetpack lose less battery if you're not ascending, or even better, having it destroy a dirt horizontally when you're stuck would've probably been a good way to fix this without breaking the game's balance.

The last nitpicks I have aren't as bad. One is just having to hold the trigger for practically the entirety of the game's runtime. I don't know if a toggle solution would've been better, or if keyboard/mouse was the way I should've played, but my hand was pretty tired after multiple hours of digging. I could've used steams controller mapping to try that myself, so clearly it didn't bother me that much, but for accessibility purposes it might be good to have the option. Trying to dig a rock that you're supposed to break with explosives still drains energy, which is frustrating because it feels like the auto-click speed ramps up when you hit one. Picking up an ore when your inventory is full just destroys it, regardless of it's value. I think it should swap out the lowest value ore you have if it's higher and destroy that one or let me discard ones I don't want from the inventory menu.

You probably caught onto the trend that so many of these issues stem from the post-game achievement hunt, which I'm a sucker for in these smaller indie titles. Like I said earlier, it's the perfect length, but all the cracks really showed in the post-game. Those last 4ish hours made the whole experience feel just the tiniest bit lesser because of the lack of polish for that half of the game. I think that the casual experience was prioritized, as the pre-post-game was clearly given that attention instead, which ultimately was the right choice I feel. 

[h1]Conclusion: It's not that deep (unlike the hole)[/h1]
If the premise sounds fun to you, this game executes upon it fairly well. It doesn't execute upon it flawlessly, and it really doesn't have much else going on which makes it a harder recommendation for those less inclined to want to just dig a big hole. However, I'm happy to report that I had fun digging a hole in this game about digging a hole.

Enjoyable no brain game

I honestly regret buying this game. I’ve only played it once or twice, and that was more than enough for me to realize how boring it is. The entire point of the game is exactly what the title says: you dig a hole. That’s it. You dig, your battery runs out, you go back up, recharge or sell stuff, and then you repeat the exact same cycle over and over again. There’s no real progression, no (big) story, no interesting mechanics, no variety. Just digging. It gets extremely repetitive very fast. After like 10 minutes, you’ve basically seen everything the game has to offer. The gameplay loop never changes. There are no twists, no challenges, no surprises. You’re just digging deeper for the sake of digging deeper. And yeah, I get it. The title literally warns you. It *is* a game about digging a hole. So part of this is on me. But with how much hype this game had, I was expecting at least *something* more. Some kind of goal, upgrades that actually feel meaningful, or at least different environments. But no. It’s just the same thing the whole time. I also tried making content on it. I tried recording it, tried turning it into a series, and it was impossible because it’s just not interesting to watch or play. It’s one of those games that works better as a YouTube concept than an actual game you should spend money on. Watching someone else play it is more entertaining than playing it yourself. There’s nothing wrong with the game technically. It runs fine, it looks fine, it does exactly what it says. It’s just… boring. There’s no depth, no replay value, and no reason to come back once you’ve tried it. I only bought it because of the hype, and I definitely fell for it. Unless you genuinely love the idea of digging a virtual hole for hours with no real payoff, I wouldn’t recommend this game at all.

Hole-digging simulator game.  You are someone digging a hole.  You bought a house that purportedly has a treasure chest buried in the back yard.  Dig.  Find the treasure.  Try not to fall down and break something.  Or burn.  Or get eaten.

Seriously, the game is about digging a hole.  You have the back yard, you have a garage with sale and upgrade stations, you have a shovel, and that's about it.  Stuff you find while digging your hole (the first thing you find is "stone") can be sold at the sales station.  Proceeds from sales can be spent at the upgrade station for better shovels, bigger backpacks, longer-lasting batteries (because your shovel is apparently battery-powered), stick-on lights and dynamite.

And that's it.  As you dig deeper you find things more valuable than stone.  As you upgrade your shovel you dig down faster.  As you upgrade your battery and backpack you spend less time running back to the garage.  And these improvements are felt rather strongly, since at the beginning you're only making small holes and running back to the garage almost constantly.

The game actually has an ending, which I reached in about six hours.  Found the chest, got the cinematic finale, unlocked achievements.  If you can get past the beginning, where you're pretty much just tearing up the yard with a hand trowel, you can maybe appreciate the graphics, the ambience and the zen-like quality of the process of getting deeper.  In other words, A Game about Digging a Hole...has depth.

Not bad for the current price of US$5.00.  I received it as a gift off my wishlist when it went on sale for $2.  I consider it not a bad hole to throw some money down.

Not worth it, even at $5. Simple games can be a lot of fun, but this one manages to be TOO simple. The concept is fine and the gameplay is mostly fine, but there's just no depth to the game at all- no pun intended. 

There is no balance to your gear upgrades; there are 5 levels for your shovel, the first 4 barely make a difference and then you suddenly have the drill, which is great and feels like it should have been the 2nd upgrade.

Your starting inventory is 3 slots. THREE. So as soon as you pick up three bits of ore, back to the garage to sell them.

The ending sequence of the game takes a bizarre left turn which I would normally enjoy, but it's so completely unrelated to the rest of the game that it's just confusing as to why it was added.

A Game About Digging A Hole is exactly what it sounds like - armed with an upgradable shovel, you dig down into your yard to get ores to sell for upgrades, in the search for a treasure chest. It takes less than 90 minutes to finish, and you can replay the game to get achievements (which you can't get in your first playthrough, for some reason, but if you made any progress towards them, it's carried over, aside from the Speedrun achievement)

I wouldn't say this game is terrible, but I also don't feel like I got anything out of it. You dig, you upgrade and the game is over before you know it. I get the game's scope is limited on purpose but there's barely anything going on before you are done and the upgrades are boring enough that you don't really get any enjoyment from delving deeper. It's like a more involved, but less fun idle game where the game ends before you even prestige once.

There's no physics except for dynamite which often rolls off a rock before exploding, no real secrets and I just felt bored. If you get this on a sale for a dollar or two, it might be worth looking at for an hour, but there's also many better uses of your time in my opinion. And sure, it's the price of a coffee, but so are many other amazing games that have more than an hour of playtime - and I disagree that this game is fun for longer, given that caffeine remains in my system for 3-4 hours and even for achievement hunters you'll be done before that.

[h2]《掘地求财》[/h2]
一款以[b]挖掘[/b]为主要内容的游戏
主要玩法:挖掘矿石→回家卖钱→升级装备→继续深入→通关
整体游戏类似于[u]挖地小子3D版[/u](从特殊矿石的设定上可以看出应该有所借鉴)
一周目游玩时间大概在1.5~3h，[strike]如果是想要玩完退款的不要在黄金层逗留太长时间(bushi)[/strike]
游戏剧情:“我”买下了一个低价抛售的房子，房子里埋着原主人留下的宝藏[spoiler]最后发现宝藏是一个骗局，事实是一群做地下鼹鼠实验的人在给鼹鼠寻找食物(?)，作者想要表达的大概是贪小便宜吃大亏、贪多无益的道理。[/spoiler]
但是在我主观看来，该游戏剧情没有前因后果的铺垫，没有文字描述，让人一头雾水的游玩过程，[spoiler]以及唯一的坏结局[/spoiler]，让我对这个游戏剧情的感觉就像是赶工期硬套上去的一样，毫无逻辑感可言
如果只是作为一款无聊时的休闲游戏，那掘地求升是很成功的
但是对于成就党来说，这游戏又很折磨:
一周目不会解锁成就系统，而这游戏的唯一存档就导致了必须开启二周目从头再来才可以解锁成就
(不过一周目完成的成就在二周目会有记录，[strike]但是我都已经重开了不还是得再来一遍吗！！[/strike]）
游戏还有无实时存档、唯一存档、矿石穿模、灯光亮度可以无限叠加(bushi)、炸药穿模(穿模后依然可以爆炸，不会被吞)、喷气背包延迟、鼹鼠无法攻击的问题，除了唯一存档导致二周目通关后没有开启三周目的想法外，其他都是小问题
价格方面：原价18.5r，史低13.69r(平台可以再便宜一些)，确实如作者所说，一杯奶茶钱的游戏体量那还是有的
但是每个人的金钱观不同，在这里我也不过多评价，我个人觉得这个价格还算可以
[u]下面是关于通关与成就(全成就送黄金钻头)的攻略，建议游玩过后再来阅读:[/u]
在挖掘到底部后，我们的灯泡、炸药、喷气背包会全部失灵，这时候只需要在鼹鼠背对着我们的时候溜过去，后面就是被发现它也追不上了，底部一共三只鼹鼠两个洞穴，第二个洞穴里有两只鼹鼠，处理方法相同
成就1:空中飞人(较难)
在空中停滞4秒，期间不允许使用喷气背包
需要至少挖空中心(到底部)留下一条角色能够穿过的通道(我就吃了没挖中心挖周围的亏)
先用喷气背包飞到空气墙高度落下(注意:在我挖空所有泥土后测试:该游戏最多停滞时间只有4.1秒，所以一定要飞到顶格并且从中心挖到底部再跳)
成就2:纯纯浪费(简单)
背包满了以后再挖50个矿石就行
成就3:辛勤挥铲(简单)
挖掘4000次(一周目通关基本上就有了)
成就4:炸弹人(简单)
扔出100次炸药(炸药丢着玩就有了)
成就5:石头收藏家(简单)
收集一百块石头(一周目通关基本就有了)
成就6:我赶时间(难)
[u]30分钟内通关游戏，先做这个再做其他的！！[/u]不能在黄金层逗留太长时间，没升完的装备钻石层再升，优先升钻头等级和能量上限(这个二周目没达成的话就太难受了，三周目玩得要ex了)
成就7:特殊矿石(简单)
收集五个特殊矿石，只有二周目才会出现特殊矿石(彩色光芒)，不止五个(被炸弹炸没了也不用担心)
成就8:大富翁(简单)
获得20000金币(一周目通关基本就有了)

A Game About Digging a Hole is as appropriate a name as I can think of. You're in a garden and you just dig as deep as you can go. It starts off slow, but as you harvest ores to sell for money, you gain access to upgrades which help you dig faster, give you more energy, allow you to carry more ores at a time, and a jetpack to allow you to get in and out of the hole safely. It's surprisingly addicting. There's even a surprise waiting at the bottom, which I definitely was not expecting.

It's a one and done deal. You do unlock achievements after you complete the game once, but it feels like this was deliberately done to get you to play the game twice - potentially more, considering what one of the achievements is (shout out to the secret feature, which allows you to expedite the process tremendously). They honestly could have been available from the start. And the reward you get for completing all the achievements doesn't warrant playing yet another time, unless you really like the gameplay. But, like Ben says, it costs merely a coffee. I won't be installing it ever again, but I had fun and would potentially like to see more from rokaplay select and Drillhounds in the future.

I was looking through the store  during the 2025 Steam Winter sale for things to add to my wish list and spotted this in a lttle box so I clicked to check it our.  I love all kinds of game and casual time waster games are right up there. A game you don't need to stress to play, you just play and enjoy. I was looking to get Leaf it Alone, I already had it in my cart. Quick Description:
-A Game About Digging a Hole is a short and sweet  first person digging game.  I love mining games and really enjoy exploring an area as I search for treasure and secrets.  This game starts off quite strong but hits a wall really quickly.  This game actually plays more like an incremental game as opposed to a simulation game.  The major problem, is that there aren't enough upgrades and the gameplay loop grows shallow and repetitive  in less than 2 hrs.  You will max out all of your upgrades in 90-120 minutes tops.  The ending feels extremely unrewarding and made me feel like I wasted close to an hour as I was trying to search every nook and cranny, assuming that I must have missed a major secret.  

Consensus:
-Bottom Shelf Game (Tier 5 and makes up 10% of my reviews).  Admittedly, I feel bad not recommending a game that I spend $3 on, but I just don't see myself ever playing this again and I don't think I'd recommend this to pretty much anyone.  There are so many strong mining and incremental games on the market that I would happily recommend over this game.  I do think that the dev could expand upon this idea and create a far more interesting and engaging experience as a sequel or future project.

[h1]DZIURA W ZIEMI LEPSZA NIŻ KREDYT.[/h1]

Tytuł nie kłamie, dostajemy dokładnie to co na pudełku. A Game About Digging A Hole.
Fabuła to celna satyra na rynek nieruchomości - kupujesz dom, bo w ogródku ma być skarb. Bierzesz łopatę i do roboty. Może to naiwne podejście, ale wciąga jak bagno od pierwszego wbicia szpadla.

[b]PRAWIE MINECRAFT (Rozgrywka)[/b]
Mechanika jest prosta jak konstrukcja cepa, ale działa.
[list]
[*] [b]Pętla:[/b] Zaczynasz z marnym sprzętem, idzie jak krew z nosa. Wykopujesz śmieci, sprzedajesz, ulepszasz. Nagle kopiesz szybciej i głębiej. Klasyczny schemat "od zera do bohatera", tylko że twój bohater siedzi w dziurze.
[*] [b]Relaks:[/b] Fizyka ziemi i usuwanie kolejnych bloków jest dziwnie satysfakcjonujące. Idealny tytuł na odstresowanie po ciężkim dniu - machasz łopatą i nie myślisz o niczym.
[*] [b]Gadżety:[/b] Z czasem dochodzi dynamit i plecak odrzutowy. Latanie w dziurze brzmi absurdalnie, ale sprawdza się świetnie.
[/list]

[b]NA DECKU[/b]
Całość zajmuje około 2-3 godziny, chyba że czyścisz mapę do zera. Na Steam Decku działa idealnie, to gra stworzona do krótkich sesji na kanapie.

[h1]WERDYKT[/h1]
Głupie to, ale genialne w swojej prostocie. Warto poświęcić te parę godzin, żeby zobaczyć co kryje się na dnie. Idealny przerywnik między dużymi grami, nie męczy i nie wymaga doktoryzowania się z mechanik.

[b]Szybki skrót:[/b]
➕ Wciąga (syndrom jeszcze jednego metra)
➕ Proste i relaksujące
➕ Świetnie działa na Decku
➖ Krótkie (ale za tę cenę warto)

[b]Ocena: 5/6[/b]

[h2]Short and barebones[/h2]

I don't understand the hype about this game. It is a very barebones incremental game. Dig, get resources, buy upgrades, dig deeper, get better resources that sell for more, get more powerful upgrades till you finish the game... You get the "drill". There are only 4 things you can upgrade (none of them is interesting or game changing) and the dynamite is essentially useless. There is a weird, out of place sequence at the end, where you can't use your 'hard'-earned upgrades, disregarding your progress. The game is 1-1.5hrs long to beat, and the NG achievement mode only contains bland, grindy stuff like sell 'x' worth of resources and blow up 'y' amount of dynamites. 

For 0.5-1€, this would be an OK meme game. For 5€, this is a ripoff. Refunded.

[h1]如果你是冲着探索、收集来的，那我劝你一句：现在就退。继续在steam商店挑游戏吧 [/h1]

这游戏的[b]“挖掘”[/b]内容看似是最大卖点，但实际体验上说白了就是不停挖出一些毫无意义的破石头，既没故事，也没惊喜，更谈不上成就感。

问题是，游戏的点子其实很棒，在探索的这一个分类上，完全可以选择做的更好，比如可以加剧情、加历史背景，或者干脆做成纯挖宝：化石、古董、遗物、破烂都行，只要能让人想继续挖。但作者偏不。

在我看来，作者选择了自己的恶趣味

看主页说明，我明明在玩一个探索收集向游戏，[spoiler]但玩着玩着突然就变成了一个莫名其妙的恐怖追逐游戏。怪追你，你只能跑，不能反击、不能肘击，连挣扎的权利都不给。探索？不存在的。[/spoiler]

最离谱的是——最让人期待的宝藏 [spoiler]是空的[/spoiler]。
[spoiler]前面铺垫半天，挖到最后告诉你：什么都没有。 [/spoiler]
这体验大概就相当于你泡了个 180 腹肌男模，氛围都到位了，结果关键时刻发现对方阳痿——前面所有期待瞬间归零。

说到底，这设计像是故意为了主播做节目效果：吓人、追逐、尖叫，视频好看就行，至于玩家玩得爽不爽、探索有没有意义？不重要。还是说不小心为了主播做节目效果得到商业上的成功而抛弃了游戏性？

如果你想要的是探索感和收集乐趣，那这游戏对你来说，真的就是在浪费时间。

Bon petit jeu chill, à lancer en regardant une vidéo ou un stream à côté. Le concept est ultra simple, mais il fonctionne bien et fait exactement ce qu'on lui demande. Techniquement et visuellement, c'est correct, rien d'exceptionnel mais rien de gênant non plus. La musique et l'ambiance sonore sont agréables, ça participe bien au côté relax.

Le jeu est assez court, et honnêtement c'est plutôt une bonne chose. Plus long, ça aurait probablement fini par être répétitif et un peu lassant.

Seul vrai bémol selon moi : la gestion des succès. Beaucoup ne se débloquent qu'en New Game+, ce qui oblige à terminer une première run sans réel objectif si on vise le 100 %. C'est un peu frustrant.

Dans l'ensemble, une expérience sympa, sans prise de tête, à faire tranquillement.

Хотя никакого обучения игра не предлагает, но управление настолько простое с геймпадом, что разобраться дело нескольких минут.
Нужно экономить энергию, особенно когда находишься весьма глубоко под землёй, т.к. там может её не хватить, чтобы реактивный ранец вытащил нас на поверхность, энергия стоить денег, а деньги получаем за счёт продажи ресурсов, которые сами и находим в процессе копки.

There isn't too much of a story other than a guy sees someone put up a flyer on a bulletin board stating that they can find a chest with $10,000 somewhere in the backyard of a house in an attempt to make a sale, this guy then decides "f**k it" and just ends up trespassing and destroys property.... what a chad.

You will dig in this yard, but you have a battery on this "automatic" shovel so you have to watch out for the battery while also attempting to gather ores in order to make some side cash so that you can then upgrade your arsenal; a shovel which can turn into a drill, upgrading the amount of space for ores, you get a jetpack oooooh, and obviously you can upgrade the battery. You can also buy lanterns and dynamite to help you along the way. Simple, very simple, but is something that is pretty relaxing especially when you can just have a couple beers while sitting back.

Easy achievements are also a pretty big plus if that's something you're into. 1 or 2 might be tedious, but nothing too bad imo. Might take closer to 2-3 hours just because you will have to play through at least once legitimately instead of just doing the money tile method and digging straight down.

I mean overall I would recommend it, not a lot is going on with the game, but like I said before it's pretty chill and has easy achievements so that's cool with me. Дом с Секретом
Мы с Максом всегда мечтали о своем доме. Не о квартире в многоэтажке, а о настоящем, с садом, где можно было бы выращивать помидоры, и с верандой, где пить утренний кофе. Мечтали, но реальность была далека от наших желаний. Цены на недвижимость в нашем городе кусались, и казалось, что наша мечта так и останется мечтой.

И вот, однажды, совершенно случайно, мы наткнулись на объявление. Дом. Очень низкая цена. Слишком низкая, чтобы быть правдой. Мы перечитали его несколько раз, подозревая подвох. Но любопытство взяло верх.

Дом оказался старым, немного запущенным, но с потенциалом. Он стоял на окраине города, окруженный густым лесом. А на заднем дворе… на заднем дворе был вклад. Огромный, заросший кустарником и сорняками, он выглядел как забытое богом место. Хозяин, пожилой мужчина с потухшим взглядом, лишь пожал плечами, когда мы спросили про вклад. "Давно никто не трогал. Говорят, там что-то было, но я не знаю. Копать придется долго."

Мы купили дом. Низкая цена, несмотря на вклад, была слишком заманчивой. Мы были полны энтузиазма. Макс мечтал превратить вклад в бассейн, а я – в уютный пруд с кувшинками.

Первые дни прошли в уборке и планировании. Мы выкорчевали кусты, вывезли мусор, и начали прикидывать, как будем копать. Вклад был настолько заросшим, что казалось, будто он поглотил часть земли.

"Ну что, приступим?" – сказал Макс, держа в руках лопату.

Мы начали копать. И копать. И копать. Земля была плотной, с вкраплениями камней. Солнце пекло, пот заливал глаза, но мы не сдавались. Каждый день мы проводили несколько часов, углубляясь в землю.

Прошла неделя. Мы выкопали уже несколько метров, но конца и края не было видно. Вклад казался бесконечным. Усталость начала брать свое, но мы продолжали, подстегиваемые любопытством и надеждой на будущий бассейн.

Однажды, когда мы уже почти потеряли надежду, лопата Макса ударилась обо что-то твердое. Не камень. Что-то другое. Мы начали осторожно откапывать. Это была деревянная крышка. Старая, сгнившая, но явно рукотворная.

Сердца наши забились быстрее. Что там может быть? Старинные сокровища? Забытые реликвии?

Мы с трудом подняли крышку. Под ней оказалась темная, сырая яма. Запах, который оттуда исходил, был странным – смесь земли, плесени и чего-то еще… чего-то неприятного.

Макс посветил фонариком вниз. Яма была глубокой. И там… там что-то было. Нечто темное, бесформенное, лежащее на дне.

"Что это?" – прошептал Макс, его голос дрожал.

Я тоже смотрела вниз, пытаясь разглядеть. И тут я увидела. Глаза. Два тусклых, пустых глаза, смотрящие прямо на нас из темноты.

Мой желудок сжался. Это не было похоже ни на что, что я когда-либо видела. Это было… чудовищно.

Макс отшатнулся. "Нет… это не может быть…"

Я не могла отвести взгляд. Глаза казались живыми, несмотря на их мертвенный блеск. И я почувствовала, как


меня охватывает ледяной ужас. Это не просто яма, это не просто находка. Это что-то, что не должно было быть найдено.

Из темноты послышался тихий, скребущий звук. Словно что-то медленно двигалось. Макс схватил меня за руку, его пальцы были холодными.

"Надо уходить," – прохрипел он.

Но я не могла. Мои ноги словно приросли к земле. Я видела, как бесформенное нечто на дне ямы начало медленно подниматься. Оно было покрыто чем-то темным и липким, и от него исходил тот самый отвратительный запах, который теперь казался невыносимым.

Внезапно, из ямы раздался низкий, утробный стон. Он был полон боли и злобы. И в этот момент я поняла. Это не сокровища. Это не реликвия. Это что-то, что было похоронено здесь очень давно, и оно не хотело быть найденным.

Макс дернул меня за руку. "Бежим!"

Мы бросились прочь от ямы, спотыкаясь о корни и камни. Я не оглядывалась, но чувствовала на себе чей-то взгляд. Тяжелый, холодный взгляд, который проникал сквозь меня.

Мы добежали до дома, захлопнули дверь и заперли ее на все замки. Сердца наши колотились как сумасшедшие. Мы стояли в гостиной, тяжело дыша, и смотрели друг на друга с ужасом в глазах.

"Что это было?" – прошептала я, мой голос дрожал.

Макс покачал головой. "Я не знаю. Но я знаю одно – мы больше никогда не подойдем к этому вкладу."

Ночь прошла в тревоге. Каждый шорох за окном заставлял нас вздрагивать. Мы не спали, прислушиваясь к звукам из темноты. Казалось, что лес вокруг дома ожил, и что-то невидимое наблюдает за нами.

Утром, когда первые лучи солнца пробились сквозь окна, мы почувствовали небольшое облегчение. Но страх остался. Мы знали, что наш дом хранит тайну, и эта тайна оказалась куда более кошмарной, чем мы могли себе представить.

Мы больше не говорили о бассейне или пруде. Мы просто хотели забыть о том, что нашли. Но я знала, что это невозможно. Тот взгляд из темноты, тот стон… они навсегда останутся в моей памяти. И каждый раз, когда я буду смотреть на задний двор, я буду вспоминать о том, что скрывается под землей, и о том, что мы случайно разбудили. Наш дом, купленный по такой низкой цене, оказался домом с кошмаром, погребенным глубоко под землей. И этот кошмар теперь был частью нашей жизни.


Мы провели следующие дни в состоянии постоянного напряжения. Каждый скрип половицы, каждый шорох ветра казался предвестником чего-то ужасного. Мы старались не выходить на задний двор, обходя его стороной, как будто само место было заразным. Макс пытался найти рациональное объяснение, говорил про старые погреба, про животных, но я видела, что и он напуган. Его глаза тоже стали тусклыми, как будто он увидел что-то, что навсегда отняло у него прежний блеск.

Однажды вечером, когда мы сидели в гостиной, прислушиваясь к тишине, которая казалась неестественно громкой, мы услышали звук. Тихий, но отчетливый. Скрежет. Он доносился откуда-то с заднего двора. Мы замерли, боясь дышать. Звук повторился, стал громче, настойчивее. Казалось, что кто-то или что-то пытается пробраться сквозь землю.

Макс схватил старую бейсбольную биту, которая валялась в углу. Я взяла в руки тяжелую чугунную сковородку. Мы медленно подошли к окну, за которым простиралась черная бездна ночи. Лунный свет едва пробивался сквозь густые кроны деревьев, создавая причудливые тени.

И тут мы увидели. У края ямы, там, где мы оставили ее открытой, что-то двигалось. Это было нечто темное, бесформенное, похожее на огромную, пульсирующую тень. Оно медленно, словно в агонии, извивалось, и от него исходил тот самый тошнотворный запах, который мы так старались забыть.

Мы отшатнулись от окна, прижавшись друг к другу. Страх сковал нас. Мы были заперты в нашем доме, а кошмар находился всего в нескольких метрах от нас, на нашем собственном заднем дворе.

"Мы должны что-то сделать," – прошептал Макс, его голос был хриплым. "Мы не можем просто сидеть здесь и ждать."

Но что мы могли сделать? Как можно бороться с тем, что не имеет формы, что исходит из самой земли?

Следующие дни превратились в кошмар наяву. Мы жили в постоянном страхе, прислушиваясь к каждому звуку. Скрежет и стоны стали нашими ночными спутниками. Иногда мы видели тени, движущиеся у края ямы, или чувствовали, как земля под домом слегка дрожит.

Мы пытались найти информацию о доме, о предыдущих владельцах. Но старые записи были скудны, а соседи, которых мы осмелились расспросить, лишь отводили глаза и бормотали что-то про "нехорошее место". Казалось, что все знали о том, что скрывается под землей, но никто не хотел говорить.

Однажды, когда мы сидели за ужином, пытаясь сделать вид, что все в порядке, мы услышали громкий треск. Он донесся с заднего двора. Мы бросились к окну. То, что мы увидели, заставило нас застыть в ужасе.

Часть земли вокруг ямы провалилась. И из образовавшейся трещины показалось нечто. Оно было похоже на корень, но черное, покрытое слизью, и оно медленно, но верно, тянулось к дому.

"Оно идет к нам," – прошептала я, чувствуя, как по спине пробегает холодок.

Макс сжал биту сильнее. "Мы должны его остановить."

Но как? Как остановить то, что растет из земли, что питается тьмой?

Мы провели бессонную ночь, наблюдая, как черная, слизистая масса медленно ползет по траве, приближаясь к фундаменту дома...

[h1]Introduction:[/h1]
This review is for [i]"A Game About Digging A Hole"...[/i] a game that really needs no introductions, but I really can't help but be... astonished with. It's one of [b]"those"[/b] games I absolutely CANNOT understand why the sudden boost in popularity and traction. It's a very short game of aimlessly digging towards treasure, and got more than a few copycats eating away dirt crumbs, languishing and profiting on the idea because of its success. Arse-grabbing and finger-licking copying business I'd tell you.

The original game's created by a guy named Ben, and made the game in his free time. Funnily enough, I bought it out of curiosity NOT of the gameplay, but more on questioning why the unexpected official novel that came out not too long ago... [i][b]WHAT IS THERE TO WRITE ABOUT!?[/b] I though to myself out loud in caps.[/i] And that's the moment where I tried this game out for the first time.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]1 / 5
Dig, grab stone/ore, full inventory, sell stuff, upgrade gear, repeat. That's all to it. For me personally, I did not feel any of the satisfaction-levels like many other people glace and praise over, it's all just brainless activities. So if you want to zone out and don't have any prescription on chill-pills to your name, this game could make the difference... and covers the expenses at the pharmacy.

[h1]Caverns:[/h1]1 / 5
Build-in caverns are procedurally generated and serve as extra filler in this already boring time waster. I'll admit, it's a nice touch, but it's really not that special or something to keep you on your toes on what's next... because you damn well know what's next, you'll need to keep digging.

[h1]Depth:[/h1]3 / 5
A positive rating, but not the way you might think. It's -100 m. And honestly, thank God it's not any deeper, couldn't deal any more depth of this game. If it was any deeper, I couldn't bare it any longer and might've just quit of boredom, because I got the overall gist of this game. So... thanks, I suppose.

[h1]Sellables:[/h1]0 / 5
Stones, coal, iron, copper... (Hell, why not) silver, gold, platinum, diamond. It really doesn't matter though, you'll need to sell it anyways. The stones and minerals you collect during the dig are at the end of the day colorful cumbersome roadblocks you need to get rid of.

[h1]Collectables:[/h1]0 / 5
On occasion, you can find briefcases, keys and buried mineshafts. Once you're nearby one, a gadget will appear. 2 variant models, when near mineshafts a remote-looking gadget, when near briefcases and keys a dish-looking gadget. BUT WHEN BOTH are nearby one and 'nother BOTH gadgets overlap your screen. A bug still present, and not fixed somehow... busy writing something Ben?

Anyways, 2 keys can be found, then you can open a chest in the garage, and gives you 2 things. An increase blast radius for dynamites and an ONETIME use teleport. Briefcases and mineshafts have the same premise. Briefcases have mediocre rewards, and mineshafts have an entryway towards a small chest of... you guessed it, mediocre rewards. Audible sighs all around.

I'm not overly surprised of the dull, lack-of proper rewards, because what else is there to be rewarded for? There is really nothing else in this game other than the occasional boulder obstructing your digging session.

[h1]The Official Story Novel:[/h1]-2 / 5
If I squint my eyes enough, I can barely see the shameless penny-squeezing DLC. [i]"Costs as much as a ☕ coffee"[/i] Imagine buying another coffee, but instead of drinking another round of coffee, you'll get for the same price a receipt of where the coffee beans come from.

If you want to spend another 4,99€, you can read an extensive lore behind the hole, previous owners, and who knows what else! It's a 60-page novel of your favorite forgettable French fried slob for you to read, fangirl, giggle and curl your tinee-tiny toes over. Don't get me wrong, I like reading books and novels. But this is outrageous! It's a hole for crying out loud, it's not that deep! [strike]Pun WAS intended, but that pun was full of bullet holes from an angry mob in a dispute.[/strike]

And before you say that this is a way of supporting the developer... steady your horse cowboy, sit tight and just think about it for a hot second! He could've done that with, IDFK... skins maybe? A deeper hole? Another game title or gamemode!? But instead a whole-ass 60-page novel!? Come on! Doesn't this just rub you the wrong way? Like an itch at the base of your neck? That's cancer I think, consult a doctor.

[h3]Overall:[/h3]
[i]"A Game About Digging A Hole And Me Writing About It Because I Do Have The Time And Money For It Now"[/i] That's better. Asking the community to nominate him for the "Sit Back and Relax" title, and be graced a novel that comes out days later... about digging a hole, nonetheless. Other than greed, I really can't fathom the thought process here.

The game's slob at its finest, meh at best. The premise becomes damn clear as the Mediterranean Sea the first few clicks on the grass patch. Those who stay long enough are avid adventurers from other titles, like Minecraft for example. Those who gave up straightaway didn't read the game's title. And me? I'm a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot that played a caffeine-free game, but really wanted a coffee instead.

I really wanted to see for myself what there was to write about, it's for all the reasons a classic case of: [b]curiosity killed the cat.[/b]

The developer on the other hand is the cat that satisfactional cash brought him back with more than he could chew. Gained a sentient brain, opposable thumbs, a crocked smile, a visit or 2 at the nearest Starbucks, and wrote a novel. True lavish spoils of a sinking ship.

My Review: Simple Bliss, Deeply Satisfying
I have to admit, when I first saw A Game About Digging a Hole on Steam, I laughed. The title is so brutally honest it's genius. I was skeptical—could a game built around such a basic chore possibly be fun? The answer, I quickly discovered, is a resounding yes. From the moment I shelled out my starting cash for a rickety house and a flimsy shovel, I was utterly hooked. The brilliance here lies in the game's immediate, satisfying rhythm. My goal was simple: chip away at the earth, collect the gleaming ores I found, drag my haul back to my tiny garage, sell it, and immediately invest in a bigger, better tool. This loop isn't just well-designed; it's practically magnetic, hitting that sweet spot of instant gratification that few games manage to sustain for long. I found myself completely losing track of time, always chasing that next tier of upgrade.

What truly elevates this experience is how meaningful every single progression milestone feels. This isn't just about watching a percentage tick up. Buying a new shovel isn't a minor stat buff; it’s a revolution. Getting a drill turns tedious work into a fast, gratifying descent. Finally affording that massive jetpack feels like I've earned wings. I loved that my hard work—the hours spent meticulously mining and selling—translated directly into becoming a vastly more efficient, cooler digger. As I pushed deeper, the atmosphere subtly shifted. The little bits of lore, the strange, ominous sounds I heard from below, and the promise of some legendary treasure added a layer of mystery. It transforms quickly from a mere digging simulator into a genuine adventure, all while maintaining a wonderfully chill and low-pressure vibe. Seriously, this is the ultimate "podcast game"—I could blissfully listen to music or a stream for hours, losing myself in the meditative rhythm of my pickaxe hitting bedrock.

I genuinely appreciate that the developers chose to keep this game short and focused. Its playtime—which I completed happily in just a few sittings—is not a flaw; it's a testament to its tight, purposeful design. Unlike so many endless sandboxes that overstay their welcome and drown you in pointless late-game systems, A Game About Digging a Hole never collapses under its own weight. It offers a premium, addictive experience and then wraps it up before the grind can become tiresome. While I know some players have criticized the final sequence for its change in tone (which I won't spoil), I found that it provided a necessary and exciting full stop. It gives all the hours I spent digging a clear, defined goal and a satisfying narrative conclusion. It proves that the developers knew exactly how much game was needed to tell their story, and they delivered it flawlessly.

A Game About Digging a Hole is a masterclass in elegant, minimalist execution. It took a concept that could have been boring and injected it with pure, addictive fun and incredible satisfaction. If you are anything like me and love a game that provides constant, rewarding progression, a relaxing atmosphere, and a brilliant core loop, you need to buy this immediately. For the low price, this game is an absolute steal and easily one of the most delightful, surprising hits I've played on Steam all year. Go on—grab your shovel and get digging!

Overall Review: A Game About Digging a Hole – Surprisingly Relaxing but Short-Lived

Hours played: 2 hours (enough to dig every inch of the yard)

At first glance, A Game About Digging a Hole seems like a simple concept: you dig a hole, explore the soil, and watch as your creation grows deeper. And that’s exactly what it is — but don’t underestimate the simple satisfaction it provides. There’s a hypnotic joy in controlling your digger, shaping the hole exactly as you want, and watching the world shift around your work. The mechanics are easy to understand, and the core gameplay loop is surprisingly addictive.

However, the game’s simplicity is also its biggest limitation. After digging for a while, the novelty begins to fade, and the short length becomes noticeable. The ending, in particular, was disappointing for me. Instead of continuing the digging experience or introducing something clever, the game concludes with glitchy giant pigs that are intended to be stealthy enemies — but they are poorly implemented and more frustrating than fun. It left me wishing the game had given me more time to dig or explore new mechanics before ending. The plot twist was OKAY but I'm not going to try to spoil.

Pros

✔ Satisfying core mechanics
Digging is oddly meditative. The physics, the way the soil shifts, and the gradual deepening of the hole are all simple but compelling. There’s a tangible sense of progress, especially when you reach new layers or uncover hidden areas.

✔ Complete achievement system
Despite the game’s short length, every achievement is attainable, which makes it feel rewarding. For completionists, being able to fully explore the yard, dig down to the core, and experiment with explosives adds extra fun.

✔ Relaxing and low-pressure gameplay
There’s no timer, no penalties, no combat — just you, your digging tool, and the ground. It’s a perfect game for unwinding or just zoning out for a couple of hours.

✔ Affordable price
At $6, the game offers a satisfying, short-lived experience at a low cost. You get a complete little package without feeling ripped off.

Cons

✘ Unsatisfying ending
The sudden introduction of glitchy giant pigs feels jarring and poorly executed. It’s not stealthy, challenging, or fun — it just abruptly ends the otherwise relaxing digging experience.

✘ Visual style issues
Some parts of the graphics are underwhelming. The textures and animations could use refinement, and the overall aesthetic sometimes feels inconsistent. On top of that, there are no graphics settings at all, so you can’t adjust resolution, effects, or quality, which limits the visual experience.

✘ Lack of multiplayer
It would have been amazing to dig alongside friends in a shared yard. Unfortunately, the hole isn’t big enough to make multiplayer feel meaningful, so this feature is absent — a missed opportunity for extended replayability.

✘ Short playtime
At around two hours, the game doesn’t offer a lot of longevity. Once you’ve dug every inch and explored the yard fully, there’s little incentive to replay unless you’re going for pure enjoyment or achievement hunting.

Gameplay & Mechanics

The digging controls are smooth and responsive, making it easy to carve out exactly the shape you want. Explosives add an extra layer of chaos and fun, letting you collapse sections of the hole or uncover hidden areas quickly. The sense of vertical progression — reaching deeper layers — is satisfying, and seeing the yard gradually hollowed out is strangely mesmerizing.

Unfortunately, the final section with the pigs feels like an afterthought. The stealth mechanics are clunky, the AI is unpredictable, and it interrupts the otherwise calm pacing of the game. It’s a frustrating way to conclude what is mostly a relaxing experience.

Visuals & Audio

The audio is subtle but effective. The sound of dirt moving, the clinks of your digging tool, and the occasional ambient noises all contribute to immersion. Music is minimal, which fits the meditative nature of the game.

Visually, the game is hit-or-miss. The yard and soil are fine, but some textures, character models, and background elements feel unpolished. The lack of graphics settings compounds this problem, especially on higher-end monitors where certain visual elements look flat or low-res.

Replay Value

There’s limited replayability due to the game’s short length. Once the yard is fully excavated and all achievements are earned, there’s little reason to return. That said, experimenting with different digging patterns, using explosives creatively, or just enjoying the zen-like digging loop can provide a small amount of additional enjoyment. Multiplayer would have helped here, but the game isn’t designed for shared digging experiences.

Final Thoughts

A Game About Digging a Hole is a short but enjoyable experience with surprisingly satisfying core mechanics. The joy of digging, shaping the soil, and reaching the yard’s deepest layers is unmatched in its simplicity. However, the game is limited by its short playtime, underwhelming ending, and lackluster visual polish. Multiplayer would have added a lot of replayability, and a few more options for settings or visual customization could improve the overall experience.

For $6, though, it’s worth a try if you enjoy relaxing, low-pressure gameplay, want to experiment with a simple physics sandbox, or just want to dig for fun. Just don’t expect hours of gameplay or a polished story-driven ending — this game is about the act of digging itself, and in that respect, it delivers.

шаг №3

шаг №5

шаг №6

 ~Modo de Preparo~

 - Massa:
1. Em um recipiente, misture o Leite com o suco de limão. Reserve até talhar.
2. Em uma batedeira, bata a manteiga com o açúcar até obter uma mistura esbranquiçada.

6. Adicione o corante e misture bem. A cor da massa deve ficar bem vermelha, se necessário, adicione mais corante.
7. Despeje a mistura em três formas redondas (20 cm de diâmetro) forrada com papel manteiga no fundo e laterais e leve para assar em forno médio (180°C) preaquecido, por cerca de 50 minutos.

- Montagem:
11. Com a Massa já fria, corte-a no sentido horizontal em 3 partes.
12. Utilize a própria forma que assou o bolo para fazer a montagem. Coloque uma das partes da massa e coloque uma camada de Recheio. Coloque a outra massa e mais um pouco de recheio, finalizando com a última massa. Leve ao freezer por cerca de 1 hora.
13. Desenforme o bolo e cubra com a Cobertura. Utilize os próprios farelos do bolo e frutas vermelhas para a decoração.

I honestly cannot say enough good things about this game--so much so that I've nominated it for two categories for THE STEAM AWARDS 2025. Where do I even begin?

1. Gameplay: Simple, Rewarding, Relaxing--with a surprise ending! There is just absolutely nothing about this game that is complex or difficult to understand. Somewhere in the yard is buried treasure. You have a shovel. You dig. Along the way, you find ore that you can sell for money to upgrade your equipment. You keep digging. Along the way you'll run into rewards, mysterious spaces, and obstacles that you need to work around or overcome to progress. The deeper you dig, the more challenging it becomes, until eventually you reach...?

Additionally, after completing the game, you're introduced to Achievements where you can acquire a golden drill! Who doesn't want a golden drill? Among the potential achievements is a time challenge to complete the game; for those who find it too difficult to achieve by "standard" means, there's an easy hack the devs were kind enough to stash in game: [spoiler] One of the tiles near the patio set on the side closest to the fence, if hit the right way by the drill, will give you an absurd amount of monies, allowing you to simply buy the advanced drill to go straight down to complete the game. It's near the space between the umbrella stand and the leg of the chair on the left. [/spoiler] 

2. Difficulty: That's where this game really is kinda unique-- it's only as difficult as you want to make it for yourself. Are you an obsessive-compulsive completionist, hell-bent on scouring away every speck of dirt from the hole on the way down until there's nothing left but a nice, clean, shiny monument to your obsessiveness? Or are you more concerned with just getting through the game as fast as possible, avoiding all the lures and exciting rewards you could potentially find on the way down? However you wanna play this game, those options and more are entirely open and up to you. 

At the end of the day, what happens when you finally reach [i]the end...[/i] makes the entire thing feel worthwhile and enjoyable. This game is well worth the full price, and I can't wait to see what this dev comes up with next!!

Can you get a more value for your money elsewhere? Sure. Does it lack infinite replayability? Yep. Would I still recommend "A Game About Digging A Hole"? Yes. 

"A Game About Digging A Hole" is almost exactly what it's advertised to be - a fun, upgrade-based time-waster, with a slight mystery behind it. Go in blind, enjoy it for what it is, replay it for completion if you want. I did everything there is to do and got all Steam Achievements in just under four hours. 

It's not going to intellectually challenge you, it's not going to last, but it might just be exactly what you need right now - A Game About Digging A Hole.

The mechanics are simple, but they work really well. No jank, no bugs, no fighting the controls; just a clean, satisfying gameplay loop that’s way more addictive than it has any right to be. Dig, upgrade, repeat… and suddenly an hour is gone.

The story is perfectly weird and random in a way that actually fits the game’s tone. It never tries too hard and never overstays its welcome, which honestly makes it even better.

My only real complaint is that I wanted more. I’d love to see DLC with additional digs or areas because once I was fully locked in, the game ended sooner than I wanted.

If you’re scrolling the store looking for something cozy, oddly compelling, and way better than the title suggests, this is it.

Fun while it lasted but this is not the game I'd seen advertised on YouTube,

You're a treasure hunter who has purchased a ludicrously cheap property with the promise of riches. 
By upgrading your gear, you can dig further and for longer in the hole that was once your lawn. You find progressively more valuable minerals the further you dig (and some sneaky smaller treasures along the way). Perhaps you'll find this fabled treasure if you just keep digging...


Misleading advertising aside, not too expensive and short, so alright if you're an achievement hunter.
My one gripe I have is that the ending (for understandable reasons) isn't particularly well implemented, especially with no crouch/sneak mechanic as it comes seemingly out of nowhere. I ended up just brute forcing it and getting lucky.

Gameplay wise, it runs smoothly, the controls feel pretty responsive, and the simplistic nature of it makes most of the game easy to pick up. I found the terrain destruction quite satisfying for the most part, especially when I reached the point I could hold the mouse down rather than clicking repeatedly (I wonder what the TTP is for this game...).

I'd have liked to see a bit more progression (as others have said), and perhaps more to spend your funds on, as by a certain point the money just accumulates. 
Some indication of the detectors being a thing (they just pop up when you're near something of interest) and or have them be something you can unlock would be nice rather than them just appearing, possibly even upgrade-able.
I know it might be repetitive and take away from the intended experience, but it'd be cool to see alternate themes/locations in future updates as options for further exploration post initial gameplay such as those you find in Placid Plastic Duck Simulator for example.

Recommend it if you fancy a chill couple of hours without having to allocate too much brain power.

[b]“A Game About Digging a Hole”[/b] — неожиданно медитативный опыт.
Геймплей простой, но именно в этом его сила: копаешь, углубляешься, и в какой-то момент ловишь себя на том, что полностью погружён в процесс. Спокойная атмосфера помогает расслабиться после дня, а ощущение интереса — [i]что же там дальше, под следующими слоями?[/i] — подталкивает копать ещё немного.

Игра отлично передаёт чувство исследования, хотя вокруг нет ни врагов, ни сложных механик. Просто ты, земля и путь вниз — и этим она цепляет. Отличный вариант для тех, кто ищет неспешную игру с элементом загадки.

[h1]A Game About Digging A Hole[/h1]

A Game About Digging A Hole je hra, která působí jako dobrý nápad na krátký experiment, ale nakonec u ní člověk spíš přemýšlí, jestli v tom není hlubší pointa… nebo jestli jen opravdu kope díru. Vžijete se do obyčejné postavy s lopatou a vaším úkolem je přesně to, co název říká. Kopat. Postupně se dostáváte hlouběji pod zem, ale že by se tam toho dělo nějak víc, to úplně ne. Občas narazíte na nějaký detail nebo změnu atmosféry, ale celkově je to spíš taková zvláštní meditace, u které si říkáte, jestli to má pointu, nebo jen prostě klikáte.

[b]Hratelnost[/b]
je jednoduchá, možná až moc. Ovládání je v pohodě, ale po chvíli máte pocit, že děláte pořád to samé dokola a nic moc se nemění

[b]Prostředí[/b]
je docela hezké na začátku, ale postupem času se přece jen okouká. Hra se na nějaké velké vizuální variace moc nesoustředí, i když pár momentů vypadá zajímavě.

[b]Umělá inteligence[/b]
v podstatě neexistuje, protože tu nemáte nepřátele.  A nebo nakonec jo? No v podstatě skoro celou hru vše stojí na vašem kopání a změnách prostředí. 

[b]Fyzika prostředí a postav[/b]
je v rámci možností fajn, kopání působí uspokojivě, hlína padá tak, jak by člověk čekal, a celkově to má dobrý rytmus.

[b]Grafika[/b]
je příjemná, stylová, ale nijak dechberoucí. Spíš minimalistická a atmosférická.

[b]Postavy[/b]
tu v podstatě nejsou – jen vy a lopata. Je to záměr, ale přidává to i trochu pocitu prázdnoty.

[h1]Shrnutí[/h1]
Abych to shrnul, tahle hra je spíš krátká zvláštnost než něco, k čemu by se člověk upínal. Doporučuji ji jen těm, kteří mají rádi zvláštní experimentální tituly a nečekají akci ani velký obsah. Kopání díry vám možná poskytne chvilku klidu nebo zamyšlení, ale po nějaké době si začnete přát, aby se tam něco fakt stalo. Zvuky a atmosféra fungují hezky, ale zbytek hry už tolik ne.

[b]Klady a zápory[/b]
+Zvláštní atmosféra
+Jednoduchý relax
+Stylové zpracování
-Minimální obsah
-Monotónnost
-Rychle se okouká

⭐ Avis sur A Game About Digging a Hole – Platine en 4.7h
Je viens de platiné A Game About Digging a Hole sur PC, et c’est un jeu aussi simple qu’original. Je l’ai terminé en 4,7 heures, d’une traite, et même si le concept paraît minimaliste, on se laisse surprendre.

✅ Points positifs :
• Un concept unique
Creuser un trou… ça paraît bête dit comme ça, mais le jeu réussit à en faire une expérience intéressante, presque hypnotique.

• Gameplay ultra accessible
Pas besoin d’être un pro : on creuse, on explore, on avance. Les mécaniques sont simples, fluides et faciles à comprendre.

• Une ambiance calme
La musique, les visuels, tout donne une vibe chill qui rend l’expérience agréable du début à la fin.

❌ Points négatifs :
• Très répétitif
Le gameplay repose presque uniquement sur la même action, ce qui peut devenir monotone si on n’accroche pas au concept.

• Peu de profondeur
Malgré le thème (😄), le jeu reste minimaliste. On aurait aimé plus de mécaniques ou de surprises.

• Durée de vie courte
Ceux qui veulent un jeu plus riche resteront un peu sur leur faim.

❤️ Conclusion
A Game About Digging a Hole est un petit jeu chill, minimaliste et original. Parfait pour une courte session relaxante. Ce n’est pas un jeu révolutionnaire, mais il offre exactement ce qu’il promet : une expérience simple, zen et un peu hypnotique.

Купил эту игру, чтобы расслабиться. "Что может быть проще, чем копать яму?" – думал я. О, наивный!

Спустя 5 часов беспрерывного копания я могу с уверенностью заявить: это не игра, это духовная практика. Моя жизнь теперь разделена на "до ямы" и "после ямы".

Что восторгает:

Глубокий геймплей (буквально). С каждым сантиметром вглубь тебя посещают всё новые экзистенциальные вопросы. "А что, если я копаю не вниз, а вверх, просто вселенная перевернулась?".

Неожиданные открытия. Нашел ржавый гвоздь, три червяка по имени Боб и свою потерянную мотивацию к работе. Черви Бобы теперь мои напарники, мы советуемся.

Я начал видеть сны в пикселях. И во сне я тоже копаю.

Вердикт: Если вы искали игру, которая задаст вам вопрос "а зачем?", но в уютной и абсурдной форме – это она. Это медитация, доведенная до абсурда. 10/10, буду копать дальше, мне кажется, я уже почти у края... вселенной. Или дна. Неважно.

P.S. Передайте создателям: моя лопата хочет кофе. Двойной эспрессо.

I have two main issues with this game. 

First, the gameplay loop is extremely basic and not about actually building a mine or anything: grind resources, buy upgrades, repeat. I don’t inherently mind that—there are plenty of games where I enjoy that kind of simple, incremental progression. But something about the way this game handles it just isn’t satisfying. Neither did the progression feel rewarding, nor did the actual mechanics feel satisfying. Out of the two hours I played at, one of them was spent pushing myself to the end purely out of curiosity, not because I was actually having fun.

And then, once I finally got there, the game abruptly shifts from a wholesome, brightly colored experience into a dark, gritty horror sequence, which isn’t for me at all.

To be fair, the horror tag is listed on the store page and the trailer does hint at it right at the end, so that alone wouldn’t warrant a negative review. But paired with the unsatisfying gameplay, the sudden tonal whiplash made the whole experience fall flat for me.

Digging a Hole can be mildly entertaining if you just want to pass some time or play a quick casual game. However, it quickly becomes a never-ending loop of upgrades and repetition; an endless grind of digging with very little sense of progress or purpose.

The game offers few tools, no story, and almost no variety. It feels more like an idle clicker without the reward loop that keeps you engaged. The graphics are standard, the gameplay is minimal, and the fun fades fast.

On the positive side, it runs smoothly and has no major bugs, so it can satisfy players looking for a simple, brainless distraction. Just don’t buy it at full price there’s not enough substance to justify it.

COMO HACER CAUSA RELLENA 

Ingredientes (para 4 porciones)
Para la base:

1 kg de papa amarilla (o blanca si no consigues)

3 cucharadas de ají amarillo molido

Jugo de 2 limones

3 cucharadas de aceite vegetal

Sal al gusto

Para el relleno:

2 pechugas de pollo desmenuzadas (también puede ser atún)

½ taza de mayonesa

1 cebolla picada muy fina (opcional)

Jugo de ½ limón

Sal y pimienta al gusto

Para decorar (opcional):

Huevo duro en rodajas

Aceitunas negras

Palta (aguacate) en láminas

Perejil picado

Preparación paso a paso

Cocina las papas:
Lávalas bien y hiérvelas con cáscara hasta que estén suaves. Luego pélalas y prénsalas mientras están tibias.

Sazona la papa:
Mezcla el puré con el ají amarillo, el jugo de limón, el aceite y sal. Amasa bien hasta que quede suave, sin grumos y de color uniforme.

Prepara el relleno:
En un bol, mezcla el pollo desmenuzado con mayonesa, limón, sal y pimienta. Si deseas, añade cebolla picada o un poco de perejil.

Arma la causa:

En un molde (puede ser redondo o cuadrado), coloca una capa de papa y aplánala.

Encima, añade una capa del relleno de pollo.

Coloca encima otra capa de papa para cubrir todo.

Presiona suavemente para que quede compacta.

Decora:
Cubre la superficie con una fina capa de mayonesa. Agrega rodajas de huevo, aceitunas y láminas de palta.

Refrigera:
Déjala reposar al menos 30 minutos antes de servir para que tome consistencia.

For $5 I feel conflicted about A Game About Digging A Hole. On one hand, it's a novel idea with a decent execution; while on the other, it is a very short, chill game with not that much else to it. With the ladder making it feel lackluster and easy to move on from after completion. Which makes this one of those games I would love to have a "mixed" option to choose from while reviewing. However, since it was a minor step above average for me, I am still going to recommend it.

I think it is worth picking it up at it's base price of $5, as long as you are keeping your expectations in check with the title and screenshots of the game. 

A heads up as well to all of you that are going to be 100% the game. Be warned that the Rainbow achievement requires multiple playthroughs and is a bit tedious just to be tedious.

Рекомендую однозначно.

A Game About Digging a Hole succeeds by being very focused. It doesn’t try to be a sprawling adventure or a massive simulation — it confines itself to one bold, simple idea. And in many ways, it pulls that off. The digging feels satisfying, the upgrade loop is crisp, and the hidden bits keep curiosity alive.

However, its ambitions also limit it. The polish issues, limited content, and abrupt ending pull it back from being a masterpiece. It’s more like a strong, quirky experiment than a full-blown AAA indie epic.

The game is pretty poorly optimized, for such a simple game you'd expect excellent performance, yet my PC which comfortably runs AAA games experienced several instances of stuttering. On my older laptop, it ran worse than FC5. Granted that game is several years old at this point, but it's still a good-looking AAA game.

Aside from that, I don't think the game mechanics compliment each other well.
The Health bar is functionally useless, you take so little damage from most falls that it hardly matters, [spoiler]and the 1 enemy in the game is an instant kill anyways[/spoiler].
The bag inventory and battery both act similarly, to limit your trip time and encourage you to come back up regularly, but I didn't see the point of having both mechanics. The bag is only an issue at the very beginning, when you don't need to worry about fuel use on the way up or anything, but you're always conscious of the battery. So why not just have the battery?
The jetpack and lanterns were good ideas executed well. Did not care for dynamite though, it was very finicky and often wouldn't stay in place, especially annoying considering how expensive it is to use.

8/10 A Game About Digging A Hole is a game where you dig a hole in your backyard, upgrade your tools, dig some more, and find a little more than treasure.

My takeaway: A Game About Digging A Hole is a simple concept game that flourished with intuitive controls, a dash of mystery, and relaxing gameplay. Play as a new home owner who digs in their backyard looking for treasure. You dig, use the minerals you dug up to get money, use the money to upgrade your tools, and dig some more. It took me a little under four hours to complete this game with all achievements.

The sounds, aesthetic, and music fit the game perfectly and the minimalistic gameplay makes for an easy playing experience. There’s no real rush to do anything which makes the digging experience oddly satisfying and relaxing. The end is a little odd but it adds to the charm and mystery of the game. Works great on Steam Deck.

The ending was unlike any other aspect of the game which was jarring. Lack of real physics also means that minerals and tiny debris float in the air making it hard to get some achievements and can be mildly frustrating late game. The game itself is very short and although it definitely could be expanded, I don’t think there’s any talk about expanding it. Very little replayability after getting all the achievements.

Aventura de exploración 3D sencilla en la cual seguimos la premisa de excavar en el patio de nuestra recién comprada casa, para intentar encontrar el tesoro que se aloja en las profundidades.

La jugabilidad es bastante buena y el movimiento es fluido.

La banda sonora es un poco inexistente (aunque no esperaba menos de un título de estas características).

La progresión y desbloqueables se siente muy bien ejecutada. La exploración de los coleccionables está bien conseguida.

Posee localización al castellano, lo cual siempre es positivo en cualquier título.

Como único punto negativo, he de decir que puntualmente he sufrido artefactos visuales al cavar, aunque muy pocas veces.

It's a simple game with a simple title. You dig a hole in the ground as deep as you can. Along the way you find ore to sell and purchase upgrades for your shovel, inventory space, battery, and a jet pack that helps you climb out of your hole. There really isn't anything else to the game. It's got simple graphics, simple mechanics, and a simple goal. It has a similar feel to digging in Minecraft in that it's something you can zone out with.

The only complaints I could voice would be that the dirt doesn't have the physics of real dirt, it will float in the air if you dig out all the surrounding material. This is fine until you end up with a tiny speck of floating dirt that you get stuck on. Trying to find that one cluster of pixels on your screen that is totally comprised of the same brown texture is like looking in a large tub of Skittles and trying to eyeball which two are stuck together.

Additionally, there is no reset button. If you are going for 100% completion of the game and want the speedrun achievement you'll have to exit out and relaunch the game if you realize your run has failed. This can be a little frustrating as there's a heavy amount of RNG in the speedrun achievement, so you'll be resetting a couple of times more than likely. Having to relaunch the game is just a little extra salt in the wound of an RNG botched achievement.

Overall, simple and fine. Not a game you'll dump a hundred hours into, but not every game needs to be that. A fun game for a weekend achievement hunter, or to turn on when you want a zen garden with holes.

Who knew that such a simple concept as digging a hole in one's own back garden would prove to be as fun and popular as it has been as can be seen here in this very indie? Certainly it wasn't one that I was expecting much from, albeit the care and attention put into this game has surprised me since I have always enjoyed those few titles that explore climbing the heights of the skies and beyond as well as those that have you mine and delve downwards below into the very depths of the Earth itself, which is thankfully a key focus of this intriguing game!

Though as always, the gameplay is what matters most as the general story of A Game About Digging A Hole revolves around the player having purchased a seemingly-cheap house under the premise of potential treasures that are assumed to be burrowed deep below the very garden of said house, hence starting off the game with nothing but a trowel in hand and the sheer determination to dig your way down to the bottom in order to reach this special treasure that awaits you!

How you go about this is largely down to you, as your tool is powered by a unique battery that is slowly consumed upon the use of each dirt removed. Whilst this saves the time and energy that one would naturally need to spend to quickly remove said land in real life alongside the soil conveniently disappearing off into the ether, this comes at a cost as one can not afford to allow the battery to run out as doing so will cause it to "explode" as the game bluntly puts it, which results in you losing all of your valuable minerals and ores gained alongside crippling your health and needing to recover it.

Which nicely transitions into the next segment of my review here as, in order to progress at a reasonable speed, one will need to improve not just their shovel for superior digging power but also the battery for enhanced lifespan and the player's inventory for extra goodies to carry with them out of their digging spot each trip as well as even a jetpack that can be bought and improved to give it more of a boost in exchange for taking some energy out of your battery if you find yourself stuck in a rut of your own making! Seeing as these ores will help to pay the bills and keep you digging alongside any extra cash being useful for making upgrades along the way so that progress isn't going at a sloth-like pace throughout the duration of the game.

Given that the ultimate goal of this game is to reach the treasure chest that has been buried deep below, it acts as a nice progression system to help players speed things along from digging up simple stones and unremarkable coal at the surface all the way down below where valuables like gold and diamonds reside at. Although it goes without saying that there are also opportunities for players to seek out as well as extra obstacles that stand in the way of your mining in the depths that one should keep an eye out for!

Such examples of opportunities are objects buried deep within the dirt that can be detected when within close proximity via a radar that glows brighter the closer your cursor is pointed towards the source whilst another instrument, a sort of 'depth gauge' detection instrument, will alert players to a different kind of treasure that will show up when you are close to a mine shaft tunnel via being told if it is below or above you alongside the circle informing you of how close you are to it, seeing as these often contain not just extra cash but other goodies that will aid players for deeper exploration into the underground!

On the other hand, such natural obstacles as sandstone rocks will not prove so easy to get rid of as these require the use of expensive dynamites to clear or otherwise be dug around. Similarly another variant of this can be found even deeper via the form of molten rocks that will quickly harm the player upon contact but can be destroyed with said dynamites if the player has any on them. (A handy tip for those concerned, as long as a dynamite's small explosion is in contact with either sandstone or lava rock then it will usually clear that specific patch outright rather than working in a circular form of clearing as you would expect from the soil destroyed around it)

Although this is one indie that isn't exactly bursting to the seams with content, given that it will likely last most around 5-6 hours to finish it and several more to fully complete all of the achievements, it delivers the promise of an interesting experience down below rather well! This is also helped by the fact that some of us as young kids will have had the fun fantasy of digging a large hole in their parents back-garden from many years ago, especially with how the colourful graphics helps to sell players on the whimsical adventures that one will likely have when digging further and further down given how dark it quickly becomes which makes the use of attachable lamps practically mandatory to see where you're going alongside the aforementioned dynamites for any hardened materials to blow up!

My only main criticism come from how there could have been extra layers that added extra progression as well as new and harder obstacles to avoid, whether as part of the main game itself or left for post-game challenges. Other nitpicks include the repetitive clicking that can get tiresome when needing to press the mouse button for every single time you wish to make use of your shovel (although the last two upgrades negate this thankfully) and the odd game design choice of locking achievements behind completion of the game although, given how short this game is to begin with, I suspect this won't prove to be too much of an issue for most players.

Concluding my review here, I can easily recommend A Game About Digging A Hole as a casual exploration game focusing on a mining-like gameplay cycle (similar to such Flash titles as Motherload and MegaDrill from back in the day) for those after something a little different here! Just be sure to not dig *too* deep here, for as the old saying goes [i]"Let sleeping dogs lie"[/i] very much applies here for those who think themselves an expert in the arts of digging hard-rock soil...

TLDR Version:

• Simple gameplay featuring a brilliant concept of fulfilling a childhood fantasy of digging one large hole in their parents' back-garden fully realized in this indie (+)
• Features various tiers of ores/minerals to acquire through digging down below in the soil which can be sold for cash to spend on four types of upgrades that furthers progression (+)
• Short and sweet experience that doesn't overstay its welcome that can easily be enjoyed within 5-6 hours of gameplay whilst also offering achievements for those seeking them (+)
• Includes randomized tunnels, objects of value and chests for players to seek out and loot using metal detection tools whilst navigating around natural obstacles with the help of lamps and dynamite (+)
• The colourful graphics of A Game About Digging A Hole are smooth and vibrant whilst not being too much of a distraction which makes for a memorable trip down the soil whilst digging in the contrasting dark underground (+)

• The gameplay cycle, whilst effective, lacks a certain extra layer of 'depth' to it for those looking for more longer-form content that adds extra challenges and further deep territory to explore (-)
• Achievements can only begin being unlocked after reaching the end of the game for the first time, something that could be off-putting to those looking to gain them as they go along (-)
• Clicking the mouse button repeatedly to dig with your trowel/shovel will likely become sore on your hands if played in long sessions, even if this is partially mitigated with upgrading to a drill towards the end (-)
