Il y a quelquechose dans l’action de creuser un trou de profondément satisfaisant. Que ce soit en vrai, comme dans son jardin, ou de manière simulée, comme dans un jeu vidéo. Comme si chaque coup de pelle, qu’elle soit de bois ou de pixels, titillait une source de dopamine primordiale, léguée par nos ancêtres, et qui ayant traversé les âges, se trouve ravivée par un jeu vidéo à l’essence simple mais pas simpliste. Poser les mots exacts sur cette sourde et subtile jouissance dépasse mon talent, mais quiconque ayant creusé un trou à la plage comprendra l’effet magnétique et hypnotisant de cette activité si anodine en apparence.

Voila la sensation que restitue brillamment ce jeu. L’expérience est courte mais intense et rejouable à souhait, voire même « speedrunnable ». Pour sublimer la satisfaction mystique de mettre des coups de pelle, le jeu propose un léger système de progression, reposant une boucle de gameplay minimale mais efficace. On creuse, on trouve des cailloux, on sort de son trou, on vend les cailloux, on recharge sa pelle, on achète des upgrades et on retourne dans son trou. Rapidement, le trou se transforme en galerie, puis en caverne, puis en crevasse, puis en canyon, illuminé comme une piste d’atterrissage par des loupiottes de mineur. Quelques trésors viennent pimenter cette excavation (apparemment) sans but. Passé les 50 mètres de profondeur, on s’aperçoit que la lumière du soleil ne perce plus du tout et un vague sentiment d’angoisse s’installe. Les cavernes semblent toujours plus noires et menaçantes, malgré une mise en scène tout à fait neutre et ne cherchant pas à susciter la peur. Pour la partie technique, c’est le minimum syndical mais tout est fonctionnel. Des visuels trop élaborés auraient d’ailleurs été un détriment pour un jeu basé sur la physique tel que celui-ci.

Digging a hole est la promesse d’un après-midi reposant, ou le temps passe vite, captivé par un concept aussi simple qu’addictif. Un divertissement pur, instantané et appréciable par tous. A faire sans se presser et sans préjugés.

[h1] A Game About Digging [h1]

This is a short semi semi-cozy game that will have you hooked for a couple of hours. The gameplay is straightforward: you are digging a hole to find treasure. The progression and upgrades are perhaps too simple, as I finished upgrading everything right around the hour mark. I did find the ending to be interesting and a different change of pace. I think if the game is on sale and you want a mindless game to lose a couple of hours in, then it's great. I do not think it is worth the full price at $10, though. 

[h2] Graphics  [h2]

They are nothing too special, super basic, yet kinda cozy feeling. The fonts used are easy to read and not too small. The only critique I have is that it can get pretty dark if you don't have a lamp with you. 


[h2] Sound / Music [h2]

The music was fine, nothing extraordinary, but still somewhat soothing. I also loved the small sound ambiance of bats and other cave sounds. Towards the end of the game, it got a little darker, which I was not expecting. 

[h2] Game play [h2] 

This game is hella simple, You are digging a hole to find various minerals, mines that contain treasure chests full of money and other supplies, as well as another secret at the end I won't spoil. You start with a shovel and then quickly upgrade to a drill. I found that when I started using the drill is where things picked u,p and I felt like a digging God 

[h2] Price [h2]

I think this game is not worth the full price of $10, but it is a great buy when it is on sale for five.

A game with a lot of potential that fails to deliver anything worth doing. 

[h2]-- Visuals --[/h2]
Nothing really to write home over with this title. It's inoffensive in appearance, with very little memorability. 

[h2]-- Story --[/h2]
Nonexistent. This is fine for this type of game, but more would have always been better.

[h2]-- Gameplay --[/h2]
It's a game about digging a hole. It does this quite well.

EXCEPT.

The upgrades stop extremely early. If you are just digging straight to the bottom, this is probably not a big deal. If you're  like me, however, and wanted to clear out the entire hole - it then becomes EXTREMELY tedious. 

This also brings me into my biggest and most severe criticism of this game. It locks almost all achievements behind New Game +, but it does not TELL you this until you have FINISHED THE GAME. The game assumes you will rush to the end on your first playthrough and then go back for more. Meaning, if you did *everything* on your first playthrough then you're locked out of all achievements unless you do it all again.

[h2]-- Final Thoughts --[/h2]
A zen time-sink that takes a nose dive into its own hole as soon as you try to engage with the game beyond 'haha funny hole game'.

This game is indeed about digging a hole, and it is cheap to purchase, but it also feels dishonest. Maybe even predatory.

Digging is a "click once to dig once" affair until you upgrade the shovel 3 or 4 times. To comfortably do that, you will also end up upgrading your other stuff 3 or so times. That's a lot of clicking, and because of that the game just doesn't feel good at all until that 3rd/4th upgrade.

You would also expect that upgrading would be something that you do throughout the entire game, but I had maxed out everything somewhere between 1/3 - 1/2 of the way down. I did dig most of the whole hole out until about halfway down so I got most of what I could find, but still...all progression was DONE halfway down the hole and after that money was pretty much worthless. Also none of that progress matters at the end of the game. Also even with digging way more hole than necessary I finished the game in around 5 hours.

Figure you'll just pick up the achievements and move on? You *technically* don't get access to achievements until you've finished the game. I say *technically* because things you would have unlocked during your first playthrough do unlock once you begin the 2nd playthrough--along with in-game trophies to track your progress towards each. However, not allowing you to get them at all your first time through feels scummy and not being able to track progress towards them until you have to start the game over and upgrade all your terrible starting equipment again--now armed with the knowledge of how monotonous, repetitive, dull, and slow the game is for the first half or more--would sure make me more likely to give up if I were the achievement-hunting type.

I honestly cannot understand why A Game About Digging a Hole blew up as much as it did, I may be in the minority when I say this, but I think this game sucks and I stand by that.

I get why the simplicity and silly nature of the game would be appealing, somehow it appears that everyone has an innate fascination with just digging a massive hole, maybe it is something primal I don’t know. However, this game did not scratch that itch for me and had a bunch of other frustrations that made this game annoying in the end. First things first, the whole exploding shovel thing seemed not only annoying to me but also completely unnecessary. The motivation to drop off your materials to sell is enough motivation to perform the loop of mining and going back up. The exploding shovel was not often a problem, but it did break the flow of the game on occasion and just took away from the fun for me. The limited upgrade path was disappointing and given how little it added to the game it felt like wasted potential. The way that the digging worked was the worst though, which, you know, is kind of the whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game so that irritates me. See the issue is that the game has too great of a tolerance for small dirt pieces and allows them to float independently so if you are not digging perfectly you will leave behind these little annoying pieces that you will catch on frequently. Cool whatever, but the real issue is two-fold. First, the exploding shovel thing is linked to your jetpack’s energy too, so if you get caught on the way up while trying to fly up by one of these tiny pieces you can lose too much energy and end up getting yourself killed which feels terrible. Second, the fall damage in this game is not gracious with distance at all, it does not take a large fall to kill you, and if there is this tiny hidden piece of dirt and you accidentally hit it you will die. It was so stupid and frustrating to die to a brown ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ speck against the backdrop of brown… Lower the size tolerance, make it so pieces just don’t float, or make it so that if the piece is small and you hit it fast enough it just breaks; how can you make a game about digging and ♥♥♥♥ that up so hard??? DRG got this ♥♥♥♥ right just look there. Now it does get better when you get the drill because you can just hold down the button and smoothly make a hole, but it is still not immune to the issue. It killed my joy when going for the achievements (they are generally really easy), trying to get the big drop achievement was way more annoying than it needed to be because of this. The other parts of the game are fine, the game feels just a bit sluggish and I found the gravity to be a bit bouncy which made hitting the ground even a bit too fast even more annoying. Overall though, I 100%ed this game because it was fairly easy and gave me a full perspective of the game, not because it was good.

The story is stupid. Obviously, it was just set dressing but with the weak gameplay it just makes me want more out of it and it did not deliver. I did not find it clever, funny, or interesting.

With repetitive simple sounds and a soundtrack so unmemorable I had to start up the game to check if it even had one, I am critical of that too. I mean the sound effects aren’t bad, but they do feel sharper than I would have expected if that makes any sense. The stepping sounds are just a bit off in my opinion because of this as an example. Also, the volume goes from -10 to 10 with “default” being the middle… Why? Was 0 to 20 not sensible enough? 0 to 100 would have been better with the extra granularity anyway. What is negative volume? What an odd choice. Yeah, as for music, just put on your own. In fact, just turn off all sound and listen to something else it will be more enjoyable.

Visually the game is fine but I think the lighting is goofy and the lack of variety in the game’s environment is definitely a limiting factor. What I mean by the lighting being goofy is that I dug a massive hole in my first run for the hell of it and yet the way that the game uses darkness does not account for the sunlight in a particularly natural way. It would have also been nice to see a brightness slider and this is especially funny because, in the speedrunning community, they apparently had to decide it was not cheating to adjust the brightness because one of the most basic features in modern game visuals is missing from the game. Animations are pretty weak as well. That being said what few models there are in the game are stylized well and what is above ground is well-lit and colorfully pleasant. Visually though, it is also fair to say that the game is not special in any sort of way either, it looks like a ton of other indie games and could easily be confused for hundreds of others.

Overall, I think it is pretty clear that I think that this game is ass. Why does it have an 89% positive? Looking through the reviews I have been unable to find a good reason as to why in my opinion beyond, “meme game memed”, all other justifications felt weak to me. When I saw how excited people were getting about this game, I decided that it would be fun to not spoil anything and go in blind; however, I wish I had saved myself the $5 by watching a video instead, it was not worth my time. Maybe it is to you, but I would suggest watching a playthrough instead before using your money, you may just be glad you did.

Обзор игры "A Game About Digging A Hole"

Ну что ж, давайте копнем поглубже в эту игру, где вы, собственно, копаете! 🕳️

👍 Что мне понравилось:

Копать и копать: Это как уборка в квартире, только без необходимости выносить мусор! Вы просто копаете, находите предметы и думаете: "Что же я на самом деле ищу — потерянные ключи или смысл жизни?" 🤔

Оптимизм и пессимизм: В этой игре есть особая атмосфера — вы можете почувствовать себя одновременно оптимистом и пессимистом. С одной стороны, вы надеетесь найти сокровища, а с другой — осознаете, что копаете в никуда. Как говорится, "копай глубже, может, найдешь себя!" 😅

Неожиданные находки: Иногда вы находите что-то действительно странное, типа старой обуви или потерянного кота (шутка!). Это добавляет игре изюминку и немного абсурда.

👎 Что мне не понравилось:

Однообразие: Как и в любом хорошем фильме, здесь есть моменты, когда вы понимаете, что уже видели этот сюжет. Копать одну и ту же яму на протяжении 10 уровней может стать утомительным. "Может, стоило заняться садоводством?" — думаете вы, глядя на свою виртуальную лопату. 🌱

Графика: Простите, но выглядеть как пиксельный шедевр из 90-х — это не то, что я ждал. Если бы у меня был выбор между этой игрой и рисованием на песке, я бы выбрал второе.

Не хватает глубины: Играть в эту игру — всё равно что читать роман с одним предложением. "Копай, пока не устанешь!" — и это вся суть. Где же сюжет, где же повороты? 😩

🤷‍♂️ Рекомендации:

Если вы ищете что-то, чтобы развеять скуку на 15 минут, "A Game About Digging A Hole" может подойти. Но если вы хотите, чтобы ваша жизнь была наполнена смыслом и глубиной, лучше выберите что-то другое. В конце концов, кто знает, может, в реальной жизни вы тоже найдете сокровища, просто копая в своем дворе! 🎉

I gave it a good go, and quite frankly... this is an awful time. Dig a hole, run back up, deal with energy / inventory, go back down, freefall a bit, almost die because you hit a single pixel of dirt.... Spend ages trying to click on said pixel...
This is a bad time.

For starters, there's energy. There really doesn't need to be, but there is. You run out of energy, you die. There's no climbing back out or trying to get your way out, no, your tool explodes. You die.

Edit: Accessibility, you cannot toggle sprint, you cannot toggle jet pack. Both are buttons you have to hold down to use. There's no option to change this.

Most of your gameplay is going to be digging down, picking up 3-6-9-12-15  however many times you upgrade your inventory, things. Then going back up and selling things. And that's it.

Like, I get that it's a cheap game about digging a hole, what was I expecting? Well. Gravity on the dirt for one. I was expecting that those single pixels of dirt might just fall, or not matter. No, if you miss a single pixel of dirt. That single pixel can ruin your play. Either by falling into it, or by trying to get past it on your way out.

For two, I was expecting that when you got the drill, you'd be able to drill all those rocks that you need dynamite for... no, the Drill is just an autoshovel. And given that I was already using an autoclicker. The drill is useless. So you upgrade the shovel so far, and then you get waste of money upgrades.

Finally, my biggest issue with the game... You cannot upgrade your shovel to a point that you can just dig straight down and not have to worry about specs of dirt getting in the way, so you can just free fall... This isn't possible. You still have to dig yourself around a bit, sure, a lot easier, but still not what I was excited for when I clicked that final upgrade.

I know this game is cheap, but there are free games that are better than this, go play one of those instead. I recommend Motherlode. A flash game from way back when I was young. Released in 2004 (I would've been 11) You play as a drilling machine, you dig, you get ores. There's a lot more gameplay to it, there's even an improved version on steam.
And yeah, sure, there's the same issue I bring up in the spoiler below... but with one key difference that I'll mention there.

If you don't want spoilers, then this is the end of the review for you. Thanks for reading, or skipping to the end, whatever floats your goat.



-------------------------------------------------------------------
Spoilers, I guess? Do you care? If you do don't read this next bit.
[spoiler]If you dig down far enough, there's a boss to fight. A giant mole. Ooh, scary... Well if it touches you, you instantly die. 
I didn't have any dynamite on me, but the boss fight I'm guessing is throw dynamite at mole, boom. Easy.
Well, for one.. I love moles. I don't want to kill them. Much less do I want to throw explosives at them. Like... Just no.
But also, in a game about digging a hole, why am I suddenly embroiled in the worst combat ever against a giant mole requiring to... have to go up again, buy a stick of dynamite and go all the way back down.

I decided instead of doing that, I'd just refund the game. Go hug my mole plushy, and promise never to throw a stick of dynamite at him.

At least with Motherlode, I didn't have to kill an animal. Like, sure, I've killed tonnes of animals in tonnes of games... But in Skyrim I always avoid killing foxes and rabbits. I'd much rather kill the devil, or a deathclaw or something.

I know this is an issue that won't matter to most people. It matters to me though, and it's my review.

Another issue that won't matter to most people. Despite the steam description of no rush, there is a rush. 10% of the achievements (Sure, that's just one achievement) are to complete the game in under 30 minutes. That's going to be a rush.[/spoiler]
----------------------------------------------------------------------


Ultimately. Steam asks you a question. "Do you recommend this game?" Well, I'm not going to recommend this game, so I have to click no. If that bothers you... as it often bothers people for some reason.... just buy the game anyway, heck, buy it to spite me. I am stating that I didn't like the game. That doesn't mean that you cannot like the game, that just means that I didn't.
If you decide to play it anyway, and you enjoy it... good. Glad you had fun.
But for me... This game isn't very fun. Not much else I can say about that.


Thanks for reading, or skipping to the end, have a lovely day. <3

Bit torn on thumbs up or thumbs down.  Going with thumbs down because there's really not much to the game which might surprise people who were expecting more based on the "very positive" rating it has on steam.  So I think thumbs down is more helpful here. 

With that said, although this game is very simple and very short, its executed well enough to be fun for that short period of time. And they do include a new game + with some achievements to get. (Although almost all of those achievements are very easy to get as well.) 

At a baseline price of 5 dollars, the devs do at least seem to acknowledge that there's really not much here with this title. And I appreciate that.  But even at 5 dollars, I think the time to dollar ratio represents mediocre value if you only plan on completing the story.  It'll take most people under an hour to complete.  (The only reason I have 15 hours on here is because I got it in my head that I wanted to clear out the entire hole and because it took me a few tries to complete the game in under 30 minutes for an achievement). 

I'd say if you only plan on playing this for the initial story play through, then wait for it to go on sale and grab it for a buck or two.  If you're the type that will spend time going for the achievements, then its probably just barely worth the full price.

The problem I have with this game is how disposable it really is. 99% of the games I play no matter how bad or good they are never seem like a total waste because there's usually something in them that keeps me going. And to be fair, I thought this game was going to really do something different and it seemed interesting. I will keep things spoiler free for those who have not played it, but this has to be one of the most simpleminded, unfulfilling games I've played in a long time. The game cheaps out on you by the very last minutes by completely shifting in tone and having the most blatantly, obvious and predictable ending I think I've ever encountered in a game. It's so frustrating to me that a game like this, which had a lot going for it, just felt like a spit in the face to the player who wasted all their time thinking something worthwhile was going to happen, only to realize there's nothing interesting, unique, special, or memorable about this ending.

And the game had a lot of momentum going for it in the beginning. I really enjoyed the gameplay loop and thought this could be something like Deep Rock Galactic but without combat and manual mining. The fact that you need to earn an automatic drill in order to have a break from clicking is great! I like that! And finding minerals and other sorts of things had some sort of semblance of enjoyment. However, I cannot with good faith recommend it at all. It left a sour taste in my mouth after finishing it.

I'm not trying to bad mouth the developer because he definitely had something going here and seriously, if it was just relaxing mining I would have wholeheartedly recommended it, but it felt like a slap in the face for all that progress only to be trolled into something so obvious. This game feels like another in what I am going to call "Viral Wastebin Games", where the goal is to seemingly make a game that will get popular for one instance (say a week, a month or so) and then will be quickly forgotten by the people who bought it and the streamers who streamed it. Games like this feel like the worst clickbait possible. And that's unfortunate. Games are more than just viral tiktoks, games are pieces of art that stand the test of time. The cynical side of my brain tells me this was done quickly and cheaply to gain popularity for an entire month. But I don't know what the developer had in mind with this game and I'm not here to understand the reasons why. All I can say is that if this was an honest effort, it could have been improved massively if the ending wasn't terribly obvious and you just focused on endless mining of minerals instead of trying to reach a goal. Hell, A Rogue-Like mode could have been fun if you wanted to continue with the tonal shift at the end so you could dig down more and see what things lay ahead and make camp sites to continue progress and sell minerals still.

Overall, I'm just not pleased. This could have been something really promising and for a rare instance I was beginning to agree with the reviews which is something I don't usually do. If you really want a small game like this that's going to stick with you, Portal is nearly 20 Years Old and still people are in awe of it today and the mystery, even though we know what's commonly known now about the game, is still fun to experience and is still remembered fondly to this day. In 5 years time, no one is going to remember this. You can bet on that.

The gameplay is as simple as the trailer shows - you start digging a hole in you garden, sell materials that you collect and upgrade your gear to be even better at digging - and keep going deeper. It's a simple, satisfying and relaxing experience.

The first run's gametime will likely be around 2-4 hour, depending how much time you'll spend getting to know the 4 upgradeable tool and how focused you are about getting to the bottom. After that, the 2nd and later runs are called achievement runs, meaning that the gameplay stays the same, but now the game will check if you unlocked any achievements.
(It won't show those in the 1st run, but will check all that you had completed when starting the 2nd run.)

I haven't encountered any bugs or crashes. The game runs stable.

There were some weird physics when you throw dynamite (sometimes it bounces out of smaller holes made above rocks) and the jetpack's control felt a little awkward (went more forward than upwards). Nothing serious, all of this can be ignored by digging a wider hole.

If the trailer made you think that you might like this game, give it a try.

[h1]Review zu „A Game About Digging A Hole“[/h1]

Manchmal braucht ein Spiel keinen bombastischen Namen oder eine komplexe Story, um zu fesseln – „A Game About Digging A Hole“ beweist genau das. Was auf den ersten Blick wie ein scherzhafter Titel wirkt, entpuppt sich schnell als eine charmant reduzierte Spielerfahrung, die mit überraschend meditativem Gameplay, cleverem Design und subtiler Tiefe überzeugt. Der Titel ist Programm – und doch verbirgt sich hinter dem einfachen Grabprozess mehr, als man zunächst erwarten würde.

[h1]Handlung[/h1]

Die Handlung von „A Game About Digging A Hole“ ist bewusst zurückhaltend. Es gibt keine klassischen Quests, keine NPCs, keine übergeordnete Geschichte. Stattdessen wird der Spieler in eine stille Welt geworfen, in der er lediglich mit einer Schaufel ausgestattet ist – und einem einzigen Ziel: Graben.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3460111160

Doch mit der Zeit merkt man, dass nicht alles so harmlos und simpel ist, wie es scheint. Unter der Oberfläche – im wahrsten Sinne – lauert eine geheimnisvolle Tiefe, die mehr Fragen aufwirft als Antworten liefert. Wer aufmerksam gräbt und die Umgebung beobachtet, entdeckt eine unterirdische Geschichte, die sich ganz langsam und wortlos entfaltet.

Dieser narrative Umschwung kommt so unerwartet, dass er einen nachhaltigen Eindruck hinterlässt – und macht „A Game About Digging A Hole“ zu weit mehr als nur einem minimalistischen Indie-Spiel. Es ist ein Puzzle in Zeitlupe, das mit jeder Schicht mehr von seiner wahren Identität preisgibt. Einfach nur ein Loch? Denkste.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3460111216

[h1]Spielprinzip[/h1]

Das Spielprinzip ist, wie der Titel vermuten lässt, denkbar einfach: Man gräbt ein Loch. Doch kaum hatte ich angefangen, konnte ich nicht mehr aufhören – ich habe buchstäblich jeden einzelnen Millimeter Erde abgetragen und das gesamte Loch komplett ausgehöhlt.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3460111314

Mit jedem Spatenstich verändert sich der Boden unter einem, man entdeckt verschiedene Erdschichten, Erze und stößt vielleicht sogar auf versteckte Objekte. Die Erze, die man beim Graben abbaut, können verkauft werden. Mit dem verdienten Geld lassen sich nach und nach bessere Werkzeuge, schnellere Grabgeräte oder sogar nützliche Gadgets wie Bomben und Lampen freischalten. So wird das Spielgefühl stetig erweitert – man gräbt nicht nur tiefer, sondern auch effizienter und strategischer.

Diese Simplizität macht das Spiel zu einem perfekten "Zen-Spiel", bei dem man komplett abschalten und sich auf das Hier und Jetzt konzentrieren kann. Kein Zeitdruck, kein Scheitern – nur du, die Erde und deine Schaufel.

[h1]Spielmechanik, Steuerung & Performance[/h1]

„A Game About Digging A Hole“ setzt auf eine angenehm reduzierte Steuerung, die intuitiv und schnell erlernbar ist. Graben, Sammeln, Verkaufen – alles geht flüssig von der Hand, egal ob mit Tastatur, Maus oder Controller.

Die Performance ist größtenteils stabil, selbst auf älteren Systemen. Das Spiel lädt schnell, läuft ruckelfrei und speichert den Fortschritt zuverlässig. Kleinere Bugs trüben das Erlebnis aber gelegentlich: Einzelne Erdstücke bleiben manchmal in der Luft hängen, was vor allem beim Hoch- oder Runterklettern störend sein kann – man bleibt daran hängen oder nimmt sogar leichten Fallschaden. Das passiert nicht oft, kann aber den Spielfluss beeinträchtigen.

Trotzdem bleibt das Spiel insgesamt gut spielbar und überzeugt durch seinen klaren Fokus auf das Wesentliche.

[h1]Grafik und Sound[/h1]

Die Grafik ist minimalistisch, aber liebevoll gestaltet. Die unterschiedlichen Erdschichten sind stilisiert, aber dennoch klar voneinander zu unterscheiden. Es gibt eine beruhigende Farbpalette aus erdigen Tönen, die perfekt zur meditativen Stimmung passt.

Auch der Sound folgt diesem minimalistischen Ansatz: Abgesehen vom ruhigen, atmosphärischen Soundtrack und den dezenten Grabgeräuschen bleibt das Spiel akustisch sehr zurückhaltend – und genau das wirkt. Die stille, fast schon kontemplative Klangkulisse unterstützt das entspannte Spielgefühl auf subtile Weise, ohne jemals aufdringlich zu sein.

[h1]Fazit[/h1]
[b]Minimalismus mit überraschender „Tiefe“[/b]

„A Game About Digging A Hole“ ist ein Paradebeispiel für den Reiz des Minimalismus. Es nimmt eine einfache Idee – das Graben eines Lochs – und verwandelt sie in eine beruhigende, fast meditative Spielerfahrung, die sich wohltuend von der Reizüberflutung vieler moderner Games abhebt.

Wer auf der Suche nach einem entspannten, unkonventionellen Spiel ist, das Raum für Interpretation lässt und trotzdem durchdacht wirkt, wird hier fündig. Es ist mehr als ein Spiel über ein Loch – es ist ein kleiner Rückzugsort im digitalen Alltag. Bis alles ganz anders kommt, als man glaubt.

[b]🌱 Wertung: 9/10[/b]

Here is the exact type of game that would REALLY deserve a precisely NEUTRAL rating if only it existed on Steam...
This game is not bad but it is not really good either, it somewhat relaxing but there is REALLY not much to it, and it's clearly not worth its price outside of sales, and barely worth its sales price.
But clearly, it's not bad. It's worth playing, but just barely.

Graphics: 
For a game like this, the graphics are honest and somewhat pleasant. In truth, you'll spend most time digging through soil without much items or places you'll encounter so... There is barely ... anyting in the game, so there is not that many examples on which to rate the visuals, so... It's fine, but it clearly has this generic independent game made on the unreal engine without much budget style of visual. I somehow found it pleasant. Some clipping here and there, but that's all.

Sound: There is no music, at all (except the two cutscenes at the beggining and the end) and the only sounds you'll here are the sound of your shovel/drill, the sound for getting a new rock and the birds on the surface in the garden... At least the birds sound nice and bird chirping is always relaxing...
The noise of the shovel/drill can get tiresome at some point... To the point you'll probably cut the sound.

Story : Hahaha, lol. There is barely a story, there is no dialogue, you don't know who your character is or even see them. There is a "big" twist at the end, but since it is both a bit shoehorned and a twist withint a quasi-inexistant story, who cares, really? Let's be honest, there is no story...

Gameplay : Now that's the thing we all came here for, right? Well, it's like the rest, average, just good enough to not be bad. It's like colouring drawings, it is at least relaxing. 
You click with your shovel and it makes the ground disappear bit by bit. You get stones, which are all the same except for a bit different of a visual and having more selling value. Then your inventory is filled up, or your battery is depleted, so you go back to your garage to sell your ores, pay to refill your battery and eventually (if you have enough money) upgrade one of the only four things you can upgrade:
- your total battery, so you can continue to dig for a longer time each time you go the garden.
- your inventory size so it takes longer for you to have to come back before it is filled and you have to sell all your ores.
- your jetpack that you unlock very early, very practical, but it is so basic that by the second time you update it, it's basically pointless to update it again.
- your shovel. That is the only one with a bit of a special twist to it. Updating the shovel just makes it make disappear more soil each time you click. However, the last two updates are not shovels anymore, but drills, making it so that you don't have to click each time to shovel a bit of soil, but instead you can continuously let the mouse button pressed to make the ground disappear, as if the drill was a vacuum cleaner sucking the earth. Which is very satisfying once you get there.

All the updates cost the same, and are the same. At least they are well timed and balanced, all being welcome and useful. Except the jetpack which gets it's maximum potential already by the third update, I never understood what was the difference between its third update and the higher ones.

And you also have two items you can buy or get from the rare chest in the ground: a lamp you have to stick to any surface to get you quite a lot of light (so you'll beeline the lamp along your path downward), and a dynamite that can destroy rocks which cannot be removed with your shovel. The lamps's flaw is that they can be destroyed by your shovel, so you'll likely end up destroying a lamp unwillingly; while the dynamite flaw is that its range is very short, it can hurt you, and it rolls, so you may often find yourself throwing a dynamite, escaping in panic, and then realizing it just rolled away of its pitiable range and didn't destroy the rock.

The biggest problem for me in this game's gameplay is that it is extrememely repetitive, you barely encounter any kind of special place or items, and even then they repeat themselves. And once you get to the end, you get a different gameplay in the last part of the game, that is compeltely different from what you had been doing before, but it lasts like 1 to 2 minutes at best, and is not interesting anyway.
The game is nearly exclusively composed of doing the same loop again:
- I dig
- I found ores
- My backpack is full or my battery is depleted so I have to go back to my garage.
- I sell my ores.
- I buy lamps, dynamites, or get an update; as well as replenishing my battery and health.
- Rince and repeat.

This one is probably the biggest disappointment I had the WHOLE year!

I was sold the idea of a silly game about digging a hole in the ground to uncover treasures and more but when I bought the game and tried...
I gained a mediocre grind-heavy game with zero history, zero meaning to what I am doing, hollow progression, hollow gameplay and zero fun.

Usually I like to give a proper review after some good hours of gameplay or after picking all it's achievements but this game I don't desire to play more than what I already did for testing. It is THAT bad. But still... let's point the bad parts of the game and IF have any good the goods too.

[h2] Cons [/h2]

First we have the grind. The first full hour of the game is identical with zero advances. You go click to dig, pick the ores you can, return home to sell, upgrade anything if able and repeat. I played for a WHOLE hour not having any cool progression and just farming for better tool so I could go deeper without the issue of dying from lack of energy,

Hollow world. Yes all you gonna do is dig, find ores, sell and that's it. After upgrading everything to the max (around 1 and a half hours of gameplay) you don't have ANY reason to keep farming. So going deeper and unlocking cool and more expensive ores is pointless. Finding chests also since you can just buy your stuff manually. So... what's the point of playing anymore?

Terrible Achievements. If you are like I, a person who likes stacking achievements over your account this game isn't a good choice. Not only they *seem* to be bugged since I didn't gained a single even tho I made some of the 100% sure. Still... why you ever print a achievements that is completely HARDLOCKED if you upgrade your shovel?? Literally the achievement is click 4000 times to dig but if you have a drill (the last two upgrades of the shovel) you just had to hold it to work so the achievements get locked in that session completely! You REALLY think I gonna delete my world for a new one just for the same of click 4000 times?? 

Short duration. Even IF you enjoy the game, actually don't mind the grind heavy play style. You still... have a 2 hours MAX playtime as after upgrading all to max you just keep digging till you find your main objective, win and that's it. END OF GAME. Even IF is the best game ever for you, you still only gotta enjoy it for around 2 hours till you explored ALL it's content!

[h2] Pros [/h2]

I really wanna say NONE. Cause I didn't found anything deeply interesting in this game and for me is a surprise that with SO many reviews and so many good ones how this game is so BORING. But then I read most of the comments and they are ''fake'' good reviews. Most of the good ones is actually saying the game gets boring fast or give a mid-rating like 6 or 7 out of ten. So most of the people that ''enjoyed'' it, was just barely still.

Only prompt I will give good about this game is the idea. Yes is a VERY unique game idea and they surf on that hype for sure. Cause if they named the game anything else or didn't relied on publishment on the game, it would 100% be one of those games in steam that no one knows about with less than 100 reviews with mixed results...

Also it is cheap. I guess...

[h1] Summary [/h1]

Even being super cheap (one of the few qualities of it), I still don't recommend it. It is boring and even IF you find it cool, ends way way to fast to be consider a proper cool game.

Unless it gets completely revamp, with new mechanics, better grind system and more content, I heavily suggest ignoring this game.

[h1] Motivos para cavar a Terra [/h1]
Há alguns anos, me deparei com esse título enigmático no meio de uma prateleira empoeirada nas ruas do Recife Antigo. Era um livrinho de poemas, vencedor do Prêmio Cepe, um grande prêmio de literatura e poesia. Acabei comprando e gostei do que li, principalmente de um poema sem título sobre uma mulher coveira. No livro, a autora Lilian Sais comentava, entre outras coisas, os temas pandêmicos e apocalípticos da época, elencando muitos motivos plausíveis para que se cave a terra.
Hoje, esse tema me retorna à mente, em um cenário mundial talvez ainda mais apocalíptico do que aquele no qual esses poemas foram escritos. Mas não para falar de poesia, e sim de arte em outra forma e substância.

A Game About Digging a Hole é exatamente o que o título sugere: um jogo sobre cavar um buraco. Mas não é só isso. Ele é também uma das experiências simultaneamente mais interessantes e decepcionantes que já tive com videogames. Vamos por partes.

O jogo conta a história de um personagem sem nome que compra uma casa sob a promessa de que há um baú de tesouros enterrado no quintal. Ele então investe em equipamentos pesados para realizar a exaustiva tarefa de cavar um grande buraco e encontrar esse tesouro. O loop de gameplay parte basicamente daí. No começo, nossa pá é frágil, temos pouca estamina e pouco espaço no inventário. Mas, a cada ida e vinda, vendemos os minérios coletados no quintal e usamos o dinheiro recebido para aprimorar nosso equipamento. Basicamente, repetimos esse processo algumas vezes, descendo cada vez mais e encontrando minérios mais raros.
[h2] SPOILERS A SEGUIR! [/h2]

Eu já tinha ouvido falar desse jogo, mas não sabia exatamente o que ele tinha a oferecer. Por isso, entrei nele sem esperar muita coisa. Porém, quanto mais descia buraco adentro, mais o jogo parecia esconder um mistério interessante. E fazia isso sem se denunciar como um jogo de terror. Spoiler: ele não é. Mas, nesse breve instante em que fingiu ser, ele fingiu muito bem.

O jogo não tem trilha sonora além dos sons ambientes. Quanto mais fundo se desce, menos se ouve o canto dos pássaros e mais se percebe que estamos sozinhos na escuridão silenciosa de um abismo que nós mesmos cavamos. Então surgem sons de passos, e a atmosfera vai gradualmente se tornando cada vez mais opressiva e claustrofóbica. Minas abandonadas aparecem esporadicamente, assim como objetos que parecem ter pertencido a alguém que fez essa jornada antes de nós. Tudo isso culmina em um buraco que parece descer até o infinito. Nunca tive tanto trabalho para levar um susto. Mas continuei descendo, crente que havia cavado uma passagem para o quinto dos infernos. Que a ganância havia me levado a libertar um capeta muito bem escondido sob cem metros de terra e pedra bruta. Mas fui recepcionado por um anticlimático encontro com três toupeiras gigantes que guardavam um baú vazio.

Depois de ter meu personagem devorado, o anunciante da casa postou novamente o anúncio: ela estava disponível para compra, com um tesouro enterrado.

E foi aí que o jogo se tornou decepcionante para mim — mas, em parte, pela expectativa que eu projetei. Eu quis tanto ser surpreendido, sentir uma grave e sinistra emoção de medo, que acabei cavando minha própria cova por um tempo longuíssimo. Esse sentimento ressoou em mim mais do que a temática geral do jogo. Meus poemas favoritos do livro de Lilian Sais carregam essa mesma marca residual: a de um eu-lírico que muitas vezes se trai, criando expectativas infinitas sobre o que vai encontrar debaixo da terra.

E há algo de profundamente humano nesse ato — o gesto de escavar o chão, de revirar camadas na busca por um significado oculto, por um sentido que talvez nunca esteja lá. A poesia, assim como esse simpático joguinho de não-terror, também se constrói sobre essa promessa. A de desenterrar algo de valioso sob camadas de banalidade mundana.

É fato que muitas vezes não vamos encontrar o que estamos buscando, seja na arte ou na vida, mas uma parte substancialmente farta da nossa experiência humana é justamente isso, a necessidade de continuar cavando mesmo sem garantias.
Dessa vez o jogo não prometeu nada. Eu que quis me enganar. Como diria a poetisa: cavar é uma promessa, e a gente cava sempre com medo do que encontra.

Далее мы понимаем, что выйдя на задний дворик, нам нужно вскопать землю, потому что негоже на газоне сеять свои плоды. Мы, закалённые русской деревней, дедовским советским ремнём и подъемом в 4 утра для прополки, начинаем раскапывать нашей богатырской силой эту мать землю как настоящий Илья Муромец.

Прокопав какое то время нам приходит в голову выставлять камни на авито, которые скупают асфальтоукладчики. Прокопав чуть глубже начинает появляться руда и мы заворожённые прибылью копаем всё ниже и ниже в надежде найти там то ли Саддам Хусейна, то ли мавзолей Ленина.

Обнаружив на сотне метров внизу шахты и различные чемоданы с деньгами, мы понимаем, что либо под этой землёй всё это время жили гномы бухгалтеры, либо твой друг, который забрал у тебя 50 рублей в долг ещё с 2008 года, но так и не вернул.

После ещё сотни метров начинаем находить алмазы, но никакого достижения не выскочило, поэтому они нас не интересуют и мы копаем ещё ниже, в надежде пробить бедроковое днище.

Потеряв некое количество времени, мы находим странную пещеру с мощным рычанием твоей голодной собаки пожравшей 9 раз за день вместо 10. Это оказывается стероидный крот размером с трактор дяди Максима что живёт по соседству от тебя. Наш главный герой богатырь конечно достойно себя показал раскопав столько земли, но к сожалению технику борьбы с кротами на Руси ещё не изучали. Разочаровавшись, что это не ящер(дракон), мы отправляемся чуть глубже по туннелям, ведь эти кроты слепые(нет, они зрячее чем очи дяди Максима когда он с другого конца деревни палит в окно переодевающуюся за домом тётю Нюру).

И вот, мы прошли к нашей последней комнате, в которой веет мраком, богатством, а также потом и кровью(от вас). Вы отчаянно открываете сундук и понимаете, что на самом деле, внутри было целое НИЧЕГО!

Обернувшись назад вы замечаете нашего любимого Крота-Горыныча и, совершив славянский зажим яицами, побеждаете его, после чего вы со словами "Кладмен мyдaк" выбираетесь наружу. Дальше вы жили в доме за 800к долго и счастливо. Конец!

Okay, listen, I don’t know what kind of black magic they’ve used to make 'a game about digging a hole' so addictive, but here we are. You start with basically some sh*te tools and the dream of digging to the center of the Earth. The materials are limited, the upgrades are slow, but every time you dig a little deeper, you just KNOW that better tools are waiting for you.

The surprises at the bottom? OH, there are surprises. I won’t spoil it, but let’s just say when you hit rock bottom, things get... interesting.

Could it have been more? Sure, there’s room for more but it’s just enough to make digging a hole way more fun than it has any right to be.

So yeah, would I recommend this game? Absolutely. It’s simple, it’s satisfying, and it makes you feel like a professional digger. Yes. Just yes.

[h3]Симулятор прочистки трубы[/h3]

В целом, я доволен игрой. Условно в ней нету нечего примечательного, её спокойно можно пройти +\- за 30 минут (Даже достижение такое есть) сюжета как такого нет, это достаточно медитативная игра на подобии многих других, ты просто капаешь туннель и всё, нечего серьёзного. Хочу подчеркнуть несколько плюсов и минусов в этой игре.

[b]Плюсы[/b]
 - Игра спокойная, не дергает и не отвлекает
 - Игра линейная, тебе не куда спешить и никто тебя не торопит 
 - Есть система прокачки
 - Имеется небольшое количество достижений, уже приятно
 
[b]Минусы[/b]
 - Отсутствует музыка, крайне не хватает 
 - Отсутствует автосохранение
 - Игра слишком короткая
 - Развитие происходит слишком быстро

[b]Как можно игру улучшить[/b]
 - Введение уровня сложности (В зависимости от уровня сложности глубина туннеля будет больше а породы всё глубже будут крепче)
 - Введение дополнительной ветки навыков
 - Возможность расширения территории, когда копать предстоит не только вниз, но и по бокам
 - Добавление большого количество предметов которые облегчат работу (Например усиление на бур/Временная бесконечная энергия и подобное)
 - Кооп (Сомнительно, но почему бы и нет?)
 - Ввести больше достижений
 - Добавить бесконечный режим который позволяет воспользоваться транспортом на подобии полноразмерного бура 

Если подвести итоги, игрой я остался доволен и получил эстетическое удовольствие после очистки туннеля от всей земли, игре ставлю твёрдную восьмерку из десяти, она ещё сырая, в ней мало гемплея, и на текущий момент представляет из себя обычную медитативную дрочилку которая может понравится не каждому, каким-то серьёзным проектом назвать её пока тяжело, но думаю, разработчики нас ещё удивят. Рекомендую к покупке!

Are you digging for a secret buried treasure? Are you digging to appease your Dwarf genes? Are you digging because you're bored or need to relax? Are you digging because you want to buy a sweet jetpack that makes no sense existing?

A cheap game with a weird premise is a shortcut into my Steam library. I'm always looking forward to checking out something that might not be like anything I've played before. Sometimes it turns out incredible, and other times, it just doesn't quite live up to my expectations. Not because it's terrible, but sometimes you just want a little more. This is one of those games.

Abbreviated Review: https://youtu.be/T5_4XE3Y5Mo

[h1]A Game About[/h1]
A Game About Digging A Hole is exactly what it says in the title. Your singular goal is to dig a hole as deep and as fast as possible in your backyard. After finding a listing for an exceptionally affordable house with the promise of treasure buried under the lawn, that's where you'll ultimately be breaking ground. You'll take on this task with some kind of battery-powered shovel – or I suppose a trowel at first – that you'll use to take chunks out of the earth that disappear into the ether. You won't make much progress at first, and your tiny crater will only reveal a handful of rocks.

The rocks and other materials you find are a commodity that you can take back to your little homebase shed and immediately sell for cash. Cash that you can use to purchase upgrades for the tools you need to dig further and faster. You can increase the size of your shovel, the battery that mysteriously powers it, the battery-powered jetpack you ultimately need to get out of your hole, and the inventory that contains the stuff you find. As well as recharging your battery and healing any health lost falling in the hole like an idiot.

This is essentially the entire gameplay loop. Digging with progressively more capability to grab and return the rocks and minerals you find to purchase upgrades and refresh your digging power. You'll also be able to obtain key consumables like dynamite used to break through (entirely obliterate) bedrock and lights to make it so you can actually see what you're doing.

[h1]Digging A Hole[/h1]
What you're doing in this hole-digging adventure is a bit more than just digging a hole, but not much more. The bulk of the game is making your way ever deeper, bursting into caverns giving you a bit more depth, and widening your perspective on your underground journey. As you carve your path, you'll occasionally have a sort of radar tracker pop-up that directs you to a certain area within the soil. Digging toward that will eventually reveal a secret, whether a suitcase of cash and tools or a special stabilized "mineshaft" area that contains a chest – which also has cash and tools in it. There are also hidden keys you can find to open a mysterious locked chest in your homebase shed for a pretty mediocre reward.

The one to two hours you'll most likely spend doing this has that classic cathartic feel to it that sits somewhere between Minecraft and Powerwash Simulator. It's a game where practically every action you take is progress toward the end. The problem is that the end comes pretty quickly, it's not particularly interesting or surprising, and the journey to it doesn't offer much variety.

Strange little games like this thrive on twists and turns. Being surprised by the outcome or discovering little mysteries along the way is often the best part. Games like Inscryption and Is This Game Trying to Kill Me give you relatively simple enjoyable gameplay, but also constantly leave breadcrumbs indicating something more is going on than what is on the surface. That isn't in this game, and it feels like it should be. You still have a game that's reasonably rewarding to play and worth recommending on that alone, but one that feels like it was one ambitious writer away from being exceptional.

A Game About Digging A Hole — крайне залипательная игра, где вам предстоит копать, копать и ещё раз копать, чтобы отыскать обещанное сокровище, спрятанное глубоко под землёй. Процесс крайне увлекает, а под конец игра неожиданно приобретает нотку хоррора, что удивляет и создаёт неплохую тревожную атмосферу, когда вы оказываетесь очень глубоко и понимаете, что под землёй есть что-то страшное и опасное.

Завязка тут следующая: протагонист замечает рекламу дома, который стоит подозрительно дёшево. На листовке указано, что на заднем дворе где-то глубоко под землёй спрятан клад, найдя который можно неплохо разбогатеть. Он быстро покупает недвижимость и начинает копать. Как такового сюжета тут почти нет, но чем ближе вы к развязке, тем сильнее игра приобретает хоррорную составляющую. Это может не всем понравиться, но мне лично финал очень зашёл.

Игровой процесс очень прост в освоении, и весь проект можно пройти буквально за час, может чуть больше или меньше, в зависимости от вашей любопытности и усердия. Неподалёку от ямы у вас есть гараж, где можно пополнить запас батареи (лопата тут электрическая), продать найденные вещи (в основном камни; чем глубже копаете, тем более редкие минералы, алмазы и прочее находите), а также купить лампочки для освещения пути и динамит, который может быстренько расчистить небольшую область.

Собственно, поначалу всё начинается довольно медленно: вы находите камни, стоят они копейки, поэтому вы снова копаете, заряжаете лопату, и так по кругу, пока не начнёте находить более дорогие минералы. Потом, заполучив побольше денег, вы прокачиваете свою лопату, вместимость инвентаря и джетпак (он обязателен и поможет быстро возвращаться в гараж для подзарядки и продажи). Чем глубже вы пробираетесь, тем чаще можете поймать сигнал, который приведёт вас к мини-сокровищу с полезными предметами и небольшой суммой денег.

Собственно, в этом простом цикле и заключается вся "залипательность" проекта. Игра спокойная, медитативная: вы методично прокачиваете свои инструменты, исследуете недра в поисках интересных вещей для продажи и постепенно опускаетесь всё ниже и ниже, к заветному сокровищу. После первого прохождения открывается режим, где становятся доступны достижения, и повозиться в этой короткой песочнице ещё немного весьма весело, тем более что ачивки простые и не требуют особых усилий.

Если вы любите проекты с простым, понятным геймплеем, где нужно прокачивать свои инструменты, копаться в небольшой песочнице и в конце найти сокровище, — то A Game About Digging A Hole точно вам подойдёт, тем более игра стоит недорого.

This game put me into a zen-like trance that I haven't felt in a long time. It tickled a part of my lizard brain that very rarely gets activated by games. I sat in silence for about 20 minutes at the start just digging and then returning and selling my ores before I realised my wife was sitting on the other side of the couch also staring at the telly completely transfixed by what was going on in the back garden of my new house.

I don't know how they did it, but this game makes me feel like the meth-heads from that episode of Breaking Bad where Jesse starts digging and they just follow along and he can rob their house while they have their head down the hole, digging, because they don't know ''how far it is''. 

What ''[i]it[/i]'' is wasn't important in Breaking Bad and isn't important here. This is a game about the journey and making a hole progressively bigger and bigger, the mystery of what [i]else[/i] might be buried in the garden, and the weird and inherent satisfaction that comes with it.

Best 5€ I've spent on a game in a long time. I might go buy a shovel today.

To anyone on the fence, here's my recommendation:

Step 1: Take a coin from your pocket.
Step 2: Spend five minutes observing all the little details, marks, blemishes, etc. on it.
Step 3: Flip the coin. Doesn't matter what side you get.
Step 4: Put the coin back in your pocket.

Congratulations. You've now had a more thrilling, joy-filled experience than this game could ever provide you without wasting your money, time or disk space.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

[b][H1]A Game About Digging A Hole[/H1][/b]

[b][H2]SINOPSIS[/H2][/b]

Compramos una casa y nuestro objetivo será excavar un agujero en el jardín, gracias a nuestra pala, sin saber a donde nos llevará nuestra exploración.

[b][H2]JUGABILIDAD[/H2][/b]

Estamos ante un juego de exploración corto pero que vicia por sus mecánicas. Tendremos que cavar un hoyo en nuestro jardín con la ayuda de nuestra pala. A medida que vamos cavando podremos ir teniendo mejoras: Nuestra pala, la duración de la batería, la cantidad de piedras que podremos llevar, comprar un jetpack y mejorarlo, comprar luces para ver las zonas mas oscuras de nuestro hoyo y incluso comprar dinamita. 
El dinero lo conseguiremos gracias a vender las piedras que vamos encontrando. Contra más abajo del hoyo, las piedras tendrán más valor. También encontraremos tesoros gracias a nuestro radar.

[b][H2]APARTADO TECNICO[/H2][/b]

Con una estética bonita y una interfaz muy sencilla. Cumple como juego simple de exploración / minería. No vamos a encontrar unos gráficos extremadamente buenos, realmente no le hace falta. [b]A Game About Digging A Hole[/b] farda de costar lo mismo que un ☕ café.
Su apartado sonoro cumple, con sonidos también bastante simples pero realistas.

[b][u]PROS[/u][/b]
🟢Buen precio
🟢Mecánicas interesantes

[b][u]CONTRAS[/u][/b]
🔴La historia no me acaba de convencer
🔴Muy corto
🔴[spoiler]Los logros se activan una vez que completas el juego[/spoiler]

[b][H2]VALORACION[/H2][/b]

Esperaba más. Sobre todo en su final. Sinceramente pienso que le podrían haber sacado muchísimo más partido y rejugabilidad al juego. Es una pena, el juego como tal engancha. Sus mecánicas me parecen interesantes y lo recomendaría a pesar de su duración. 
Quizás en un futuro vengan actualizaciones y tenga que cambiar el final de esta reseña :)

Затягивающая игра на час-полтора с незамысловатым на первый взгляд сюжетом. В игре вам предстоит копать(в соответствии с 19й статьёй "О недрах" в РФ копать глубже 5м. запрещено), выкапывать полезные ископаемые, продавать их и улучшать свой инструмент, чтобы найти похороненный под землёй данного земельного участка клад. Как только вы находите клад, игра пройдена.
!ДАЛЬШЕ СПОЙЛЕР! 
В игру заложен философский смысл, по сюжету главный герой покупает дом за 10к грязных зеленых бумажек и под землёй ему обещают клад. В безумном желании отыскать сокровище главный герой роет землю, находит ближе к концу игры золото, платину, алмазы и просто продав их он может получить сумму кратно большую чем он потратил. По-сути цель легкого (относительно) обогащения достигается не благодаря нахождению некого клада, который якобы зарыт здесь. Но главный герой, одержимый иллюзорным сокровищем, не замечая своё счастье, продолжает поиски. И действительно, в какой то момент натыкается на подземное сооружение, не сложно догадаться что вот тут то и находится клад. Попасть внутрь можно только упав внутрь и выбраться оттуда уже не получится, а из глубины мрачного подземелья слышен рёв неизвестного существа. Здесь герой встаёт перед выбором: идти до конца в неизвестность или остаться с тем что имеет теперь. Точка невозврата пройдена и оказавшись внутри герой сталкивается с огромными кротами, которые пытаются его убить, не остается ничего, кроме как бежать. Сбежав от трёх кротов герой всё же добегает до зала с большим сундуком и предвкушая богатства, которые человек не способен даже представить, главный герой открывает сундук... в нём нет абсолюно ничего. Let's dig into "A Game About Digging a Hole." This isn't some epic, sprawling adventure; it's a focused, minimalist experience about exactly what the title says: digging a hole. And somehow, it's weirdly captivating. For $4.99 ($4.49 during the Spring sale), you get a solid couple of hours of digging, upgrading, and uncovering a secret. I even went back for a second dig, which, in my gaming library, is high praise. It's simple, repetitive, yes, but the gameplay loop is oddly satisfying, like a digital fidget spinner that actually gives you progress.

[b]Check this one out if you are:[/b]
[list]
[*]Autistic
[*]Like incremental progress and upgrade systems.
[*]Looking for a short, satisfying experience to unwind with.
[*]Introverted
[/list]
[b]Skip if you:[/b]
[list]
[*]Are a dopamine fiend
[*]Dislike repetitive tasks
[*]Expecting a long, in-depth experience
[*]Need AAA graphics and a complex narrative
[/list]
Basically, "A Game About Digging a Hole" is a surprisingly addictive little gem. It's not going to revolutionize gaming, but it's a perfect way to spend a couple of hours if you're looking for something simple, satisfying, and a little bit weird. If you're okay with repetitive gameplay and have some nagging curiosity, grab your shovel and start digging.

A Game About Digging a Hole é um jogo singleplayer com o único objetivo de cavar um buraco, o jogo se inicia com o seu personagem comprando uma casa que promete um báu do tesouro enterrado nas profundezas do seu quintal, junto com a casa você ganha a Super Mega Digger 3000 Ultimate 2.0 e um Detector-Set, que o ajudarão nessa jornada inesquecível, cave fundo, encontre minérios, melhore os seus equipamentos, volte, pegue mais minérios raros, e quanto você menos esperar, o buraquinho que você imaginou ser pequeno já esta um belo de uma descida pro núcleo da Terra.

PREÇO -> BARATO
DURAÇÃO -> CURTA (2hrs)
REQUISITOS -> COMPUTADOR SIMPLES

Впринципе неплохо, но коротко - первое прохождение заняло как пишет игра 106 минут (Неожиданно, но у игры даже ачивка есть где нужно пройти игру за менее 30 минут). Прокачки на самом деле маловато, после фулла всеравно хочется чтобы бур был более мощным к примеру. Чисто за половину игры (за час) ты уже весь прокачан что по итогу деньги копятся разве что пополнять здоровье/энергию и закупаться динамитами чтобы раскидываться ими по приколу (Накопил 47к мани, прошел игру, начал новую игру и вышел) Вот если бы была такая штука, что после каждой новой игры открывались бонусы в прокачке, чтобы с каждым НГ ты становился той еще машиной, то было бы интереснее перепроходить игру. Но по итогу после прохождения открываются как я понял только достижения и всё. Надеюсь будут какие нибуть обновления которые добавят больше контента и сделают игру куда интересней.

Итог: 6 из 10, очень коротко, контента мало, но зато расслабляющая. Рекомендую так чисто попробывать на вечер)

Honestly, it's a near perfect game. Dig, find ore, sell ore, buy better shovel. Repeat. I would say my issues are balancing, and some physics.

You basically get all your gear upgraded to full in no time, meaning everything after that point in the game, which is very early, maybe an hour or two, is completely pointless since there's nothing to work for.

Physics are essentially non-existent. You can dig a floating island if you want. It's weird, but that's not my complaint. My complaint is the near microscopic floating islands you create all over the place as you dig down. I often find myself tempted to leap into my chasm and activate my jetpack at the last second, but I have nearly killed myself while doing this countless times as I land on one of these microscopic floating islands.

My solution? Remove all collision for objects smaller than the size of an ore. As far as balancing, I'd say make upgrades cost more, and/or double the amount of upgrades a player can buy. If you make them a quarter as impactful towards progress, and double the cost, it would give the game a LOT more playability.

It's great overall though, these complaints are detailed because there's nothing else to complain about!

A Game About Digging a Hole – Proste, ale Wciągające Kopanie

Ocena: 8.5/10

Opis:
"A Game About Digging a Hole" to zaskakująco relaksująca i satysfakcjonująca gra, w której głównym celem jest... kopanie dziury. Brzmi absurdalnie? Być może, ale w praktyce to niezwykle wciągające doświadczenie, które trudno odłożyć na bok. Gracz zaczyna z podstawową łopatą i stopniowo ulepsza swoje narzędzia, odkrywając przy tym różnorodne warstwy ziemi, skarby oraz sekrety ukryte głęboko pod powierzchnią.

Co jest na plus?
✅ Satysfakcjonująca mechanika – kopanie i ulepszanie sprzętu daje mnóstwo frajdy.
✅ Minimalistyczna, ale przyjemna oprawa graficzna – voxelowy styl pasuje do rozgrywki.
✅ Relaksująca atmosfera – dźwięki otoczenia i powolny progres sprawiają, że gra świetnie sprawdza się jako odprężające doświadczenie.
✅ Zaskakująco uzależniająca – "jeszcze jedno kopnięcie łopatą" szybko zamienia się w godziny rozgrywki.

Co mogłoby być lepsze?
❌ Brak większej różnorodności – mimo satysfakcjonującego kopania, po pewnym czasie gameplay może stać się monotonny.
❌ Mało wyzwań – gra nie stawia przed graczem żadnych większych celów poza samym kopaniem, co może niektórych zniechęcić.

Podsumowując, "A Game About Digging a Hole" to dowód na to, że nawet najprostsze pomysły mogą przynieść masę frajdy. Jeśli lubisz gry nastawione na spokojną, ale satysfakcjonującą eksplorację, to ten tytuł może cię pozytywnie zaskoczyć. 🚀

[h1] Преимущества: Залипательная, простая, интуитивно понятная [/h1]
[h1] Недостатки: Слишком короткая [/h1]

Начнем с самого заметного плюса — это стоимость игры. Думаю, отдать 200 рублей за приятное времяпрепровождение может позволить себе каждый.

Графика в игре простая и немного размыленная. Со временем на неё перестаешь обращать внимание. Да и сама игра не направлена на выдающуюся графику, а скорее на расслабляющее провождение времени. Звук копания может немного надоедать, но если включить музыку, это не создаст никаких проблем :)

Игра представляет собой симулятор копателя. Сначала кажется, что это будет похоже на Майнкрафт, но приятно, что здесь не нужно копать блоками. В начале процесс немного затянутый: чтобы выполнить одно действие, нужно постоянно нажимать кнопку мыши, так что просто зажать её и копать непрерывно не получится. Это придаёт игре атмосферу типичного кликера.

В игре доступна система прокачки различного оборудования, что позволяет добывать более ценные ресурсы из недр Земли. Но есть и недостаток — сама система улучшений не такая обширная, и вскоре добытые средства некуда будет вкладывать, так как все деньги уходят на расходные материалы.

Удивительно, но у игры есть даже сюжет. С самого старта у тебя есть определенная цель — поиски клада! А что ещё можно искать под землёй? На удивление, в конце появляется враг — [spoiler] кроты! [/spoiler]

Однако еще одним недостатком является то, что игра слишком короткая. Первое неспешное прохождение заняло около двух с половиной часов. Хотя после завершения открываются достижения, они не влияют на саму игру. Все достижения можно собрать за дополнительные пару часов.

Игра выглядит недоработанной, в ней чего-то явно не хватает. Может, стоило бы добавить многопользовательский режим, где можно соревноваться с друзьями в том, кто быстрее доберется до финала? Или реализовать песочницу с возможностью улучшения своего жилища и более продвинутой системой прокачки. Даже возможность переезда в новое место была бы интересной добавкой. Упрощенная возможность начать игру заново не делает её привлекательной в долгосрочной перспективе.

Ohne Zeitdruck geht es ins Loch, Erze raus, in die Garage in Geld umwandeln, Schaufel und Co. entwickeln. Und wieder ins Loch und wieder raus... und wieder...und wieder. In die Spielphysik und dem Entwicklungsbaum muss man sich nahezu gar nicht Einarbeiten und das Spiel fordert das Gehirn kognitiv maximal im Ruhemodus. Wer einen entspannten Nachmittag Zeit hat und sich die Zeit mit dem Urtrieb zu Buddeln und zu Finden verbringen möchte: "A Game About Digging A Hole" ist der perfekte Titel dafür. Dynamit, Lampen, Schaufel - los geht´s. Entspannendes Spiel für 4,49 Euro im Steam-Sale. Überraschend schöner Titel - Klare Kaufempfehlung!

My wife loves to dig in games.  I introduced her to 7 Days to Die and she spent a ton of time digging trenches around our base like she was in Europe fighting in 1915.  I saw this and thought "5 bucks, sure why not."

She downloaded it and started playing.   After a little bit I bought a copy for myself and played as well.

This is a cheesy little game about digging and selling ore and "finding the treasure".  It was awesome, cheap entertainment for the $5.  I kept me occupied for hours.  It doesnt have a lot of "continued playability" when you finish unless you wish to get all the achievements or try to see how much ore you can dig up but dont let that deter you.  I hope they add more to it later but even if they dont so be it.  I enjoyed it.  I literally laughed myself stupid when I got to the very end scene.  

Would I suggest this?  If you enjoy a wide range of game play then YES.  If all you enjoy playing is COD or RUST and such then it isnt for you.  Again, for $5 it is well worth its value.  I hope the developers sell a million copies or better.  Nice job.

It is also family friendly so if you want something you wont worry about your kids playing then go for it.

Also, dont ruin the experience by watching a playthrough.  Spoilers will definately spoil the experience.

Cookie Clicker-like progression surrounded by the urge to remove all the material like in Minecraft. Great timekiller, very satisfying to play. Main game length about 90 minutes, but has some replay value, or can just be soothing if you like that sort of thing.

You know going into its a dumb game meant for only a few hours of fun. But at $5 its still overpriced. There is an achievement for beating it under 30 minutes, so worst case youve got 30 minutes of play time. No replay value either unfortunately, as starting a new game gives the exact same gameplay experience, but with trophies, half of which youll probably unlock based on stats from your first playthrough. The digging system is ok, but it leaves little pieces of ground floating in midair so if you miss it you might not be able to get it later since it only digs on 'valid' digging spots, of which the air is not one. Then you try to go into the hole and get stuck on those little pieces. Additionally controllers mostly work, but youre gonna want to set up a custom controller profile to avoid stick drift. I assume this is the devs first game so good for them, but it should have been free or maybe a dollar or something. Maybe an update will come with more to find underground or maybe different upgrade paths or something. idk. If an update does come itll probably be a $5 DLC lol. Also the endgame is a stealth game not a digging game so beware. Personally I hate stealth. This game had potential to be like powerwash simulator, a meaningless game that lets you unwind while doing a pointless repetitive task, but instead i just cant help but feel I didnt get my $5 worth.

A Game About Digging A Hole – Too Short to Be Worthwhile

This could have been a fun time-waster, but it's over way too quickly.

In just about 30 minutes, I maxed out every upgrade (Shovel, Inventory, Battery, and Jet Pack). The early progression feels great as you go from barely being able to dig to efficiently mining deeper. But once you've upgraded everything, there's little left to do beyond collecting the same few ores and hitting the game's very odd and blunt ending.

Hidden treasures don’t feel rewarding, either. They mostly offer small cash prizes that are less than the ores you just sold on the journey just to get to them. The additional rewards (lights and dynamite) aren’t particularly exciting either, since you’ll likely have plenty already. The dynamite also bounces unpredictably, making it frustrating to use throughout your adventure.

With better balance, more content to discover, and a wider variety of tools, this game could be much better. As it stands, it’s just too short-lived to recommend.

Мой путь познания данной игры с моей точки зрения начался с... копания небольшой ямки. И совершения ошибок. 

Разберём стандартный путь прохождения. Энергии аккумулятора не хватало выбраться или не покупал мощный реактивный ранец. Советую больше ходить продавать ресурсы и сильно не задерживаться в глубине удлиняющегося туннеля. Также обратите внимание на крестик и когда появится радар - не зевайте. И это не единственный клад, как я узнал из расширенного пути, о нём позже. В основном качал до бура и желательно докопаться до алмазов. Не раз умирал от кротов из-за незнания их паттернов. Приловчиться можно, советую бежать вправо (потом поймёте, о чём я, а кто знает тот знает). 

Разберём расширенный путь прохождения. То есть мазохизм в чистом виде. Не нужно копать сначала поверхность земли и выкапывать кучу камней и угля. Нужно копаться как можно глубже, к алмазам, ради денег для прокачки оборудования. Эта роковая ошибка стоила мне переигровки на осознании в половине пути, где уже три часа мучался. В конце скажу, сколько я потратил времени и вывешу свою статистику (да-да). Предупреждаю, перфекционисты будут страдать из-за малюсеньких остатков земли. Дима не зря отметил то, что нет гравитации, жутко бесят эти остатки. Не столь бесят застрявшие минералы в белых глыбах. Раскапывал за забором и под домом тоже. Использовал кучу ламп, нашёл ключи на -15 высоте вроде. 

Если вы готовы бросить вызов своим нервам и собственному свободному времени - осталось рассказать о статистике. Её я вёл на протяжении всех раскопок. С полуночи до четырёх утра, а также сегодня, в одиннадцать часов утра часок. То есть да, опускался и поднимался для подхода к обмену минералов на деньги для детального подсчета. Очень выматывало, потому слушал на фоне гениальный альбом ANTIHYPETRAIN, длительностью 6:11:48. В общем и целом, данный опыт прохождения мне понравился. Пробовать себя в этом или нет - решать вам. Осталось устроить спидран, последнее достижение.

A Game About Digging a Hole (GAD) is a game where strangely enough you dig a hole. There isn’t a strong narrative to start with, so you get to digging after a couple minute long intro scene. GAD becomes a mix between Minecraft, and a sort of House Flipper-esque game as your hole increases in size, so do your tools and speed in which you can dig (or “Vacuum” the dirt….). 

To start with the negatives, for me the biggest drawbacks were the dirt physics and the ending. 
In regards to the dirt physics, traversing your hole becomes an annoying challenge as tiny bits of dirt will forever remain floating in the air until you move your cursor over the pixel-wide space and dig them up. I wouldn’t care about this too much except for you being body-blocked by every single one of these floating pea-sized dirtballs. Literally jumped to fall long enough to get an achievement and died by landing on a floating dirt pea. 
As for the ending…I wouldn’t recommend reading this unless you already beat the game, it's best to go into GAD blind… [spoiler] I don’t really care about the treasure being empty, I had enough fun just digging the damn hole. What annoyed me was how the ending trek devolves into one of my most hated mechanics: the “Amnesia style horror mechanic”. For some odd reason, as soon as I enter the giant mole cave I can no longer use dynamite, drill or even a jetpack! Nope, just gotta run from them. 
[/spoiler] So to summarize my disdain towards the end, I am just not a fan of you working throughout the game to build up your items, only to make them all useless for the final challenge. 

As for the positives about the game, I enjoyed the digging progression and the feeling itself of digging a hole. 
The progression is fairly typical - you get ore and sell it to get better. While simple, I do enjoy the feeling of a tangible increase in “Power” as your tiny little spade evolves into a dirt-destroying vacuum monster. 
As for the digging itself, I found it almost cathartic. Best way I can describe it is something like House Flipper or Crime Scene Cleaner where you're focused on just using your tools to alter the environment. I spent way more time than I needed to just playing around with the darn size of the hole - making it bigger, easier to progress, trying to get light in, ect. 

Overall, GAD is a good example of a game where it’s more about the journey and not the destination. It has some fun concepts, it's cheap as heck, and while I didn’t enjoy the conclusion, I do think it's worth a playthrough.

Я только что завершил игру "A Game About Digging A Hole", и у меня остались исключительно положительные впечатления!
С самого начала игра погружает в уникальную атмосферу, где простота концепции – копать яму – оказывается удивительно захватывающей. Графика минималистична, но стильна, что позволяет сосредоточиться на игровом процессе. Каждый уровень предлагает новые механики и задачи, что делает игру разнообразной и интересной.
Особенно понравилась возможность исследовать подземный мир и находить забавные секреты. Музыка и звуковые эффекты создают отличное настроение и подчеркивают атмосферу приключения.
Игра также отлично подходит для расслабления, ведь ее можно проходить в своем темпе, не спеша.
В общем, это отличный способ провести время и насладиться простым, но увлекательным игровым процессом. Обязательно попробуйте! Однако концовка расстроила)
Обязательно нужно фиксить баг с маленькими кусками земли, об которые ударяешься и застреваешь.

[h1] Diggy Diggy Hole [/h1]

Imagine working on a indi game with a bunch of devs and artist. Imagine you send one of those on a well deserved 14 days vacation. Only for them to return and hand you a game about digging a hole. That alone speaks work of how well the workload must be managed within this peticular studio. 

What feels like a joke acutally plays out decently. The game is about digging. You see an advertisment for a house with garden where gold is buried so go grab your trusty shovel and start digging. The loop is simple. Dig down, find ores, return ores for money, spend money on upgrades an refills and return digging again. While a small inventory and low battery capacity will bring you up to the surface more often, in later stages of the game you spend some minutes in the land down under. While digging you can discover some secrets with additional loot. Some tools you carry with help discover those treasures. 

The game is easily beaten within an hour for the first time. It has an ending. Some liked it and some dont. While the story may not be the strongest pillar of this game its decent enough to give everythin a little context. After you beaten the game for the first time you may hunt additional achievements. I am not sure wether this practice is nice. Since it may lead to an overstayed welcome from the game. Afterall the game is entertaining for the reminder of the joke it tells.

There are some frustrating parts i found myself bumping into. First it can happen that you get floating small pieces of dirt that still have a hit box. This either leads to curtain death when falling onto a small pixel sized dirt blob or you can make yourself stuck with the need to look arround really carefully. If you wanna dig quick in some direction to gather some secrets this may lead to some frustration if it happens serveral times within a run. 

Secondly the game has no return to menu button. If done some smaller runs for achievements exspecially the speedrun one and its annoying to close the game and restart it all the time you wanna reset your garden. 

Thirdly and finally the wasted potential. Its a bit more complicated. The game never promised endless fun. The whole storepage scream fun as long as it takes to sip a coffee for the price of a coffee. The content present matches the length of the game. Still afterall there is this little something that screams more. While its not in dire need to be expaned the idea allows for more diggable depth, more upgrades, maybe even additional gadgets or longer side tunnels and layers to be discovers. The game surely does everything right not to be to long. But at the same times this means sacrafized potential. Luckly in modern days this means perhaps for a second part or some other fans to pick the idea and make there own game. 

At the very end what I wanna say is this. The game is fun. For what it offers. Dont go in and accspect a deep well branchend simulator. Take it in more as the here I have a little joke I wanna tell yeah and will laugh for an hour or maybe more.
