At first, this game was pretty enjoyable. A neat concept! A great way of managing resources. A bit rough around the edges, but sometimes that makes the best games. I kept continuing on, and I had a lot of fun, but I had a feeling something else was coming. I was excited as I went through typical progression - items you harvest get more valuable, so each trip you end up with more and more cash that allows you to upgrade to the moon.... And then I got to that something else. Spoilers ahead, spoiler free TLDR below it!

[spoiler] It all came to the bottom of the hole, which lead to... Another hole! I paused at the weird breathing... I guess this was the horror game tag part. That's fine, I just had to get my brain to switch from relaxed simulator adventure to horror. And to my horror, every single item I had worked on upgrading suddenly was useless! No using my drill, jetpack, or large number of explosives. Gasp, it's giant moles! Makes enough sense. But for moles, they certainly have amazing vision. For some reason, you can just outrun them. It's a shame that I couldn't change it to an easier binding on my controller; you don't get to change those. But after having to look up that you just really need to run through the sections, I come across the fabled treasure, open it and... Nothing! I turn around and am promptly killed. I then am informed that if I want to try to get achievements, I need to reset my save and do this all again. I love 100%ing games! I will not be doing that for this game. I was at least relieved to see the achievements I fulfilled (without knowing) were given to me, but also, there's no way I'm trying to speedrun this game that starts off extremely slow. It was so frustrating to play through this game, actually enjoy it, and then have that all taken away by disappointment that could have been solved by simply having a hole with a few extra things in it. [/spoiler]

Pros: 
- Fun gameplay, enjoyable progression system
- Cute graphics

Cons: 
- Unsatisfying, especially the ending
- Terrible Achievement system
- Lack of keybinding customization
- The horror tag should be removed. And the content that caused there to be a horror tag. Play an actual horror game if you want that aspect.
- Limited progression system, when you get to that ceiling, money gets *too* plentiful.

For the price, it's... Fine. However, I feel the game needs a large overhaul before I could see myself going back to it. I also wanted to be thorough because this has become a viral game, and I feel that people should get what they're going into, even if it's a cheap game.

Cute little game. If you enjoy monotonous task games like Power Wash you will enjoy this. I was able to 100% it without guides in under 5 hours (and that was with taking my time in the first run) so it isn't a very lengthy game. 
There are a couple cons that I'll list now:

It became a big headache multiple times where a single speck of dirt would be floating in the air, causing you to run into it. Sometimes it's almost as small as a pixel but still enough to completely body block you. Died once because I couldn't fly up out of the hole and couldn't figure out why until coming back and landing on the tiny speck in the middle of the hole. At a certain point, loose dirt should just auto break to avoid this.

There was a constant visual glitch throughout the whole playthrough (and playthroughs I saw online of big creators) where the dirt, usually where your hole is, gets glitchy for a second before going back to normal.

Having achievements not unlock until your second playthrough, even preventing you from seeing how much progress you have towards it, is very anti fun and anti consumer. Just felt like a way to make me waste my time. 

Dynamite is very frustrating. It bounces like crazy so you have to be super careful about where you throw it as to avoid wasting your money and then it just feels extremely weak for the price as well. Late game I bought 100 just to mess around and spam throw them, expecting huge destruction. The results were depressingly boring and minimal lol. But really, just having a "place" button with the dynamite like there is with the lights would solve the entire main issue. Unless the desire is to make dynamite frustratingly bouncy and inconsistent.

This one is more person to person, but this is legit an arthritis simulator. Especially if you go for the 100% in one sitting (which again, is only like 3-6 hours depending on how quickly you move so not anything crazy for one session). Just putting this here as a warning rather than a critique. You have to click your mouse so frequently that I ended up having to switch fingers and then even switch hands a few times lol.

The last two points are just personal preference/wants rather than cons (spoilers):

I wish there were "fun" things to unlock or do. This just seems like the perfect type of game to add zany upgrades. Opening the garage chest gets you two special items. An upgrade to dynamite and a teleporter that teleports you back to the surface. The dynamite I thought was going to be a much bigger explosion. But the upgrade is barely noticeable. And the teleporter being a one time use was very depressing too. It takes so much diggiing to get both keys. To the point that on my first run where I spent around 2.5 hours playing, I didn't even know there were keys. I only learned there were keys because I watched Markiplier play it after I beat it the first time lol. So I just feel like the chest should be more fun/powerful. Sure someone might run across both keys on their first playthrough right away and make the game too easy. I dunno. Just underwhelming lol.

Lastly, I wish the moles were more interesting? I was just hoping for something scarier when I got down there rather than 3 moles that walk back and forth and then chase you and lose interest easily if you run for a couple seconds. This game was PERFECT for some Lovecraftian horror or Junji Ito type stuff. Even if it wasn't super horror heavy, playing into it would elevate it a ton imo. Maybe a second "scary mode" so that people who don't like horror can still enjoy the base version with the moles.

Anyway, fun game. I enjoyed my time with it.

[h1]Я копал. И я не должен был этого делать.[/h1]

[i]Дом был дешевым. Слишком дешевым.[/i]

Риэлтор нервно теребил галстук, когда я подписывал бумаги. "Прекрасный сад", сказал он. "Большие перспективы". Я не слушал.

На третий день я нашел лопату. На пятый – начал копать.

[h2]Первая земля, первое безумие[/h2]

Сначала это казалось терапией. Я вытягивал из земли камни, мусор, старые монеты. Продавал их за гроши, покупал новые инструменты.

Но с каждым ударом лопаты земля становилась [i]страннее[/i]. Я наткнулся на кости. Они были слишком большими, чтобы быть птичьими.

Я продолжал.

[h2]Глубина.[/h2]

Я вырыл яму глубже моего роста. Потом глубже дерева во дворе. Потом глубже моего страха.

Тьма обволакивала меня, и я уже не помнил, был ли день или ночь. Когда я продавал найденное, продавец за прилавком не спрашивал. Только смотрел.

[h2]Трещины в реальности[/h2]

На глубине ста футов земля начала шептать. Я не понимал слов, но они царапали сознание, как ногти по стеклу.

Я нашел дверь.

Деревянную. Старую. Под землей.

Она не должна была быть там. [i]Но была.[/i]

[h2]Последняя лопата[/h2]

Я не помню, как оказался на поверхности. Вчера или год назад?

Сосед спросил, почему я стою у пустой ямы, разговаривая сам с собой.

Но ведь я не был один.

Они звали меня обратно.

[h1]Вывод[/h1]

[b]Это не просто игра. Это экскаватор в вашу душу. [/b]

Вы копаете, продаёте, улучшаетесь – а потом замечаете, что реальность [i]трещит[/i].

Зачем я копал? Зачем я продолжаю копать?

Bom, é o que o título diz ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
Apesar de ter me decepcionado, não vou pesar na review do jogo, pois acho que eu criei essa expectativa sozinha. E vou começar logo por esse ponto: não crie expectativas. Realmente, o jogo é sobre cavar um buraco. Nada mais. Sem terror e sem mistérios, apenas buracos. Não espere pela satisfação do tesouro, porque ela não vem (sem spoilers).

Agora que você já aceitou isso e, realmente, só quer passar um tempo cavando, vamos aos detalhes:
- O jogo tem uma dificuldade bem equilibrada. De primeira, os upgrades parecem muito caros e a energia é um absurdo, mas conforme você desce fica bem fácil juntar dinheiro. Zerei o jogo com um saldo de mais de $20000, então é, a progressão é bem suave eu diria.
- Cavar não é difícil, mas não é perfeito. A terra não é retirada em blocos ou pequenos montes, tá mais pra uma esfera de raio x onde o centro é sua mira. O problema disso, são os mini pixels de terra que acabam ficando pra trás, flutuando no ar, e que ainda possuem colisão, então às vezes você pode simplesmente ficar preso no ar pq existem mini partículas invisíveis aos olhos que você não retirou. Não sei se deu pra entender, mas é tipo usar uma borracha pequena pra apagar algo muito grande em um software de desenho.
- Alguns itens são mal explicados ou mal usados. Acho que seria legal se o sensor de metais fosse um item usável de fato, e não um objeto que surge aleatoriamente na sua mão e depois some. Não entendi o que era pra ser a caixinha up/down misteriosa (é um jogo sobre cavar buracos, eu sei que tenho que descer?). Os itens na caixa da garagem são extremamente mal explicados (sem spoilers), um deles eu nem sei o que mudou e o outro eu quase perdi porque, quem diria, era de uso único. Por sorte tinha um save e consegui recuperar sem perder progresso.
- Pra um jogo de simulação pacato, eu senti que os devs poderiam ter adicionado mais coisas pra "entreter" o player. Eu adoraria ter jogado com um rádio, onde eu pudesse ouvir algumas faixas bacanas, e nem precisava ser músicas pop, eu entendo que o jogo não tem esse budget, eu ficaria satisfeita só de ouvir umas músicas originais mesmo que ajudassem a passar o tempo.

Eu não ironicamente tinha me empolgado muito com o jogo, vi muito potencial nele e tive uma baita decepção. Esperava encontrar cartas, itens de pessoas que já tentaram achar o tesouro, locais subterrâneos com alguma relevância, alguns crânios talvez, coisas que REALMENTE adicionassem um mistério e uma história. Acho que se o plot tivesse sido desenvolvido DURANTE o jogo, ao invés de duas cutscenes (a inicial e a final) eu teria me agradado muito mais com o final, teria a experiência de tentar descobrir o que é o tesouro? pq alguém colocou ali? O jogo é sobre a jornada, mas ele não desenvolve nada durante e não faz nada pra que ela seja mais do que o título. Não foi uma experiência ruim, mas não consigo não ficar triste com o que esse jogo poderia ter sido.

The game is cheap af, its worth its money, nothing more.. is this a good or a bad thing? You decide..
I love buying indie games and playing them casual, but this game feels too clunky for me.. I really setup my mind over finishing it somehow and (SPOILER) finding the lurking monster in the ground (SPOILER) , but sadly, the way the game started  let me cold.. dont get me wrong, i did play this without buying it IF YOU KNOW WHAT I MEAN, and then bought it to support the DEV.. 

Movement is not for a casual who likes to jump around and explore on its own.. you have to manage the fcking battery so much, it rips out the joy of digging a hole.. literally the only thing this game is made for, dig a F hole..
Also, the terrain gets you stuck for no reason..
I made a ramp at first so i would not DIE because my battery ran out all the times, surprise, after digging 2 more meters in the ground, my ramp, all of a sudden, was not ramping anymore.. i was getting stuck.. Skill issue or just bad game design?

You cant hold click to continously dig, i got an autoclicker eventually, if you do unlock this later, well, sad, i didnt know about it..

The upgrades dont feel like real upgrades up until later, the 300$ shovel actually digs compared with the starting one, but the inbetween upgrades? Hate it tbh...

The Jetpack is a nice addition to the game tbh, especially after digging for a bit, but hey, IT USES THE F BATTERY! Which explodes when it runs out.. oh, you want to do a longer run? too bad, go charge your battery.. the wort part about it, is the fact that you lose the ores when you DIE BECAUSE YOU RUN OUT OF BATTERY, and they dont get dropped or something, no friend, they get eradicated from the surface of the planet..

AGAIN, I WISH STEAM HAD A MEH REVIEW BUTTON, THIS GAME WOULDVE FIT IT PERFECTLY.

This game is a hole lot of fun. For about five bucks, I feel I got my moneys worth.

It simple, need little to no instruction. If you don't know how to dig a hole yet, it might be a good place to start. Maybe.

Not that I see it happening, or that it needs to happen, but I feel it may need a bit of improvement, with the tinny specks of dirt that I may not notice floating about after I clear an area. I may try to drop down, only to land on a speck I missed, and can't see well, that can drain my heath by a lot. That has happened a few times. But, one can just chalk that up as just a self made hazard, when not being careful enough, while clearing the dirt away.

One of the best things about this game, is it works. I have not run into any glitches.

Nor moles as of yet. I am at about 70m. Thy must be much deeper in. I been itching to chuck some dynamite at them. Dy-no-mite! ^.^

I had thought of making a game like this, with one of the many available procedural land generators for Unity. Such as MoleEngine or Voxelab. This game works much like I had imagined it. All it lacks is a way to place at least some dirt down, to be more like I had envisioned.

The fact you can't lay any dirt down or build anything in it, makes digging, in itself, a hazard. In that you must be extra careful with how you remove the dirt, or you could get stuck down their with no way back up. Been fortunate, that had yet to be an issue. Ya, for planing ahead.

Also, just like in Minecraft, is not a good idea to dig strait down, directly under your feet. Never know when you may end up standing on some lava rock, or fall into a ready made hole that could make you lose a lot of health quickly.

Knowing the game a little better, I feel if I was to start over, I would try to dig strait down in a safe way, to get to the good stuff far more early. I ended up clearing a level area, one layer at a time, as I kept a ramp of dirt to go up and down along the side wall. That meant only collecting all the cheap stuff to start with, and made buying things take longer, than it should have. Don't be like me, and instead, try to dig deeper near the start. You will find, all the stuff to collect up top, is basically not much worth getting.

Don't settle for mere rocks and coal. When you find gold. That be a good time to start clearing the land for all it's real wealth to be had. ^.^

I came. I dug. I questioned my life choices.

This game perfectly captures the raw, unfiltered thrill of digging a hole. The moment I picked up my virtual shovel, I knew I was in for something special. The dirt physics? Immaculate. The existential dread of digging endlessly? Overwhelming. The sheer power of making a hole deeper for no real reason? Life-changing.

At first, I dug for fun. Then I dug to see how deep it could go. Eventually, I was digging because I had become one with the hole. My friends and family no longer recognize me—I am but a mere shadow of my former self, whispering "just one more scoop."

Would I recommend this game? Absolutely. But be warned: once you start digging, the hole stares back.

A Game About Digging A Hole – Eine überraschend fesselnde Erfahrung
Ein simples Konzept mit erstaunlicher Tiefe
„A Game About Digging A Hole“ klingt zunächst nach einer minimalistischen Spielidee – und genau das ist es auch. Doch was auf den ersten Blick wie ein Scherz erscheint, entpuppt sich als meditatives, fast schon süchtig machendes Erlebnis, das Spieler auf eine unerwartete Reise der Selbstentfaltung mitnimmt.

Gameplay – Mehr als nur ein Loch graben
Das Gameplay ist bewusst einfach gehalten: Man gräbt ein Loch. Doch genau darin liegt der Reiz. Das Spiel nutzt minimalistische Mechaniken, um eine tiefgehende Erfahrung zu schaffen. Jeder Spatenstich fühlt sich befriedigend an, der Boden verändert sich allmählich, und man entwickelt eine fast schon persönliche Beziehung zu seinem Loch.

Was dieses Spiel so einzigartig macht, ist das Gefühl des Fortschritts – auch wenn es eigentlich keinen „klassischen Fortschritt“ gibt. Es ist eine Erfahrung, bei der man sich fragt: „Wie tief kann ich gehen?“, sowohl im Spiel als auch metaphorisch.

Atmosphäre und Sounddesign
Das ruhige, fast meditative Sounddesign trägt enorm zur Atmosphäre bei. Die dezenten Geräusche der Erde, das Knistern kleiner Steine und das Echo tief in der Grube sorgen für eine immersive Erfahrung. Es gibt keine störenden Elemente – nur den Spieler, das Werkzeug und das stetig wachsende Loch.

Faszination durch Einfachheit
Was „A Game About Digging A Hole“ so besonders macht, ist die Art und Weise, wie es mit Erwartungshaltungen spielt. Man beginnt mit einem Schmunzeln, bleibt aber überraschend lange dabei. Es ist ein Spiel über Beharrlichkeit, über kleine Erfolge und über die Schönheit von Simplizität.

Fazit
„A Game About Digging A Hole“ ist ein wunderbares Beispiel dafür, dass ein simples Konzept mit der richtigen Umsetzung eine tiefgehende Spielerfahrung liefern kann. Wer Lust auf ein ungewöhnliches, entspannendes und fast schon meditatives Spiel hat, sollte unbedingt den Spaten in die Hand nehmen und loslegen.

⭐ Bewertung: 9/10 – Einfach, aber unerwartet fesselnd!

This game is great, especially for a game that the dev made in their spare time. If you enjoy games like this (e.g., Power Wash Simulator) or digging in other games (e.g., Minecraft), you will probably enjoy this game. It is pretty short, which is understandable, and the fact that you have to complete the game once and start a new game to unlock achievements is somewhat strange to me, but didn't really subtract from the overall experience. I don't know if the dev plans on returning to this game or adding anything to it at any point, but if they do, I have some suggestions:
- More upgrades! If you enjoy the experience of digging and you're thorough like me, you end up with way more money than you know what to do with. Adding more upgrades would make the game more enjoyable and give you something to do with all that extra cash.
- Making it easier to destroy rocks and remove small bits of dirt that are floating up in the air, perhaps by allowing the jetpack to hover or allowing dynamite to be placed precisely instead of thrown. Personally, leaving things floating in the air bothers me and if you don't notice it until you've dug far below it, it can be hard to remove.
- Making the amount of dirt needed for the player to stand on bigger. It sucks to drop down in the hole and somehow land on a tiny speck of dirt you couldn't see and lose a bunch of health.
- Adding a mode or something for after you've beaten the game once to dig further and avoid the hole at the bottom or something like that, so you can dig for longer and give the game more replayability.

В принципе, название игры говорит само за себя. Вам нужно в игре копать дыру, чтобы добраться до сокровища на заднем дворе некоего дома.

Плюсы:
1. Необычный геймплей. Как бы это глупо не звучало, но - да, в игре интересно копать дыру. Т.е. иногда нужно подключать мозг, чтобы трезво оценивать, сможешь ли ты выбраться из дыры или нет, потому что если ты там потеряешься в темноте, не взяв с собой лампочек, то есть риск, что из ямы ты не вылезешь и погибнешь. Либо и вовсе сможешь заблудиться.


2. Система прокачки. Она здесь максимально примитивная, но, тем не менее, интересная в реализации. Под землей ты можешь найти алмазы, золото, серебро, руду и прочее. Продаёшь находки -> Получаешь бабки - > Улучшаешь снаряжение. Да, просто, но как-то... Со вкусом, что ли. Чувствуешь прокачку.

3. Финальный твист. Спойлерить не буду, но в финале игры можно неплохо так охереть. Этого от игры точно не ожидаешь.

Минусы:
1. Продолжительность и отсутствие реиграбельности. Игра проходится за полтора часа. Но возможно пройти и за полчаса, за что даже соответствующая ачивка в Стиме есть. Было бы идеально, чтобы игра предоставляла больше каких-то участков для копания ну и в целом какие-то механики, которые бы позволяли игру пройти по-новому.

2. Мало снаряжения. Хотелось бы, чтобы игра давала чуть больше челленджа и чуть больше снаряжения. Например, чтобы была возможность устанавливать тросы и так далее. В общем, чтобы было чуть больше разнообразия.

Игру бы оценил на 6.5 баллов из 10. Т.е. если разработчик добавит больше механик и больше локаций, то игра точно станет ещё интереснее.

Lights you can place in the Mine wherever you want to give you... well, Light.
And Dynamite should be self explanatory. Boom!

Just keep in mind that it's pretty short. I got about 5 hours out of it, that includes getting all the achievements.
There's not much reason to play afterwards unless you just enjoy digging for the sake of digging.

That said, I got my 5 Euros worth that I paid for that game.

[h1] Points positifs : [/h1]

- Effet de creusage réussi
- Satisfaction de la foreuse en main
- L'accomplissement d'une tâche simple mais satisfaisante
- Gameplay accessible et relaxant
- Mystère sous-jacent qui ajoute une touche d’intrigue et pousse à aller toujours plus loin
- Pas de contrainte de temps ni d'objectif imposé
- Développé par une seule personne
- Jeeeeeetpaaaaaack !

[h1] Points négatifs : [/h1]

- Très court (environ 1h30)
- Arbre de compétence trop rapide à compléter
- Tutoriel inexistant
- Effet des explosions inexistant
- Aucune bande-sonore
- Régénération de l'endurance pénible

[h1] En conclusion... [/h1]

[i] Vous démarrez avec une toute petite pelle de jardin et vous commencez à creuser. Vous obtenez deux/trois pierres, vous les vendez sur l’ordinateur, vous remettez de l’énergie dans votre pelle (oui, c’est magique). Vous creusez alors encore plus loin, obtenez encore de l’argent et pouvez améliorer votre pelle, qui deviendra plus grande, puis rotative, puis… Vous l’avez compris, c’est un jeu qui vous demandera d’améliorer votre équipement (batterie, jetpack). Enfin, vous pourrez acheter des lumières à poser dans vos galeries et de la dynamite pour faire exploser des gros tas de pierres.

Plutôt joli et simple, A Game About Digging A Hole utilise la technologie du voxel pour donner du sens à son énorme trou, ce qui n’est pas sans petits défauts d’affichage : mais pas grave, on creuse encore, de plus en plus loin, pour essayer de trouver le coffre final qui vous réservera une belle surprise. C’est ce genre de petit jeu qui vous récompense avec une simple révélation, frustrante, mais amusante. Frustrante parce qu’on en veut encore, amusante puisqu’elle arrive pile au moment où on commençait à trouver le temps long. C’est bien pensé !

Le jeu est court et propose une rejouabilité liée à quelques succès uniquement. Au-delà de ça, on est sur un jeu « blague » mais honnête, un gros jeu de game jam qualitatif qui mérite d’être joué, surtout à petit prix. Si le concept vous plait, sachez qu’il s’arrête trop tôt, que ce n’est pas aussi satisfaisant que ça, mais vous en aurez pour votre argent. [/i] >> 13/20

I bought this game assuming that it had taken the old flash game Motherlode (an absolute gem of a game), revamped it, and put it on Steam. For the first hour or so, that's about the case. Not quite as rich as Motherlode, but still a fun digging game: Dig minerals, upgrade drill and gear, dig shinier minerals, upgrade gear etc. The controls are pretty poor, with your character easily getting stuck on a lot of terrain.

Then, right as you're feeling good about your gear and starting to really make money, it completely negates anything to do with digging holes, drills, or jetpacks, and decides to throw you into the most generic stealth game imaginable. Also, remember the horrid controls? Definitely does not add to this stage.

Overall, a half-decent game about digging that decides to stop being about digging and turn into an abominable stealth game.

裏庭で穴を掘るだけのゲーム。実質的にはクリッカーに近い（ボタン押しっぱでも掘れる）。
穴を掘る→鉱石をゲット→ガレージで鉱石を換金→貯めたお金でインベントリ容量やショベルのパワーなどをアップグレード／HPや掘削ゲージを回復／ダイナマイトなどのアイテムを買う→また穴を掘る→…………というループを繰り返すだけで、それ以上のことは特にない。
アップグレードのタイミングなどはちょうどいい具合にデザインされていて、クリッカーでよくある「次の段階のアップグレードに手を出せなくてイライラする」というようなことがないのは美点。ゲームプレイの面では、掘り残しの土のポリゴンが宙に浮いててキモい以外のストレスは感じないはず。一地上までの残れるエネルギーとインベントリの残り容量を常に意識しながら掘り進めていくので、一回の掘削ループごとに緊張感もある（さすがに最終アップグレードまでいくとなくなるけど）。
「ひたすら掘る」というコンセプトの上ではよくできているとおもう。

けれども、1.5～3時間のプレイスルーでストーリー上の大きなツイストが一度しかないのはちょっと看過しがたい。もちろん、最初はただ掘り進めるだけでワクワクするし、途中で「おや？」とラストをにおわせるくすぐりみたいのは用意されている。それでも、掘削のループ自体変化がなく、その単調な退屈さを解消するほどの驚きはなかった。

はっきりいって、PV以上のお楽しみは出てこない。そういう意味では注文通りともいえる。その注文が「穴を掘るだけ」なのはともかくとして。
定価含めてギリギリ暇つぶしにちょうどいいかな、というくらいの温度感。
ちなみにストア紹介文には「たった一杯のコーヒーの価格」で楽しめます！　と謳われているけれど、580円ではドトールはもちろん、スタバやブルーボトルコーヒーより高い。円安の影響か、あるいは制作者は非チェーンのちょっと洒落たコーヒーショップに通っているのだろう。

It is exactly what the name implies, but also more than just that.

The premise of the game is simple: you bought a new house from an ad that promised riches by digging in your graveyard, so it's exactly what you do. You start with very simple equipment collecting stones and coal, which you then sell and then use the money to recharge your battery, heal yourself and buy upgrades and this consists of most of the gameplay loop. Upgrades involve improving your shovel, backpack size, battery charge and jetpack power. Along the way, there are some structures and other things to be found, but you're mainly just digging to the bottom, where the game then ends.

Finishing the game once unlocks achievement mode, which then makes it so you can unlock more achivements in the game, such as finishing the game in under half an hour.

It's a very fun game, but I think that what mostly holds it back is that it's [i]too[/i] simple. While I understand that the game is meant to be simple and fun, I also wish the game was a bit longer, with more things and secrets to find along the way and with some more upgrades to buy (maxing out all upgrades doesn't take too long).

This is, nonetheless, an easy recommendation.

So... I feel like this was made just to prove on how simple and easy it is to keep a guy entertained... Well, proven correct. Enjoyed it. Channeled my inner dwarf that I didn't know I had and Yes, Yes I did have the "Diggy diggy hole" song playing on repeat as I played this game.

A game with a title like this hardly needs much of an explanation, but an explanation I shall give nonetheless. If you find yourself wondering if this game is for you... well, if you have played enough of those 'mine for ore, sell ore for cash, use cash for upgrades, dig faster, get more ore, get more money and so on" games, the answer will be a definitive yes. Or, if you really like digging holes, also yes.

The premise is really simple. There's a back yard. There's supposedly a treasure in the back yard, so you decide to dig it up. What will happen?

Well, you start off with a really small shovel, a small backpack, low amounts of energy, no jetpack, and so on. You'll dig slowly at first, but as you dig up ore, you can take it back to your shed, sell it, and spend it on upgrades.

Before long, you'll have a high powered shovel, tons of ore space, a high powered jetpack and so on. You can buy little items like lamps and dynamite to help you out.

I mean, most of it is pretty straight forward. You dig, sell, upgrade, dig more. Eventually you'll get to a place where there's kind of an 'ending sequence,' and since I don't want to give away any spoilers, I'll just leave it mostly at that. It won't be very hard for you to figure out what to do.

Most of the game is passive digging; there is only one part with 'enemies.' During your dig you'll find ore, treasures, little caverns, and some little hidden' rooms.' Again - it's REALLY not all that complicated.

The gameplay is satisfying - especially once you've finally upgraded your shovel to be able to dig quickly, and have lots of energy so you don't have to go back to recharge all the time. It's very simple, low-IQ fun (you will NOT have to use your brain, in case the incredibly simple videos weren't clear).

The achievements were mostly easy; there was one I had to try a few times for but eventually got. 100%'ing the game will not take the remainder of your life.

And it's just kinda fun.. rather than deleting the game and moving on, I think I'll leave it installed in case I want to come back to it.

Graphics are fine - fun and engaging. No music thank God. Sound effects cheesy. Gameplay easy. ONLY frustrating part is that sometimes when you dig, little tiny 'particles' remain in midair, and those particles can block your path - so you have to carefully aim your shovel at the microscopic little mid-air dirt particles and dig them out of the way. It doesn't happen enough to be frustrating, but that was the only annoying mechanic in the entire experience - otherwise the playing felt quite natural and fun.

Worth full price? Worth five bucks? I'd say yeah, five bucks for a decent small distraction. You can get as much or little out of this game as you like - you can play and win, or you can achievement hunt, or you can just mess around. (At one point I was just digging out massive swaths of the backyard for no reason, lol.) So yeah, I'd say this would be a fine purchase at full price.

So if you want to dig a hole, this will be your dream come true. Otherwise, if you're NOT a fan of digging a hole, I would suggest you move along, because this game DOES feature digging of holes @_@

The concept of A Game About Digging A Hole is interesting, but the execution falls short. It feels more like a demo version rather than a fully fleshed-out game. There is so much untapped potential here—it's a shame it hasn't been expanded upon.

I completed all achievements in just 3.5 hours, which left me wanting more. If the developers were to add more depth, mechanics, and content, this could be a much better experience.

Cons:
- Feels incomplete, like an early prototype
- Lacks depth and variety
- Too short, needs more content

I really hope this game gets expanded in the future, as it has a lot of potential. But in its current state, it’s hard to recommend.

This game has a really cool premise, but if you are coming into this game with the fantasy about digging a sick base or finding cool events and collectibles, this is very much just a simulator about digging a hole and a really disappointing ending. [spoiler]Like no treasure and your own perilous death after wasting an hour or two.[/spoiler] I also didn't love the upgrade system as much either, in the beginning of the game it's very tedious and slow, which I guess is pretty standard, but you're working with bad shovels that's awkward to use and leaves a pixel sized dirt block that blocks you from moving often. Until you unlock your max capabilities midway through and there's no more upgrades you'll be cruising, but by the time I have any decent equipment I'm collecting pointless money since the shop is useless to me now.
In the end this game has been getting positive reviews and I can understand why, the concept is cool and the ending was, albeit annoying, a creative tale that leaves you wondering. It's a pretty cheap game, and if you don't mind digging for an hour or two, buy it! But for people like myself expecting way more because of the positive reviews please consider that you may not enjoy it for these reasons. All in all, happy digging!

[h1] A Game About Digging a Hole: Does what it says on the tin. [/h1]

[h2] Story: [/h2]
Probably the shortest part of this review, because there really isn't one, not there needs to be. You see a flyer stating that there's treasure buried in the backyard of a house for sale, and you buy the house and start digging. That's it. If there's any deeper connections or lore implications in this game, I wasn't able to find them.

[h2] Gameplay: [/h2]
The terrain in your backyard is voxel-based, and you'll find resources, hazards, and obstacles at every level of the hole. There are several upgrades you can buy by selling off the resources you find while digging, but you'll snatch them all up fairly quickly, with no use for excess cash aside from recharging your health and energy, and buying the meager consumables. There's no deep upgrade paths or meaningful progression aside from being able dig more, move faster, carry more, and spend more time underground before needing to recharge. I'd have more of an issue with the rougher edges of this game if it wasn't $5. The dynamite is too expensive in my opinion, especially considering how it's pretty underwhelming and useless. The lamps are decently priced, but the light doesn't travel that far and they wash the area in a pretty harsh orange glow. At this point, I'm just being nitpicky, because honestly the game is great for what it costs.

[h2] Visuals/Audio: [/h2]
As mentioned before, the graphics are all voxel-based meaning you can run into some annoying bugs like getting caught on a minuscule piece of floating geometry, which actually happened more often than I'd like. There's no music to speak of, and the sound effects are repetitive and annoying, but can be turned off. Again, the amount of grace I'm willing to extend for these problems is enormous because I paid less than a coffee for about 2 hours of decent fun.

[h3] Personal thoughts: [/h3]
The game is fine, runs great on the Steam Deck, but it probably won't win any awards, and that's okay. I went into this game with zero expectations, and you could say that all of my expectations were met. You could probably watch a movie or play an episode or two of a podcast while digging, but this game is far too short to be considered a chill game I'd ever return to. That being said, it made an excellent little palate cleanser after sinking 140 hours into Persona 5 Royal. Would love to see more short, sweet games like this pop up at a similar price point.

Wer hat als Kind nicht davon geträumt, einfach loszulegen und ein riesiges Loch zu buddeln? A Game About Digging a Hole nimmt genau diesen schlafenden Traum und macht ihn zur Realität – zumindest digital.

Das Konzept ist simpel, aber genau das macht es so genial: Man gräbt ein Loch. Immer weiter. Immer tiefer. Doch es bleibt nicht nur beim simplen Buddeln! Während man sich in die Tiefe vorarbeitet, findet man wertvolle Erze, die man verkaufen kann, um bessere Werkzeuge zu bekommen. 
Mit jeder Verbesserung wird das Graben schneller, effizienter und noch befriedigender.

Die meditative Atmosphäre und der endlose Buddelspaß sorgen für Unterhaltung. Man verliert sich regelrecht in der simplen, aber suchterzeugenden Gameplay-Schleife.

Kurz gesagt: A Game About Digging a Hole ist das perfekte Spiel für alle, die jemals eine Schaufel in der Hand hatten und dachten: „Wie tief kann ich wohl graben?“ Absolute Empfehlung! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

Imagine my surprise when my fun dig hole game turned into a horror game...

It's $5. You'll spend about 2 hours with it. It's probably worth $2.50/hour. Thumbs up, it was fine, but only because they knew what they had to offer and what it was worth.

Having to click repeatedly sucks, you'll get tired of it by the end, but then it's the end so, whatever. Also you can't see your body but you will be constantly reminded that it exists, because the holes and passages you dig are never quite big enough for you to fit through. What part of you is there not enough room for? Do you have a giant head? Is the hole not wide enough for your shoulders? Are you just too thicc? You'll never know, all you can do is just keep making the holes wider until the game decides you can fit.

You'll probably get to the end and your response will be something like [spoiler]... really? that's it? I dug for two hours for this? [/spoiler] But Digging a Hole, like life, is all about the journey. And the repeated clicking, and the getting stuck for no clear reason, and the somewhat disappointing ending. On reflection I guess Digging a Hole is remarkably like life.

Lo recomiendo, con peros.

Obviamente se nota un juego muy sencillo para que creo que explora el concepto bastante satisfactoriamente y que, si te gusta lo que ves de él de primeras, seguro que pasas mínimo un par de horas divertidas que no está mal por el precio. 

Lógicamente, el juego tiene sus grandes peros, el primero de ellos, la progresión. Si te lo tomas con relativa calma, a mitad del juego ya tienes absolutamente todas las mejoras y no hay incentivos para seguir consiguiendo dinero, y eso si te lo tomas como vaciar el agujero entero, es lo normal y tienes que asumirlo, pero lo veo un problema si partimos de que eso puede llegar en 40 minutos - 1 hora si te lo tomas con menos calma.

Eso por no hablar de que parece que los tesoros, a parte de pocos, no te dan cantidades que resulten satisfactorias y no están compensados con lo que ya llevas. 3/4 de lo mismo con el tesoro del garaje.

Evidentemente tiene pinta de que es un juego para recaudar dinero para el developer, que supone el esfuerzo justo para él y al resto nos da un rato entretenido (que ya es más que muchos), y eso lo respeto, pero me da la sensación de que está algo desaprovechado y que podría explorarse bastante más es concepto (que, con la ventas y éxito que ha tenido, seguro que lo hará).

En general y como resumen: Divertido para un rato pero la progresión pierde sentido al poco rato.

Honestly, from what I've seen and from what I've heard, it seemed like it's right up my alley. A game about doing mundane tasks like digging holes or cleaning up? Managing resources and purchasing upgrades? Doing something as boring and silly as this for possibly an insane amount of hours? Sign me right up! Sadly, this wasn't exactly what I expected, which is odd given that the whole premise is in the title.

Like, I'm a big fan of Power Wash Sim, Hardspace Shipbreaker, Trash Goblin and other similar games. I should be a fan of A Game About Digging A Hole but I'm just not. It feels janky but not in a good way. The character gets stuck on barely visible specks of dirt. The game also starts to lag eventually which makes the whole experience quite rough to deal with. And then once you beat it, you'll unlock the ability to unlock achievements for things you've done already, meaning you'll start the game again and do the same thing again.

I don't know. I think a lot of games like this are great to take your mind off things and to just do something as mundane as digging or cleaning for a long time in a relaxing way... but in this specific case, I found it more frustrating than enjoyable or relaxing.

I guess it's just not my cup of tea. Oh well.

Im Stream war das wirklich eine Wucht: klicken, klicken und nochmals klicken macht einfach Laune.
Jedoch wirklich nur, wenn Du auf diese Art von Grinding Games stehst.
Sonst regiert schnell Langeweile und später dann Frust, wenns vielleicht lahmer voran geht, als Dir lieb wäre.

Doch solltest Du zur Fraktion der Aufwertungs-süchtigen, Loot klaubenden und stets der nächsten Stufe des Effizienz hinterher hechelnden Optimierungs Gamer zählen...
... ja dann...
...
...
...
... dann hau die fünf Tacken auf´n Kopp und rein ins frisch im Vorgarten gebuddelte Loch und dem Schatz ganz weit unten hinterher gehetzt, aber dalli!

Im Grunde macht man im Game nämlich nix anders als Graben.
Du passt auf, dass Deine Elektro-Schaufel nicht leer läuft, sonst hast Du halt soeben Dein frühes Grab ausgehoben.
Behältst Du den Batterie-Stand jedoch im Auge, entreißt Mutter Erdes Schoss fleißig Erze und Materialien und verhökerst den ganzen Kappes dann bei Mineralien-Ebay... dann kannste richtig reich werden.

Oderrrrrrrr......

Du kaufst eifrig Upgrades für Deinen Grabo-Mat und vielleicht am Ende auch noch ein Jetpack, falls Deine Ausgrabungen doch weiter hinab führen als Du wieder hinauf jumpen könntest.
Wer will schon in nem Loch im eigenen Vorgarten verhungern?
Denn: Da unten hört Dich niemand schreien!
(Faustformel für Autoren: Da unten hört Dich niemand schreiben!)

Und so ist das hier im Grunde in Klicker Game mit netter Grafik, ner anfachenden Loot-Upgrade-Karotte vor der Nase und nem schön inszenierten Ende.

Mehr nicht.

Und das reicht auch vollkommen, denn:
Solltest Du das Spiel dann endlich durch haben, ist auch erstmal gut mit der Klickerei und Du kannst Deinen halb toten Klickfinger ein wenig erholen.
Außer:
Du kriegst einfach nicht genug von der immer und immer und immmmmerrrrrrr weiter gehenden, nie enden wollenden Klickerei...
... dann stürzt Du Dich in den Achievement-Modus und legst mit tollen Errungenschaften nochmal von vorne los.

JUHU!?!

Also prüfe die eigene Ausdauer: Wie viel Klickarbeit bist Du bereit zu investieren, um dem Ganzen hier sprichwörtlich auf den Grund zu gehen?

Kriegst Du wie ich vom Werte hoch klicken nie genug, dann rein hier und ich wünsch Dir beim Klicken, Graben, manchmal explodieren und am Ende erstaunt gucken wie immer...

... viel Spaß  ;-)

A Game About Digging A Hole è un gioco che, nella sua semplicità, è riuscito a conquistare un vasto pubblico. L’idea alla base è tanto basilare quanto affascinante: scavare una buca. Ma ciò che potrebbe sembrare un passatempo ripetitivo si trasforma presto in un’esperienza coinvolgente e, per molti, addirittura terapeutica. Il titolo si è rivelato una piccola gemma per gli appassionati dei giochi di esplorazione e miglioramento progressivo, con numerosi riferimenti a classici come Motherload e altri titoli storici del genere.

[b]Gameplay e Meccaniche[/b]

Il cuore del gioco è un ciclo di gameplay estremamente intuitivo ma incredibilmente soddisfacente: si scava, si raccolgono risorse, si vendono materiali per guadagnare denaro, si acquistano potenziamenti e poi si torna a scavare con maggiore efficienza. Questo loop di progressione continua a stimolare il giocatore, portandolo a voler raggiungere sempre nuove profondità.

Le meccaniche di scavo sono semplici, ma efficaci. Il giocatore inizia con una pala di base e una batteria limitata, ma man mano che si avanza nel gioco è possibile acquistare potenziamenti per migliorare la capacità della pala, aumentare la durata della batteria e persino ottenere un jetpack per rendere più agevoli gli spostamenti nelle profondità della buca. Tuttavia, molti giocatori hanno sottolineato come le opzioni di upgrade siano piuttosto limitate e si possano ottenere rapidamente, riducendo il senso di progressione a lungo termine.

Un altro elemento che ha diviso la community è la fisica del terreno. Se da un lato vedere la terra sgretolarsi e rimuoversi in modo realistico è un aspetto apprezzato, dall’altro molti giocatori hanno trovato fastidioso il problema dei piccoli frammenti di terreno che rimangono sospesi e bloccano il passaggio. Questo potrebbe essere migliorato con futuri aggiornamenti.

[b]Atmosfera e Immersione[/b]

A livello estetico, il gioco adotta una grafica minimalista ma funzionale. Le texture del terreno sono dettagliate e l’illuminazione cambia in base alla profondità, creando un senso di immersione graduale man mano che si scende sempre più in basso. L’accompagnamento sonoro è altrettanto efficace, con effetti realistici di scavo e una colonna sonora rilassante che contribuisce a creare un’esperienza meditativa.

Molti giocatori hanno descritto il gioco come un’attività quasi zen, perfetta per essere giocata senza particolare stress, magari mentre si ascolta musica o si chiacchiera con amici in una chiamata. Questo aspetto lo rende un ottimo passatempo per chi cerca un’esperienza rilassante e priva di frenesia.

[b]Durata e Prezzo[/b]

Uno degli argomenti più dibattuti tra i giocatori riguarda la durata complessiva del gioco. Per chi si focalizza solo sull’obiettivo principale, il titolo può essere completato in circa 1-2 ore, il che per alcuni potrebbe sembrare troppo breve. Tuttavia, coloro che si lasciano coinvolgere dall’idea di svuotare completamente l’area di gioco possono tranquillamente passare anche 10-15 ore a scavare e migliorare la propria tecnica.

Il prezzo di 5 euro è stato giudicato da molti adeguato, soprattutto considerando che ci sono titoli tripla A molto più costosi con una durata simile. Altri, invece, ritengono che il rapporto qualità-prezzo potrebbe migliorare con l’introduzione di nuovi contenuti o modalità, come una modalità infinita o un supporto al multiplayer.

[b]Finale e Critiche[/b]

Uno degli aspetti più discussi è il finale del gioco. Senza fare spoiler, molti giocatori hanno trovato il cambiamento di genere e gameplay nelle fasi finali piuttosto brusco e fuori contesto. Dopo ore passate a scavare e migliorare il proprio equipaggiamento, ci si ritrova di colpo in una situazione che stravolge completamente le meccaniche di gioco. Alcuni hanno apprezzato questo colpo di scena, mentre altri avrebbero preferito un finale più in linea con il resto dell’esperienza.

Altri punti critici segnalati dai giocatori includono la mancanza di varietà nel gameplay e l’assenza di una vera e propria storia o lore che giustifichi il viaggio del giocatore. Alcuni utenti avrebbero voluto più segreti nascosti o elementi narrativi che dessero maggiore profondità al gioco.

[b]Conclusione[/b]

A Game About Digging A Hole è un titolo che riesce a offrire un’esperienza soddisfacente grazie alla sua semplicità e al suo gameplay rilassante. Sebbene abbia alcuni difetti, come la breve durata e la ripetitività, il gioco ha colpito per la sua atmosfera e per la capacità di trasformare un’azione elementare in un’esperienza appagante.

Se siete alla ricerca di un passatempo leggero e senza troppe pretese, o se avete sempre sognato di scavare un’enorme buca senza alcun motivo apparente, allora questo gioco fa per voi. Tuttavia, se cercate un’esperienza più articolata e longeva, potreste trovare il contenuto un po’ limitato.

Voto finale: 7.5/10

Review of A Game About Digging A Hole

A Game About Digging A Hole is exactly what it promises: a game about digging a hole. Yet, this simplicity hides a surprisingly engaging and relaxing experience that has captivated a broad audience. What might seem like a repetitive pastime soon becomes a deeply satisfying experience, and for some players, even therapeutic. The game is a small gem for fans of exploration and progressive improvement, with clear inspirations from classics like Motherload and other well-known digging games.

[b]Gameplay and Mechanics[/b]

The core gameplay loop is simple yet incredibly satisfying: dig, collect resources, sell materials for money, purchase upgrades, and dig deeper with increased efficiency. This continuous progression keeps players engaged, pushing them to reach greater depths.

The digging mechanics are straightforward but effective. Players start with a basic shovel and a limited battery, but as they progress, they can purchase upgrades to improve their shovel's efficiency, increase battery life, and even acquire a jetpack for easier movement in deeper areas. However, some players have pointed out that the upgrade options are rather limited and can be obtained quickly, reducing the long-term progression appeal.

Another divisive aspect is the physics of the terrain. While watching the dirt crumble and shift realistically is a highlight for many, others find the floating fragments of dirt that obstruct movement to be frustrating. Future updates could improve this aspect.

[b]Atmosphere and Immersion[/b]

Visually, the game features a minimalist yet functional design. The textures are detailed, and the lighting changes as players dig deeper, creating an immersive descent into the earth. The sound design is equally well-crafted, with realistic digging noises and a calming soundtrack that contributes to a meditative experience.

Many players describe the game as a relaxing, almost zen-like activity—perfect for unwinding while listening to music or chatting with friends. This makes it an ideal casual experience without the stress of more complex games.

[b]Final Thoughts[/b]

A Game About Digging A Hole successfully delivers a fun and satisfying experience through its simplicity. Despite some shortcomings, such as its short duration and repetitive gameplay, the game excels in creating an immersive and oddly compelling experience.

If you’re looking for a lighthearted, casual game that allows you to dig endlessly, this game is for you. However, if you’re seeking a more elaborate and long-lasting adventure, you might find the content somewhat lacking.

Final Score: 7.5/10

The hole, a breathtaking implementation to our earthly experience disguised as empty space.

There is nothing through analogous comparability that even gets close to overshadowing the beauty, the complexity and the utter designed-by-a-creator aspect that is the hole.

Once I went for a walk in the woods, back in my youth and back in what i considered to be the stage of simple, joyous life. I was trekking along when unbeknown-st to me I would have such an enigmatic experience that I wouldn't understand it for far too many years in the future. I sauntered noisily down the dusty path when I encountered a large beaver standing there. 

He was a kind soul but in a feral state perhaps caused by a dispute with a close loved one or maybe a traumatic involvement in the death of a lasting family pet. He turned his eyes to face in a pugnacious mind only a beaver could possess. He wanted the feeling of being in control again and to feel some sense of disassociation from his troubling life. There stood his opportunity for a release of that anger in 4'2 kid just living carefree.

The beaver attacked. he lunged forward with the plan to strike his large timber-modification mouth tools into the side of my neck. This was the moment that changed everything. a mere 3 seconds from an untimely demise, an uneven footing on the dirt path caused me to fall just in time to avoid the herbivore-turned-carnivore's assault. He flew threw the air and hit a tree that knocked him backwards off the side of the trail and down a steep bank. I sprinted home and in my exhaustion never realised that one... simple... hole. saved my life.

Now comes to the present, when to my surprise, the hole has affected a lot more people around me than I could have imagined. I see the people and their stories wherever I go. If it's a hole that helps start a young star's music career or simply the saving of someone life from what seemed an irreparable accident, I have seen it work miracles and change my perspective on life.

Thus i recommend this experience for those of you who didn't get it yet or haven't been able to see the great power of the hole. This is a glimpse into the beloved memories and treasures that it is, in real life. I'm glad it is not forgotten and can be valued for what it is for generations to come.

"We are surrounded by monstrous and tragic things. At the same time, we are also surrounded by moments of incredible, almost unbelievable, beauty," - Werner Herzog. What a world, a dazzling mask before the void that bared itself before my unsuspecting id. I am gripped with the sense that I am alone in voicing the authors' perverse intent. They have cleverly woven a metaphor that initially demonstrates contempt and malice, but slowly relinquishes that grasp to gently inform: 

"You are the mouse on my wheel."

This could also be perceived as a metaphor for a laboratory, where the cheese is preyed upon by libidos unmoderated by higher reason. The players are reduced to rodents, after all. It’s a well-accepted fact, tested, that the desire to run on wheels isn't unique to selectively bred lab mice. Any field mouse will do. It's remarkable, really: this creature, with its short, miserable life, a short-sighted and instinctive bundle of desires, is betrayed by itself. Seeing the wheel, feeling its unsteady and mysterious chassis, the mouse can finally run. Like never before, faster and more than ever, but never further. For once, it seems, they are free to indulge their primary drive: to run, and by extension, to seek, and to hopefully acquire. In vain, it gives up its energy, its life's essence, and what is most cherished by nature, willingly to the trap. Today I learned that moles eat mice.

"The life of every individual, viewed as a whole and in general, and when only its most significant features are emphasized, is really a tragedy; but gone through in detail it has the character of a comedy." which I am informed Schopenhauer said. On the second playthrough, one should be jarringly aware that they have struck quarried bedrock, that they have not only hit pay dirt, but that it is only dirt. They should be aware that it is all too easy. By then, they can choose to mindlessly pursue achievements, earning fiat rewards for each strange thrust down the co-created chasm. Another turn of the wheel of samsara, serving only to deepen the soul's exhaustion.

Honestly this game is exactly what it says on the box -- a game about digging a hole. It's fun, if a bit simpler and quicker to finish than I'd have expected. I'm happy to have gotten my money's worth but I wouldn't have minded a little more in the way of secrets and or additional upgrades. 

As many people say, the ending comes kind of out of nowhere and with very little fanfare. Deeply underwhelming. Which isn't unfair, I suppose, given how little plot or fanfare the game opens with. Still, rubbed me a little wrong without ruining the experience. Just sort of one of those "you could have gone with anything, and you went with [u]THAT_[/u]??" sort of moments.

For anyone who wants to know, and remember, I'll put it here in spoiler text at the end of my review. (I'd have liked to have known so I figure I'll pay that forward). 

Despite my feelings about the ending the game really scratches an itch that my brain enjoys: dig stuff up, sell it, improve stats, dig up more stuff and go further and dig better every time. It's honestly a tight little gameplay loop. Would've loved a few more tools or a few more upgrade steps (gimme a really expensive upgrade that's god tier, you know? where I'm just making chump work out of it at the end, let me break things a bit), but overall, it's a fun time. 

If I were to be honest I thought the dynamite was going to matter more. You use it to blow up rocks and magma rocks but you could just dig past almost all of them and it wouldn't change anything. Or that's how ti felt. But still, overall satisfying and enjoyable. Once you beat it you can open a 2nd play through for in game achievements. 

[spoiler]The ending: once you get down to the bottom of the yard there's a stealth section avoiding some stuff (which I won't spoil) and when you finally get past it, there's a chest. You open the chest, and it's empty, and then your character turns around and gets eaten (pg friendly) by the things you were avoiding. The intro cut scene plays, with the mysterious unseen figuring marking off another line on their tally. It just feels frustrating, the haha, the treasure was your own demise all along sort of ending.[/spoiler]

A Game About Digging A Hole is a fairly good game, pretty short most people can probably get a few hours out of it maybe a few more if you're going for 100%. I do wish it had more objectives or unique things to dig, not the most replay-ability, but for about $5 I thought it was pretty fun.

I lost track of time, lost in the rhythmic motion, the push and pull, the raw satisfaction of going deeper. Every layer of earth stripped away felt like shedding my past self—my stress, my addictions, my doubts. My body grew stronger, my mind clearer. Nothing else mattered. No hunger, no sleep. Only the hole. Only the descent.

They say there’s a treasure at the bottom. I don’t know if it’s real. I don’t know how long I’ve been digging. But I do know one thing—I'm not stopping.

10/10 Would keep digging

Eu, um latino americano sem dinheiro no banco, devendo o preço dos meus órgãos prum agiota, encontro uma casa nos Estados Unidos da America pela batela de 10.000 $, no panfleto em frente a casa, mostrava um png bem convincente de um báu do tesouro, e dai como não sou bobo nem nada, pedi mais dinheiro pro agiota, prometendo a ele o céu e a terra com o tanto de dinheiro que eu arrecadaria nessa empreitada. Assim, com o dinheiro em mãos e a escritura da casa no meu nome, comprei uns equipamentos básicos na ULX, incluindo uma pá ultra mega super hiper RFRP (Rápida, Forte, Resistente e Potente), e dois detectores, um de objetos detectáveis e outro de detectação, (por incrível que pareça os dois possuem mecânicas muito semelhantes), e com estas minhas bugigangas comecei onde demarquei o x a cavar, e cavar, e cavar, e cavar... e cavar... e cavar... e cavar, até que finalmente, eu voltei a cavar, já não aguentava mais, eu sentia o magma do núcleo da terra queimar o meu pezinho, não encontrei muita coisa a não ser ouro, diamante, prata, alguns fosseis que datam de milhões de anos, estruturas antigas de mineração, algumas maletas cheias de dinheiro,  mas nada de tesouro.

  Realmente acho que a esse ponto não valeu a pena compra essa casa, eu já gastei cerca 1 bilhão de dólares que eu mesmo arrecadei vendendo essas pedrinhas transparentes e brilhantes com o equipamento que estou usando para encontrar esse maldito tesouro, e até agora, não consegui juntar dinheiro o bastante pra pagar o agiota ou se quer a pensão do meu filho, mas agora que literalmente voltei do inferno a superfície, queria nada mais que tomar um pouco de limonada que o antigo dono tinha deixado especialmente pra mim, onde havia deixado na geladeira de dentro, pena que ele esqueceu de me dá a chave da casa e na ultima vez que nos vimos ele tava estojando uns cristais em uns compartimentos esquisitos no caminhão de mudanças, por mais que eu não entendesse como um caminhão de mudanças poderia ter uma caçamba ao em vez de um contaneir e o por que ele precisava de tanto feno assim, pra ter uma ideia, eram tantos empilhados que parecia até a casinha de palha de um dos 3 porquinhos kkkkk, por um momento eu até pensei em ter ouvido alguém tossindo lá de dentro, mas ele falou que na verdade era os pássaros da região que cantarolavam desse jeito, e com muito euforia me apontou para o passarinho, a primeira vista quando me virei parecia que ele estava bem longe pois eu não conseguia se quer ver um pássaro pela redondeza, mas quando me deparei, ouvi novamente o canto que mais soava com uma tosse abafada vinda de trás, e empolgado de que ele estivesse do meu lado eu me virei rapidamente, mas dessa vez era só ele, ele disse que o pássaro era muito rápido e seria difícil que um iniciante como eu fitasse os olhos nele na primeira tentativa, e que se eu quisesse vê-lo teria que tentar mais vezes, por não ter tempo livre para isso, acabei recusando a sugestão e me despedindo dele.

  Mas de qual quer forma, ouvi alguns sons grotescos vindo de uma larga extensão cavernosa que encontrei em minha expedição, logo irei lá continuar essa ardura procura, lá, não tem oxigênio e o fogo por vez não consegue entrar em combustão, a também uma forte radioatividade na região que interfere correntes elétricas tais como presentes nas lâmpadas e na minha perfuradeira, estou sentindo um leve gosto de ferro na boca, o que embora seja provavelmente do meu resfriado não sairei daqui até encontrar o que por direito é meu, meu baú!

Start digging a hole.

Dig deeper.

Dig so deep you briefly see the meaning of existence… then immediately regret it.

The dirt starts looking suspiciously like your missed deadlines and crushed dreams.

Occasionally, rocks appear, forcing you to re-evaluate your strategy and your life.

Friends ask what you’re playing. You mumble, “It’s about holes, leave me alone.”

The controls? Surprisingly satisfying, like a zen garden made of soil and existential dread. The soundtrack? Silence. Because silence is the only appropriate response to digging a hole this deep.

I saw this game making the rounds as the current "random surprise hit indie game of the week" that came out of nowhere, with lots of people suddenly talking about it and streamers all suddenly playing it. Decided to bite and play it myself as it seemed interesting.

The game is short and has a simple gameplay loop of Dig -> Sell Ores -> Upgrade Equipment -> Repeat until you reach the game's ending. That simple loop honestly just clicks, and the short length of the game means that it won't overstay its welcome. Achievements become available on a second playthrough as well, if that's your thing. 

If you're looking for a game that you can waste a single afternoon playing or just a short simple game to play, then I honestly recommend this game a lot! I hope in the future we can see a sequel of sorts that greatly expands on the idea of this game, I think the concept is great!

It's OK but I mostly felt annoyed. Too many annoying and user hostile features:

The first hour is way, way too slow. Put on a podcast.
Have to click like mad, but can't click too fast: annoying. An autoclicker is necessary. The autoclick upgrade comes in way too late and isn't very satisfying.
Inventory full? Annoying.
Low battery? Annoying.
The low battery warning kicks in way too early because it's tuned for the endgame, which makes me ignore warnings.
If your inventory is full and you dig up and ore, it gets destroyed -> lost money: annoying.
Every upgrade doubles in price but doesn't double in effect.
The battery recharge price is unclear and unsatisfying. Am I getting overcharged because of rounding?
Fall damage is inconsistent. Why am I getting damaged from falling such a short distance sometimes?
Tiny almost invisible pieces of terrain that you get stuck on and take fall damage from: annoying.
$100 dynamite that I had to save up for just disappears: annoying.
Lava rock every 3 feet: annoying.
The game knows you haven't saved for 30 minutes, but doesn't autosave.
You can easily and accidentally destroy your own lights, but you don't get a refund, nothing.
Dynamite can slip off rocks.
In the endgame you have a very deep hole, but getting in and out is annoying, mostly because of floating terrain bits and fall damage.
Shadows are too harsh and the game is artificially dark (I can literally still see the sun), making digging (!) annoying.

Endgame was sort of cool. Ending was meh. [spoiler]I literally have a freaking jetpack. What are they gonna do?[/spoiler]

요즘 폰 겜에 5600원으로 가챠 한번 돌리고 꺼야 한다는 걸 생각해보면 혜자도 이런 혜자가 없다.

Un’ode alla vanga: il sublime scavare del tempo

Oh, voi che bramate il dolce suono della terra smossa e il gaudio di un pozzo senza fondo, prestate orecchio a questo inno ludico che narra di una maestosa impresa: A Game About Digging A Hole. Questo gioco, che par appalesarsi umile nel nome, cela invece un’esperienza tanto profonda quanto la fossa ch’esser vi si chiede di scavare.

Ludus et mirabilia
Il fulcro del giuoco è un’arte antica quanto l’uomo: affondare il ferro nel suolo e proseguire ancor oltre, in un viaggio senza fine né meta se non quella imposta dallo spirito tenace del giocatore. L’impeto dello scavo si fa via via più ardente, la gravità più severa, la fatica più dolce nel vedere la propria opera crescere in vastità e profondità. Ogni granello di terra rimosso è un trionfo, ogni attimo speso un inno alla dedizione.

Un’euforia interattiva
Non vi è mera ripetizione in tale impresa, ché ogni colpo di vanga è permeato da una fisicità sublime, un’interazione che sa d’arcano e di mistico. Il suolo risponde con realismo sconcertante, la luce muta col calare della profondità, l’aria stessa sembra rarefarsi nell’oscurità crescente della voragine. Il giocatore non si limita a scavare: egli sfida il Creato, tentando di giungere là ove nessuno ha osato prima.

Bellezza e immersione
Lo stile visivo, seppur di apparente semplicità, cela una cura certosina nei dettagli: le texture terrose si sgretolano con dolcezza, la palette cromatica evolve come un affresco rinascimentale, e l’acustica, con suoni di suolo spezzato e venti sussurranti, immerge l’animo in una dimensione quasi ipnotica.

Giudizio finale
A Game About Digging A Hole è più d’un semplice passatempo: è una meditazione interattiva, un’esperienza catartica, un inno alla perseveranza e alla scoperta. Scavare non è mai stato così entusiasmante, così profondo – nel senso più letterale e spirituale del termine. A voi, o spiriti avventurosi, non resta che impugnare la vanga e lasciare che la terra ceda sotto il peso della vostra volontà.

Voto: 10/10 – Un buco senza fondo nel cuore dei giocatori.

You can't dig them unless you get your crosshair right on the tiny piece.  Some pieces are so small that you can't see them, so it's impossible to dig because it's too tiny to see, yet you can still impact and take fall damage landing on them.  Other than that, great little indie game. SPOILERS: I'm about to check out achievement mode.

If you’ve ever wanted to play a game that’s both simple and deeply satisfying, "A Game About Digging a Hole" is a unique and oddly compelling experience. At its core, it’s exactly what it sounds like: a game about digging. But don't let the simplicity fool you; this game has a surprising amount of charm and depth, turning a seemingly mundane task into a relaxing and rewarding adventure.

Gameplay: The mechanics are straightforward, but that’s part of the beauty. You dig a hole, and as you progress, you uncover various underground treasures, strange creatures, and bizarre situations. It’s more about the journey than any end goal, and it’s this relaxed approach that makes it so enjoyable. You don’t feel pressured or rushed; it’s a laid-back, meditative process that allows you to just unwind and enjoy the experience.

The controls are simple and intuitive, making it accessible to everyone, from beginners to more seasoned gamers. The game gives you just enough challenge to keep things interesting without ever feeling frustrating.

Atmosphere and Design: The art style is minimalist yet effective, and the sound design complements the experience perfectly. The simple, almost hypnotic digging sounds and quirky music add to the overall sense of calm and immersion. The visuals, while basic, have a playful and charming quality that makes the game fun to look at. Each layer you dig through brings new surprises, whether it’s a cool discovery or a random oddity that adds personality to the underground world.

Humor and Quirkiness: One of the standout features of "A Game About Digging a Hole" is its sense of humor. The game doesn't take itself too seriously and is filled with quirky, lighthearted moments that keep you amused as you dig deeper. It’s not about complex narratives or intense action; it’s about enjoying the absurdity of the situation and embracing the fun of discovery.

Final Thoughts: "A Game About Digging a Hole" is an experience like no other. It's calm, fun, and oddly satisfying, with just the right amount of weirdness to keep you entertained. Whether you're looking for a short escape or something to relax with, this game is a perfect choice. Digging has never been so fun!

[quote] They say the grass is always greener on the other side. In A Game About Digging A Hole, there is no other side — only deeper, darker, and somehow more satisfying. ⛏️🕳️ [/quote]
Hey everyone. The author takes no responsibility for any damage caused by their reviews. Any resemblance to other reviews is purely coincidental. This review is solely the author's opinion and you are always free to have your own! Thanks for understanding and happy gaming!

[hr][/hr]
[h1]📜 Description[/h1]
A Game About Digging A Hole is exactly what it says it is — and therein lies both its greatest strength and its most honest limitation. You dig. You sell. You upgrade. You dig deeper. There is no grand narrative twist waiting at the bottom, no secret world to discover, no elaborate systems hiding beneath the surface. Just a hole, your shovel, and the quietly hypnotic satisfaction of going further down than you did yesterday. For a certain kind of player — the kind who finds peace in repetitive, incremental progress — this is a perfectly crafted little experience. For everyone else, it is a charming curiosity that outstays its welcome before the dirt settles.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]🎨 Graphics & Sound[/h1]
The presentation is clean, unpretentious and well-suited to its subject matter. The real visual standout is the [b]dirt physics[/b] — genuinely impressive for a game of this scope, lending each dig a tactile satisfaction that elevates the core loop considerably. A handful of minor bugs exist, but nothing that meaningfully disrupts the experience.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]🎮 Gameplay[/h1]
The loop is as pure as it gets: dig, collect resources, sell them on the surface, upgrade your equipment, and descend further. A [b]jetpack[/b] and [b]lamp upgrades[/b] expand your mobility and reach as you progress, and [b]dynamite[/b] provides a satisfying solution to stubborn obstacles standing between you and the next layer. The upgrade path is enjoyable while it lasts — though it moves quickly and doesn't offer a great deal of depth before it runs dry.

The digging mechanic itself is genuinely addictive. There is something deeply satisfying about chewing through layers of earth, watching your equipment improve and your hole grow into something impressively deep. Fans of classics like [i]Motherload[/i] will feel immediately at home. The gameplay is undeniably repetitive — but for a mining simulator, that is largely the point, and it wears that repetition with confidence.

One persistent minor annoyance: [b]dirt remnants[/b] left behind during digging can occasionally obstruct movement in frustrating ways. A small thing, but noticeable enough to mention.

After completing the main descent, an [b]achievement mode[/b] opens up, offering completionists additional reasons to keep digging — though some achievements lean toward the tedious side of the spectrum. The ending itself, when it comes, is abrupt and underwhelming — a genuine missed opportunity to punctuate the journey with something memorable.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]📖 Story & Atmosphere[/h1]
Story depth is not on the menu here, and the game makes no apologies for that. The atmosphere is relaxed, low-pressure and quietly meditative — the gaming equivalent of a long walk with a shovel. If you approach it as a stress-relieving, casual experience rather than a narrative adventure, it delivers exactly what it promises. The hole is the story. The descent is the journey. That is enough — just barely.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]✅ Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*]⭐ Genuinely addictive and satisfying digging mechanic that nails its core loop.
[*]⭐ Relaxing, stress-free gameplay perfect for short, casual sessions.
[*]⭐ Impressive dirt physics that add real tactile satisfaction to every dig.
[*]⭐ Clean, polished performance with low hardware requirements.
[*]⭐ Great value for its price — easy to recommend at the cost of entry.
[*]⭐ Achievement hunting adds a layer of post-completion replayability.
[*]⭐ Achievements present for the dedicated collectors out there.
[/list]

[h1]❌ Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*]⚠️ Shallow upgrade system that runs its course faster than it should.
[*]⚠️ Lacks content and replayability once the main run is complete.
[*]⚠️ Ending is abrupt and disappointing — the journey deserved a better finish line.
[*]⚠️ Some achievements are more tedious than fun to pursue.
[*]⚠️ Dirt remnants left during digging can hinder movement in annoying ways.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]😈 Conclusion[/h1]
[i]A Game About Digging A Hole[/i] knows exactly what it is, commits to it completely, and delivers it with quiet competence. It will not change your life, challenge your intellect or linger long in memory after the credits roll. But for the hour or two it lasts, it offers a genuinely enjoyable, surprisingly addictive and thoroughly relaxing experience that is well worth its modest asking price. If you love mining simulators, find peace in repetitive progression loops, or simply want something low-stakes and satisfying to fill a casual evening — grab a shovel. The hole won't dig itself. Just don't expect too much waiting at the bottom.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]💎 Final Score[/h1]
[b]Overall: 7/10 ⛏️[/b]

- Le trou n'est pas assez profond, seulement 100m. 
En 4 heures avec la foreuse, j'ai enlevé l'intégralité de la terre du trou, c'est trop rapide.
- Le Jetpack est très peu maniable, une vraie purge.
- Le nombre d'améliorations est trop limité et s'acquiert trop vite. Arrivé à 50m/100 j'avais déjà toutes les capacités au max, ce qui fait que les minerais rares du fond ne servent à rien.
- Le détecteur ne sert pas assez, il faut mettre plus de trésors dans le trou pour qu'il soit plus utile. Au final, 2 clés, 2 mines et 2 valises c'est trop peu.
- Quel est l’intérêt de casser les roches volcaniques ou les pierres blanches à la dynamite si on peut les contourner ?
Cela fait perdre de l'argent surtout qu'elles ne contiennent/ne cachent rien.
- Les dynamites rebondissent sans arrêt, ce qui est vraiment pénible pou viser.
- Le trou devraient être au moins 2x plus large et faire au minimum 1000m de profondeur pour être challengeant.
L'idéal serait une partie où la limite est aléatoire.
- Quand on arrive aux taupes, je pensais qu'il s'agissait d'ennemis d'un palier intermédiaire à éviter pour continuer de creuser plus loin mais non. Cela pourrait être intéressant de pouvoir les tuer et continuer de creuser encore ; les 3 dernières taupes étant cachées vraiment beaucoup plus profond.

Au niveau de la rejouabilité :
- ll faudrait que les minerais multicolores servent à quelque chose.
On pourrait avoir un haut-fait par exemple où il faudrait tous les trouver.
- Un haut-fait pour avoir déblayé 90% ou + de la map.
- Des coffres supplémentaires à débloquer avec des clés.

[h1]Докопался… но до чего?[/h1]

[i]Копал я тут огород на 100 метров в глубину в надежде отыскать клад и что же я нашел? Может быть истинный смысл жизни? Или дату выхода третьей Халфы? Или великую тайну мироздания? Или ту самую канализацию, через которую можно идти захватывать ящеров с НИБИРУ? Нет, я открыл великую тайну того, что эта игра… ОЧЕРЕДНОЙ И НИЧЕМ НЕ ПРИМЕЧАТЕЛЬНЫЙ «ПЛЕЙС» ИЗ РОБЛОКСА, ЗА ВХОД В КОТОРЫЙ ЕЩЕ И ДЕНЬГИ ТРЕБУЮТ.[/i]

По факту это детище проходится примерно за 1-2 часа и представляет из себя «расслаблялку» на вечерок с некой ИНТРИГОЙ в конце. Да и, в следствии своей не очень большой продолжительности, выглядит игра как очередная демоверсия, за которую еще и деньги берут, что… в принципе недалеко от истины. Данное творение слепил один человек буквально за две недели, когда тот просто отдыхал от разработки другой расслабляющей «чиловарни» (это буквально история самих разрабов, с которой они поделились со всеми, когда игра вышла). Но, как мы знаем, все гениальное – просто, все высокодуховноинтеллектуальное искусство держится на пИнусах, а все самые высокооцененные элитарным критиками и эстэтами картины... нарисованы в Paint'e за десять минут, ибо даже такой незамысловатый проект умудрился получить нормальное такое внимание со стороны игроков. Заслуженно ли? Не, игра довольно приятная чисто покопать на фоне просмотра какого-нибудь документального фильма про борьбу Русов с ящерами. Но, опять же, зачем она, когда есть Роблокс?

[i]Хотя, если так рассуждать, то остальные игры и даром будут не нужны, когда существует РОБЛОКС! И ТОЛЬКО ПОПРОБУЙТЕ СКАЗАТЬ, ЧТО ЭТО НЕ ТАК![/i]

[b]Вложился… но куда?[/b]

Купил чувак такой домик, а там в огороде крестик стоит. Предвкушая того, что там будут сокровища (надо ж ипотеку как-то гасить на новоприобретенный дом), покупает новоиспеченный хозяин с ОЗОНа китайский «ЛопатоземлекопокопательныйНАТОР-3000» и начинает с ним копать дырку, параллельно сажая грядки с овощами.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3426716414

Копаем, копаем и понимаем, что сундук ДО САМОЙ МАТОЧКИ закопан. Благо по пути нам встречаются природные богатства разной степени ценности - от камней, до алмазов, с которыми можно получить определенный такой "гешефт" при их продаже. Однако в инвентарь помещается лишь определенное количество руды и при попытке вскопать больше при заполненном рюкзаке новая добытая руда тупо уничтожается. Надо постоянно копать и постоянно возвращаться назад, чтобы все имеющееся сбагривать.

[b]Просчитался… но где?[/b]

Наш «ЛопатоземлекопокопательныйНАТОР-3000» потребляет энергию и при ее исходе... вся накопленная в инвентаре руда теряется. Также природные богатства у нас исчезнут, если неудачно упасть и подвернуть себе ногу и тело в форму "Коловрата". Благо есть возможность восполнять потерянные энергию и единицы ХП за денюшки, а также, за счет них же нам надо постепенно прокачиваться для того, чтобы быстрее достичь цели. Можно постепенно превращать свой «ЛопатоземлекопокопательныйНАТОР-3000» в "БУРОПРОНЗАЮЩИЙНЕНЕБЕСААМИМОЛЕЖАЩЕЕGOVНОНАТОР-10000", увеличить количество энергии и ячеек в инвентаре, а также купить джетпак, чтобы быстро выбираться из выгребной ямы (он тоже требует энергию, кста), лампы для освещения и динамит для подрыва более обширных подземных камней.

Вся игра своими кором геймплея и простенькой графикой прям ощущается, как очередной "place" из Роблокса в жанре "tycoon" (в которых каждый школотронник делает свой бизнес и становится медиамагнатом), если я правильно помню. Ииии... это неплохо. Копается лопата приятно и прикольно. Прогресс ощущается, когда ты по началу еле выкапывал камушки, а далее ты прям уничтожаешь землю буром. Игра прям идеально подходит для расслабления или СДВГ активностей. Но РОБЛОКС ТО БЕСПЛАТНЫЙ, А ЭТА ИГРА КОРОТКАЯ И 200 РУБЛЕЙ С ВАС БЕРЕТ! ДУМАЙТЕ!

[b]Прошел это… но зачем?[/b]

И что же там в сундуке, ради которого мы, по ощущениям, свою Кольскую сверхглубокую скважину раскопали (Хотяяяяя, это я преувеличиваю. Максимум ямку для деревенского туалета раскопали и все тут). А таааааааааааам [spoiler]ничего нет и нас сжирают подземные кроты. Как бы… это ДЕЙСТВИТЕЛЬНО ТОНКАЯ аллюзия, которую НЕ ВСЕ ПОЙМУТ, а также ГЛУБОКИЙ СМЫСЛ, который БЫДЛО НЕ ВЫКУПИТ насчет того… что мы очередной ГОЙ и нас нае6али.[/spoiler]

А что делать после прохождения? Ну, есть тут достижение "ЗаСПИДораннить игру за полчаса" (вот настолько эта игра коротковатая). Или же, как и многие перфекционисты тут делают, можно раскопать все до основания. Ну знаете, тот самый челлендж проженных до мозга костей ТЕРРАРИстов, где они раскапывают все, чтобы ни одного блока в мире не осталось. Однако вспоминаем масштабы даже самой маленькой карты в Террарии и понимаем, что уже тут, в этой маленькой игре  разгуляться и поТЕРРАРИЗировать им уже будет особо негде. Да даже если бы Роблоксеры сделали подобную игру, то они бы надр1стали земли и природными богатствами тут в десятикрат раз больше и сделали бы проход в эту игру бесплатным, но с возможностью за РОБУКСЫ заиметь более быструю прокачку и скинчики. Так что копать тут прикольно, но особого смысла покупать эту игру я попросту не вижу из-за её коротковатости. Можно, конечно перезапускать игру по новой каждый раз, чтобы ещё на расслабоне покопать, но тогда опять будут заморочки с прокачкой, где ты по началу еле еле можно один камушек откопать и т.д. Однако, какой-никакой успех игры довольно заметен и, думаю, можно ждать обновлений, которые, МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ, и вернут меня в этот симулятор землекопа. А я, пока, пойду задротить в РОБЛОКС!
