I paid 5 dollars to do hard manual labor and enjoyed it immensely. It's oddly relaxing for what it is, and I had a good time planning out where to dig and how to place everything. I dug way more than I had to and had a great time. Not much replay value, sadly--once you unlock all the upgrades, there's nothing to spend your loot on, save healing and charging, which makes the end stretch feel a little dull. The ending was a fun surprise, though it'd be nice if you could use that You Know What for an alternate outcome. But, in the end, it's about the journey. It's worth at least one playthrough, and more than worth the price.

Once upon a time, in a yard so wide,
A man named Ben stood, shovel beside.
He scratched his head and tapped his chin,
And said, “Well now… let’s dig right in!”

The sun shone bright, the birds did sing,
As Ben prepared for his hole-digging fling.
Why dig a hole? No one quite knew—
Not even Ben, but he’d see it through!

He thrust his shovel, deep and true,
And flung the dirt—a messy debut.
Clods of soil flew left and right,
A worm screamed, “Hey! That ain’t polite!”

But then—clang! His shovel struck,
A chunk of silver—what good luck!
He pried it loose and gave a cheer,
“I'm rich! A miner's career is near!”

With newfound hope, he dug much more,
And soon unearthed a trove of ore—
Some copper, iron, even gold!
(And one weird rock that smelled of mold.)

He took his finds to town to sell,
And with the coins, he upgraded well.
A brand-new shovel, sharp and grand,
With diamond edges—best in the land!

With shovel mighty, strong and bold,
Ben kept digging through dirt and cold.
The hole grew wider, deep and vast,
His legend spread—his fame was fast!

But just as he settled, deep in his lair,
A whisper echoed—from under there…
The dirt began shifting, the walls caved in,
And something below gave a ghostly grin.

A dark passage, in eerie light,
Appeared beneath him, shining bright.
Ben gasped, his mind askew—
Had he just found... a portal through?

Then suddenly—crack! The floor gave way!
Ben tumbled down with no delay!
The wind howled loud, the world spun fast—
He reached for a ledge, but fell right past...

Down and down, through endless black,
No ground below, no turning back.
And as he fell, one thing was clear—
A voice below whispered, “You’ve dug too near.”

I love the game so far. I do enjoy digging, though I noticed some stuff that could use improvement (note, this is all my opinion, and I think the game is great as is anyway).

Secret area with no minerals - In the back of the yard, you can dig far behind the garden bed. This sin't a big problem, but for someone who is trying to dig out the whole yard, it is an annoyance. It doesn't give any minerals and it can't actually be fully dug out. I think it might be smart to block that area off.

Birds chirping is very pleasing when I drink my morning coffee, for about 10 minutes - The ambience of the game is enjoyable, but it can get old fast. I think it might be idea to add some music, and then make the sound sliders separate for the music, sound effects, and ambience.

Movement creates invisible walls - When you are moving in the game, you may want to check your inventory. However, if you do so, and are still holding the movement button, you may be surprised to find a lack of movement. When opening any of the menus in the house or your inventory, all movement keys that you're holding onto break until you let go. This isn't a huge problem, but I think allowing movement while accessing menus would be beneficial to the player.

It's difficult [i]not[/i] to recommend a game when the developer has put in some effort and it's relatively cheap. For example, €5 wouldn't be enough to buy a large coffee in some places here. While I understand that everyone's finances differ, I think it's a bit ludicrous that people complain about the price-to-time ratio. They'd have no problem buying a coffee for that money, but they think it's too much for a 90-ish minute game?! 

Anyway, the game itself... is fine. It scratches the dopamine itch of gradual progression. The issue is that the progression is relatively shallow, as you'll find yourself discovering the final bits of the game quite quickly, and the upgrades won't make you feel empowered until it's too late. However, it gives me the same vibe as other tedious but satisfying games like Powerwash Simulator. 

The ending has a twist, but from what I've read here, many players find it an insult rather than something rewarding. I'd be inclined to agree, but [i]honestly[/i]? I don't care that much. 

In sum, there are worse ways to spend your time and money. If you enjoy games with gradual progression and/or tedious satisfaction, then this game is for you. Just don't expect too much in return. This game's actual value is that it has signalled to the developer (and others) that a more in-depth and meaty version of this game would likely be successful.

Some real shovelware (haha). 

I had low expectations, but somehow a game about digging a hole (something I'm usually a big fan of in any context) disappointed. The digging isnt fun compared to almost any other game that allows it. It should be easy to trigger the ol' monke brain when digging random holes in the ground, but it just looked ugly here; very unsatisfying results despite my efforts to keep things neat. Holes are messy and floating bits of dirt, that are an annoyance to remove, constantly get in the way. Map is small (made smaller by annoying bedrock everywhere), and mostly empty. There's a few items/chests to find, but they only give you stuff you'll have an abundance of anyways.  Unsurprisingly there's no real challenge, just grind out the best gear to make digging faster, but with nothing else to do, you might as well finish the game well before then. 

Despite all that, for 5 bucks I wouldn't have complained if it wasn't for 2 things. The ending and achievements.
Spoilers. 

Ending sucks. Its a separate zone at the bottom of the map. You can't dig, You can't use your jetpack. You can't use dynamite. All you can do is briskly walk past some oversized moles to the empty treasure chest, and then die to said moles in the end cutscene. Felt very out of place and easily the lowest effort part of the game.

Achievements can't be unlocked until the second playthrough. I have no idea why. There isn't really anything new besides this on run 2. Maybe this is my fault, but upon reaching the end area and noticing that I hadn't unlocked anything yet, I figured I must have missed something. Spent way too much time looking for secrets around the map. Basically dug out everything and found nothing. I didn't expect to get every achievement on the first go, but the way its set up here just felt like the dev wanted to pad out the playtime of game clearly very sparse on content. Super obnoxious, and made me waste way more time on this game than it deserved. 

There are many games with better digging experiences. 
5 bucks is cheap, sure, but you could also dig holes outside for free if you wanted, and that never disappoints.

This isnt a game.

Its a simulator.

And its not a bad one, its a good one. For it to be a solo project of one guy in a very short amount of time, all code, assets and music in it by this one person, this is great work!

However while it is only 5 bucks (depending on your currency, it is 5 for me) it also feels like it just doesnt have enough to really justify the price. You notice that I said "Feels" right? Yea thats the issue here. Im conflicted about this one.

For one I played it for 2.5 hours and I got exactly what was advertised. I dug a hole, got treasure and dug to the bottom. But Ill be honest, thats literally all there is to the game. Your upgrades are not very varied. You have 4 to max out and by the time you have, you just... continue to dig for more treasure to sell. Which I suppose is kind of the point since its "buy this house and get rich" but then you have other games that did the very same and... they have more to do, more to go through, more to play with.

And some of them... ARE FREE.

Enter Motherload and Super Motherload. The latter of which is a practically sequel to the original flash games made entirely... FOR FREE. Well... the flash games are for free. The sequel isnt. However the sequel also has done far more than the flashgames. It adds storymoments, more gameplay, multiplayer and so on and so forth.

In comparison even by price this one feels... and this just honest feels just really crap to say... too expensive for what it gives you. Dont get me wrong. I dont regret buying this game for 5 bucks. It just doesnt feel worth 5 bucks if I had to recommend to anyone else.

I am a bit torn between feeling ripped off and having enjoyed my time with it. But for as much as it matters, unless you are into speedrunning, this game just doesnt have any replayvalue to offer. You can dig the hole once, dig the entire pit once and then also speedrun it. Thats it. There just isnt more to this.

A game about digging a hole in which you do exactly as its advertised. Least its not a scam. But at the same time 5 bucks just doesnt feel justified for the gameplay it provides when we literally have actually free alternatives that are, I really apologize to the solo dev cause again this is not at all a bad game, better in comparison.

---

This game needs more of... honestly everything. More upgrades, more tools, a detector you can USE after certains over it just being automatic, actual hole variations, endless mode for highscore cause Ima be honest... No one is gonna dig this hole more than once unless its for speedrunning or actually painful challenges. Makes for funny content on youtube. No one else is gonna do that.

“A Game About Digging a Hole” es una experiencia de juego sencilla pero profundamente entretenida. Su concepto, aparentemente simple, es sorprendentemente adictivo. La mecánica de excavar permite a los jugadores perderse en la tranquilidad del proceso, mientras descubren secretos ocultos bajo la tierra. El diseño minimalista y la sensación de progresión constante le dan una satisfacción gratificante en cada capa que se perfora. Además, el juego tiene una atmósfera única que puede ser relajante y desafiante a la vez, lo que lo convierte en una excelente opción para quienes buscan una aventura ligera pero envolvente. Definitivamente es un título que sorprende con su capacidad para enganchar y mantener la curiosidad.

This is a game where I wish Steam had a "meh" option.

The premise is nice. Dig a hole, get money, upgrade your stuff, dig a bigger hole. It's fun, I could probably play it for at least 5 hours if that was all the game was. I mean, hell, that's what I do in Minecraft and I probably have thousands of hours in that game.

But I can't recommend it simply because it's so short. Yes, it's five dollars. It's cheap. But if we're focusing on price of the product, World of Warcraft is $15 for a subscription and I can play for 50 to 100 hours on one month and still have stuff that I want to do.

This game should be priced at $2 at most. And that's not for a playtime price, that's an art piece price. 

I understand, I develop games as well. You put a ton of time into the product and want some return on investment. And that's entirely understandable! But for $5, you are putting yourself in the price range of things like Terraria. I understand Terraria is $10, but it is a ♥♥♥♥ ton more replayable and deep than this game. There are other games that will give you much more playtime and entertainment for a similar or cheaper price.

To the buyer: If you want a [b]SHORT[/b] (and I mean short) game about digging a hole, this is right up your alley. If you price things based on their worth as an art and not as a medium for entertainment, you might enjoy this. But if you are expecting a game that you can put some time into, this isn't for you. You will be extremely disappointed.

A Game About Digging A Hole is a game about digging a hole.

In A Game About Digging A Hole, you dig a hole. You start with a pointy stick that will mildly inconvenience the ground upon contact, exiling a small chunk of soil to the shadow realm, never to return. After repeatedly mildly inconveniencing the ground, you may have produced a small dip in the ground, or a series of tiny craters if you lack the neurological capacity to repeatedly mildly inconvenience the same patch of ground.

In this small, curious landscape feature, you may find rocks. If you collect them with your pointy stick, you may then sell them for a paltry sum of cash. With that cash, you can buy supplies, such as battery charge or suspiciously cheap healthcare, or more importantly, upgrades, such as a slightly pointier stick, or pockets to hold more rocks to sell.

With your slightly pointier stick, you may now noticeably inconvenience the ground, excising larger chunks of soil to a heckish existence in the shadow realm with each jab. With this, you can deepen your small dip in the ground into a small crater, which may yield more valuable rocks, which you can sell for more and buy better equipment, perhaps even replacing your pointy stick of gradually-increasing pointiness with an actual digging device, or a jetpack so you don't have to construct an elaborate transportation system between the surface and the dark, damp depths of your yawning abyss. With these improved tools, your digging ability improves astronomically, and you accept your new life as a mole-man, digging beneath the ground for rocks of increasing rarity and value.

But surely the yawning abyss must have a bottom... right..?

у игры свои плюсы и минусы:
Плюсы:

here's the thing, if you've seen ANYTHING about this game, you already know if you want to play it or not. its an incredibly basic premise. and without going into spoilers, the ending is exactly what you'd expect it to be. there is no surprise twist, there is no deeper intricacy to the game. what you see is what you get, from start to finish. so this is less of a review and more like customer feedback...

the only reason i give it a thumbs down is because there's a couple of, what i consider to be, glaring issues with this game. and since it was lucky enough to hit the streamer zeitgeist, the games garnered tons of positive reviews already. so i dont feel any need to offer a fake thumbs up in order to 'support an indie dev'. here are my problems...

1) the point of the game is to upgrade your tools so you can descend further, faster. but because there are so FEW upgrades to purchase, you will completely max out everything before the hole is even 15% of the way to the bottom. maybe if you're REALLY impatient and dont take time to dig around, you'll max out everything closer to halfway down. even still, this brings the fun to a grinding halt. instead of constantly working towards that next huge upgrade, the game very quickly becomes rote repetition. which is boring. instead of getting excited about finding a bunch of high value ore because it will help me reach another upgrade, it just means my $$$ will go up. whoopty-doo. which is made all the worse by my second point...

2) locking your achievements behind the second playthrough, without telling this to your player in advance, is a real ♥♥♥♥ move. nobody wants to play this game twice. once you've done the thing, you've done the thing. theres literally nothing to be gained from doing it again. its not even a 'New Game+', where you get to keep your upgrades or even purchase new ones. its literally just "play the game again". and all the effort you might've put into your 'first run' is basically wasted effort. i know not everybody cares about achievements, but if you're the kind of person that wants to, for example, dig the entire hole out...you wont be rewarded in ANY way. because there are no expensive upgrades to buy that might have been impossible to get otherwise, and you dont get achievements for your work. you're just doing it for the sake of doing it. i know it sounds like a dumb nit-pick, but this REALLY rubs me the wrong way because its a perfect example of not respecting the player's time. you've made the decision to waste my time on the first playthrough, and then EXPECT me to do another playthrough with ZERO changes from the first. why?? why would you expect someone to do that? its genuinely baffling. getting to the bottom of the hole already takes long enough that anyone who beats it wont be able to refund. so its not like you were trying to force people to keep playing the game. i dont get it. but its a terrible decision and you should really, really reverse it in an update to the game. that, or add a LOT more depth (no pun intended) to the second playthrough.

In the simplest words, this is the anti-clickbait game. What you see is what you get.  The entire game is just clicking to dig a hole that gets bigger and bigger.

For a lot of people, this isn't going to be their thing. However, for others like myself it scratches that perfect little itch in the back of our minds. You get a consistent ratio of upgrades to progress, and every step of the way down provides new (if small) things to do. While it would be neat if there were more upgrade options or things to do, I don't feel that was the point, and I can't be mad at the game for delivering on a single solid product that it focuses on solely.

If I did have to provide any particular complaints, I wasn't quite a fan of the shovels requiring constant clicking when you wanted to dig. I feel like you should have been able to hold down left click to let it keep digging, which WAS show to be possible given a later upgrade that gave you a new tool. Also I do think you can max out your upgrades a bit too quick, and I wish it would have taken a bit longer to reach max upgrades, maybe with just a few more extra payments to be made than the game required.

Overall I'd say this is a solid game. If you like treasure hunting and cave exploring, you'll enjoy your experience with this game!

Have you ever thought to yourself, "[i]I wish I could spend hours digging a hole in my backyard without my neighbors calling the authorities"[/i]? Well, good news, [i]A Game About Digging a Hole [/i] lets you do just that—without the risk of an awkward conversation with law enforcement.

You start as just a humble human with a dream and a tiny shovel, hacking away at the dirt like a toddler discovering the concept of "outside." At first, it's all innocent fun—finding little nuggets of ore, selling them for better tools, and upgrading your gear like some kind of entrepreneurial landscaper. Who knew a simple garden could be such a goldmine? 

But the deeper you go, the more things start to feel… off. The tunnels begin to twist in suspicious ways, and you get this nagging feeling that maybe—[i]just maybe[/i]—you’re not the only one digging this deep. You stumble upon a labyrinth, and it becomes clear that finding treasure isn’t the only thing on the agenda.  

In less than 4 hours, I reached the treasure. But let’s just say, I learned the hard way that sometimes, the journey is more rewarding than the destination—especially when the treasure is not exactly what I had in mind.

Alright, with that out of the way, [i]A Game About Digging A Hole[/i] is done and dusted. I think it's safe to say that this game has captured the interest and imagination of players around the globe. And even though you can't dig a hole to China or the U.S., you will be digging for a grandiose treasure said to be waiting in the depths of the yard you'll be digging in.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3429066783

The story set up is pretty simple. Some unnamed soul put up a "for sale" sign for the very house you will coincidentally be buying, lol. And talk about an amazing deal! They only want $10k for it and you are informed that there is also buried treasure in the back yard. [b]So excited were you at the thought of buying a house for the price of a dozen eggs (in today's market)[/b], that you failed to notice the numbers scratched into the for sale sign. Why have so many people moved out of this idyllic house?

And so, with your house secured and some special digging equipment in hand, it's time to get to digging. Conveniently, there is a big "X" painted onto the grass, and so you don't need to guess as to where you will start digging. You do have a special powered shovel to ease the burden of digging. But you need to be careful. If it runs out of power, it will explode. Nobody wants to see that happen. And, you also have a special metal detector that detects treasure and lost objects instead of metals when close enough.

Additionally, your garage/work room is outfitted with a computer to sell the different stones, gems, and metals you find. You also have a computer to buy and upgrade gear. Said gear is your trusty shovel, the battery capacity for your shovel, your backpack size (carrying capacity), and a jet pack as well! I guess that hole is gonna be every bit as deep as I implied earlier. You will also use this computer to heal yourself and refill your shovel's power bank. Last but not least, you can buy both dynamite and mining lights there as well. And to round things out, there is a book in your garage which functions as your manual save point. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3429357438

So, what are you waiting for? Get to digging!

The actual gameplay is pretty addictive. In addition to the digging and gathering materials to sell, which is already awesome; your jetpack also handles perfectly and is also pretty satisfying to use. But most important, your diggy diggy hole activities just got much easier after you purchase your third upgrade for your shovel. At that point, it switches from diggy digging to straight up Hoovering dirt and objects. I gotta say, that feels really good in use. Just don't stick your hand in front of it or put it on your cheek to check its sucking ability. Or wherever you were thinking of putting it... Don't do it. Resist the temptation.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3429485445

That's honestly the majority of the game until you actually reach the area where said buried treasure lies. There is a nice little surprise waiting for you down there. :)

Oh, one final note. The game tracks your actions, but most achievements don't actually drop until you start NG+, where any cheevos you've earned will all drop at once.

What's this game cost? $4.99? That's exactly the correct price. Only a minority of players are going to feel like their money was not well spent. You might be in said minority, but I doubt it. It's a fun and ridiculous game that took me a little under six hours to complete, but I also spent a lot of extra time widening out my hole in ways no hole was ever meant to be widened out. By that, I mean I also dug under the patio a bit. Absolutely worth a look. Fun and casual times await. 

p.s. The game is discounted on Humble at the time of this review and is sold out on Fanatical/GMG. :)

It's a nice minimalistic gameplay loop, perfect to have a "dwarven evening" and letting "diggy diggy hole" run on a loop. But while the story-finale on the bottom of the hole is giving it all an interessting twist, 

What's a bit unexpected is, that the game turns into a short (possibly very short) stealth game. Depending on your luck and affinity for hide and seek... um... I mean hide and run games, it's somewhere between kidsplay and "seriously?". 

The idea is okay, the twist storywise somehwat clever even... but what really rubbs me the totally wrong way is how it's done. Basically the whole gameplay established so far is just turned off without putting any visible creative effort into the "how" and "why" of it.

Your Drill? Doesn't work anymore. It just doesn't react anymore.
Your Jetpack? A text message tells you, that you can't use it.
Your Dynamite? A text message tells you, that you can't use it. Can't even take it into your hand anymore.

Why you can't use your Jetpack or even the dynamite, you might ask? The developer couldn't care less of providing an answer.

Your Lamps? <--- Well that single item shows how they should have done it with the other things too. It fizzles and burns out. Nice effect.
It would have been incredibly easy to find ways to explain why all but the Dynamite isn't working anymore.

[spoiler] How it could have been done:
Your whole equipment is ordered through the computer in the garage and comes likely from the same people who later fill in the hole again, when you're done. 

It would have been easy to put a warning sign against strong EM fields into the cave down there. Then add a wimpering soundeffect and some sparks to the drill, add something similar to the jetpack and both would have been explained.

Than put another warning sign in the cave that it's dangerously instable and fade to black if someone uses dynamite it in just like it's done if the stealth approach is failing.[/spoiler]

It would have been so incredible easy to make the end sequence fit into the short minimalistic but fun game. And this review might be a bit on the game design philosophy side, but after seeing that the developer obviously thought:

"Oh, let's just turn off the gameplay, ignore everything the player did and learned so far, let's just turn it off and change the game and not even take the time to put some effort in smoothing the edges of it all...." 

That's just a very bad attitude towards game design. That's totally careless towards the game experience and it makes me not wanna take even another look at the other games of this developer so I threw those which were already on my wishlist out of it.... buuut.... well.... this don't have to be your way of looking at it.

Searching for a minimalistic game to scratch that dwarven diggy hole mood? Take it. Be prepared that it's short but the price is fitting and there is even stuff to love on this game. Like the "Warning - You haven't saved your game for at least 30 minutes" message that visually (but not physically) blocks the door into the garden. The way that is done is just so great!

But if anything of the above also gets you onto the fence... well... then stay away from it and try something else.

“A Game About Digging a Hole” might sound simple—even absurd—but that simplicity is exactly what makes it brilliant.

From the moment you pick up your virtual shovel, you're drawn into a meditative, oddly satisfying loop of digging. Every layer unearthed holds its own charm, from the quirky sound design that makes each scoop feel tactile, to the subtle narrative woven through environmental clues buried beneath the surface. What starts as a mindless task quickly transforms into an introspective journey. Why are you digging? What will you find? Does the hole end, or does it simply keep going as a metaphor for our endless human pursuit of meaning?

The game balances humor and existential depth flawlessly. One moment, you're chuckling at the sheer absurdity of what you're doing, and the next, you're contemplating the futility—or beauty—of effort itself. And just when you think you've reached the bottom, A Game About Digging a Hole surprises you again.

Whether you play for 15 minutes or 15 hours, this game leaves an unexpected impact. It's not just about digging a hole—it's about what you discover along the way.

Highly recommended for anyone who loves quirky indie games, subtle storytelling, and, well, digging holes.

[i] I am a dwarf and I'm digging a hole, diggy diggy hole, diggy diggy hole! [/i]

Jokes aside, this game is a very chill, simple, and relaxing but takes a only few hours to do everything kinda game. it's in a similar vein to Power Washing Simulator in terms of its calming and fairly monotonous nature, but about digging instead of washing and with a fair few more mechanics. The main game takes only a couple hours or so to finish, but upon completion you unlock the ability to earn achievements which extends the game a bit (and of course if you're a dedicated completionist you can dig out the entire map lol). The real only negatives I can think of are it'd be nicer if it was longer and had more features, but with the way it is now it's still worth playing in my opinion.

An important warning (minor spoilers): the very end of the game does have a fairly dramatic shift in theme and gameplay from calming digging to mild horror (though no jumpscares), so if you're sensitive to frightening themes be warned. It's nothing too extreme but it can be rather terrifying at first if you're not expecting it. I personally liked it but it's definitely not going to be everyone's cup of tea.

The ending delivers a solid plot twist, which adds a nice touch to the journey.

That said, the game could be longer and offer more content. However, for just €5, it’s an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a fun and relaxing game.

なんか爆発的に人気になっていた穴掘りゲーム。
面白くはあったが、ものすごく良くできているからバズっているのではなく、バズっているからバズっていたゲームだった。
全人類に数％いる、穴を掘るのが好きな人類に上手く届いたという感じ。
そして自分もその一人であったらしく、遊び始めてからぶっ続けでクリアまで、そしてオマケの実績解除まで5時間遊び続けてしまった。

ゲームとしては、穴掘りゲームでありながらシステムはクリッカー系。素材を集めて売って金をためて装備をアップグレードさせて、新しい素材を集めて売って装備をアップグレードさせて… まさにクリッカー。穴掘りという無心要素とクリッカーという無心要素が合わさればそれはもう違法スレスレの中毒性になるのだった。

日本語対応しているようなので選択してみたら、まずオプションでフォントがバラバラだった時点で嫌な予感はした。
そして「トータルだ」「セーブゲーム？」「節約…」で乾いた笑いが出たあとに、スッと英語に戻した。
日本語翻訳なんてなかった。いいね？とは言え、言語が必要なゲームではないのでプレイには問題ない。

最初はスコップ片手にちんまりとした穴ひとつしか掘れないから正気ではないが、割とすぐにドリルが手に入り、ドリドリと庭に広大な洞窟を作れて楽しい。庭にある財宝を探す途中でダイヤがザクザク見つかるようになったらもうそこで満足して良いのではないかとは思った。

穴掘りゲームというから、庭の穴から地球の反対側まで行けるレベルに掘れるのかと思っていたが、割とコンパクトだった。
ただ、サイズとしてはなかなかちょうどよかった。あのシステムで1000mまで掘れたとしたら、地上に戻って来るのがだるすぎるゲームになってた。

ただまあ、他の人も言っているように、なぜか最後に突然ステルスホラー要素が出てきたのだけは最悪だった。Steamレビューではオススメにしてるが、人によっては絶対オススメしない。
それもあって実績の30分以内クリアをやる気がなくなってしまった。

After completing PowerWash Simulator, I was itching for another casual game where I can zone out and gradually progress and A Game About Digging A Hole is perfect. It even includes subtle lore.

Gameplay is simplistic yet fun and relatively relaxing. I honestly really enjoyed digging a big hole and going deeper. The experience is short, probably an hour or two, but I played through again for achievements and had a decent time.

I have a few complaints:
- There are minor graphical bugs which can make navigating the hole a little confusing at times but after a while you get your bearings and it's ok
- There are a few things to discover where you dig the hole but it was a real missed opportunity to have tiny cave systems to discover interesting items rather than just money.
- It's a bit too expensive for the experience. $7.50 AUD is a lot for a clicking simulator and there's not really enough of an enjoyable gameplay loop for the cost so I was a little disappointed. 
- The [spoiler] Old Crate [/spoiler] achievement. [spoiler] The first key was incredibly easy to find but the second one took me over 2 hours and was quite frustrating. Continuously digging out the entire area in search for a tiny object was not the greatest experience. [/spoiler]. That being said, there are community guides that can give you more direction but despite that it was still quite boring.

Overall, it's a decent game I would recommend to those wanting a simplistic experience of digging a hole. I would wait for a sale or a major update with some new features before purchasing.

unfathomably lazy engagement bait, id call it an asset flip but the assets are so low quality i honestly cant tell. there are good games about digging holes- the most profitable game [i]in the world[/i] is about digging holes. this is not one of them. it is uninspired default Unreal slop so barebones you can't tell if there was any meat on them to begin with. at best it is comparable to the most simplistic incremental games out there, except instead of making the numbers go up for you it forces you to keep engaging with the most mind numbing "gameplay" imaginable right up to the end, which mercifully comes soon enough to refund this waste of $5. 

i have to stress that the problem is not inherent to the concept of the game. even if nothing was changed about the stale gameplay loop at all, i could think of a dozen minor additions that would vastly improve the experience. heck, even technical improvements would help- like the use of an actual physics system, instead of allowing dirt specks to float annoyingly in empty space and loose ore to delete itself from existence. it's not like Unreal doesn't make this sort of thing readily available to even amateur developers! i can only speculate that the sudden positive reception of this "game" either comes from streamer-based irony poisoning, or artificial/paid engagement boosting. either way, it doesn't earn such success in any meaningful way. you could throw a rock on steam and hit a better indie game than this.

Okay, so I just needed something to tootle around with, something that would fill a bit of time, but not require a bunch to really get into. So, for $5, it's fantastic. The act of digging is just satisfying, and the upgrades give you a very noticeable boost, rather than a shovel that's 2% wider and a battery that's 1.5% more efficient. There's something cathartic about digging down through the ground, finding new materials, watching your profits soar as you get deeper and find better things to sell. If you want a real laugh, once you get the fully upgraded shovel, take it to the top layer of your yard and see just how plentiful those starting resources are.

That's the thing, though. Once you get down deep enough, you start grabbing diamond. Lots of diamond. I mean, you bought this house for $10k because there was buried treasure. Now you're pulling up well over that just from the minerals under your yard. Something seems a little funny about that.

A fairly short game, but a fun afternoon.  The balance of upgrades feels a bit off, as you quickly max out everything and then still have a good ways to go to the end.  Without any spoilers, the endgame is at -100m, so you can know how far you've still to go.  Also, why include a one time use teleporter if you can't use it when it really counts?

“Unerwartet fesselnd – Ein Meisterwerk des Lochbuddelns!”

Ich hätte nie gedacht, dass ein Spiel über das Graben eines Lochs so unterhaltsam sein könnte – aber hier sind wir. A Game About Digging a Hole nimmt eine simple Idee und verwandelt sie in eine überraschend tiefgehende (Wortspiel beabsichtigt) Erfahrung.

Die Steuerung ist intuitiv, das Gameplay meditativ, und bevor man sich versieht, steckt man Stunden in der perfekten Lochstrategie. Die Physik ist erstaunlich realistisch, und die kleinen Details – von der Beschaffenheit des Bodens bis zur Befriedigung, wenn ein großer Brocken Erde endlich nachgibt – machen das Ganze unerwartet immersiv.

Ein Spiel für Perfektionisten, Zen-Meister und all jene, die einfach mal entspannt in den Boden schauen wollen. Absolut empfehlenswert!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 – würde wieder graben.

To the unaided eye, A Game About Digging a Hole will probably appear an exercise in babyish simplicity, a computer simulation of digging manually that cannot be seen as having any depth. But look more closely—nay, subject it to the kind of radical epistemological deconstruction one would otherwise reserve for post-structuralist theory treatises—and it reveals itself to be a dialectical exploration of the very essence of existentialist drudgery.

Essentially, the game offers a Sisyphean reflection on the constant entropy of human labor. With each subsequent spadeful of dirt shoveled, the player is caught in an ouroboric loop of progress and pointlessness, an allegorical smallness of the capitalist dilemma wherein labor is both end and means. The seeming absence of traditional ludic reward—narrative progression, oppositional confrontation, or ultimate teleological terminus—opens into a metatextual deconstruction of gamification proper. By not using external motivators, the title compels the player to internalize the hollowness of task completion in its simplest form, thus becoming an unwitting critique of work as an end in itself.

The visual asceticism, seemingly the product of technical self-control, is in fact a deliberate act of defamiliarization, forcing the viewer to abandon familiar expectations of beauty and engage with the digital substratum in an unmediated, phenomenological manner. Soundtracklessness is particularly conic, bringing on an audio void which is the reflection of Beckettian absurdity where silence is as much present as the void itself—an abyss into which the player, as much as sight, instead constructs.

Mechanically, the game exists within its own austere ludic minimalism, where the action of digging as both single verb and reference point for experience constitutes the entire work. And yet, undergirding this mechanistic constraint is a profound condemnation of the reductionist tendency of contemporary game design—where complexity is mistaken for depth, and iterative mechanisms cloud rather than illuminate the thematic question at issue.

The case here might be that the fact that such a game exists at all is an acidic rebuke to the condition of games, in which acquisition narratives, victory narratives, and electronic hyperreality dominate more contemplative engagement with primal human action. In this interpretation, A Game About Digging a Hole might best be the electronic equivalent of Duchamp's Fountain, dadaist rejection of interactivity conventions per se.

In short, A Game About Digging a Hole is less a game than an ontological detour into the abyss of purpose, labor, and recursive human want. It is either an ascetic experiment in game design, an inadvertent masterpiece of high satire, or simply the delirious work of a developer inebriated on their own hubris, but one thing is certain—it is a hole, and it is being dug.

Final Verdict: 10/10, a work of unimaginable sophistication, to be misunderstood by lesser minds.

Dieses Spiel habe ich zu aller erst auf "Social Media" gesehen, bevor ich mir das Game vor ein paar Tagen selbst gekauft und inzwischen mehrfach durchgespielt habe. Das Game sah sehr witzig aus und erinnerte mich direkt an Games wie "PowerWash Simulator", fragt nicht warum. Ich habe wirklich keine Ahnung. Jedenfalls hatte ich mir direkt in den Kopf gesetzt, dieses Spiel durchzuspielen zum einen wegen den Errungenschaften und zum anderen, um so absurd wie sich das auch anhören mag, einmal die ganze Erde aus dem Loch zu entfernen. Beweis dafür gibt es in meinen Screenshots :3

Das Spiel "A Game About Digging A Hole" wurde vom Entwicklerstudio "Cyberwave" entwickelt und bereits im Februar diesen Jahres veröffentlicht. Alles fängt mit dem Kauf eines neuen Hauses an, in dessen Garten ein angeblicher Schatz versteckt sein sollte. Diesbezüglich fangen wir dann auch direkt an mit dem Umgraben seines Gartens. Auf dem weg nach unten findet man ein bis zwei Geldkoffer, 2 Schlüssel und noch ein paar alte Minengänge, in denen Kisten versteckt sind. Um nicht all zu viel zu Spoilern, kürze ich nun das buddeln im Loch an der Stelle ab und überlasse es euch selbst herauszufinden, was in den tiefen eures Gartens lauert. So viel sei gesagt, es ist nichts für schwache Nerven. Wie dem auch sei, was dort unten ist und wie das Spiel ausgeht ist auch für mich sehr erstaunlich gewesen. Diese Entwicklung hätte ich nicht erwartet. Die einzelnen Erze welche man über die Zeit ausgräbt, kann man auch in seiner Garage verkaufen und wieder direkt in besseres Equipment investieren. So ungefähr sieht dann das gesamte Gameplay aus, bis man sein Ziel erreicht hat. Was ich dennoch an dem Gameplay etwas schade fand ist die Tatsache, dass die Errungenschaften erst nach einmaligem durchspielen aktiviert werden. Grafisch ist das Spiel jedenfalls ganz okay und gleicht mit der heutigen Grafik der meisten kleineren Simulatoren. Der Spielspaß ist ganz zufriedenstellend, kann jedoch auf dauer sehr stark abnehmen, da das Gameplay auch sehr monoton wirken kann. Die Steuerung wurde gut umgesetzt und beschränkt sich auf die notwendigsten Funktionen. Das Spiel besitzt zum aktuellen Zeitpunkt 10 Errungenschaften zum freischalten und kostet gerade mal 5€ auf Steam. Das Preis Leistungsverhältnis ist durchaus akzeptabel.

Ich muss ehrlicherweise gestehen, dass mir das Game sehr gut gefallen hat und hoffe, dass die Entwickler sich vielleicht noch ein paar Gedanken machen, was man noch dem Spiel an Features hinzufügen könnte. Ich für meinen Teil, wünschte mir vielleicht ein paar "Schrott-Objekte" (bspw. ein verrostetes Fahrrad, Blechdosen, Knochen, etc.), welche man dann für ein wenig Geld verkaufen könnte. Weitere Maps währen natürlich auch wünschenswert. Das Spiel bekommt definitiv einen Daumen nach oben und ich freue mich schon auf baldige Updates. Macht euch einfach ein eigenes Bild davon. Müsst ihr wissen.

The game itself is only bare minimum. It feels more like a demo of a main mechanic that yet still lacks the depth of a fully fledged game. For me, this game with it's simple promise of letting you dig a hole scratches a very satisfying itch i have when it comes to investing time and interest into something. There is basically nothing of substance but the fact that you're digging into your lawn, selling materials you find along the way to upgrade your digging tool to make it easier and more productive to dig deeper. Rarely, some kind of compass pops up as a handheld gadget that gives you hints to nearby secrets as you keep digging. Unfortunately, right now as mentioned the area to explore is very limited and lackluster of any real treasure to be found. If you like games like Crime Scene Cleaner, where you meticulously remove blood stains, you basically remove dirt. It is satisfying, every cave is unique and the urge to clean out every single last patch of dirt is there, i hope they build on this and come up with something cool to go along with this little idea of a game.

[h2]도전과제 수집 난이도 : ★☆☆☆☆[/h2]

└ 최소 필요 회차 : 2회차 (+a)
└ 요구 사항 : 특수조건 달성
└ DLC 필요 여부 : 없음
└ 최소 플레이타임 : 4시간


보물상자를 찾기 위해 집 앞 마당을 파고 들어간다는 내용의 게임입니다.

단순히 땅을 파고 광석을 팔아 업글을 하는 과정의 반복이지만, 삽질하는 소리가 나름 ASMR같기도 하고 이것저것 찾는 재미도 있어선지 유튜브 보면서 재밌게 했습니다.

도전과제는 개수도 적고 난이도도 굉장히 낮아 편히 즐기시면 되겠습니다.


[i]-- 오직 도전과제 수집에만 초점을 맞춘 리뷰, 스포일러 주의 --[/i]


1) 우선 가장 깊은 곳까지 땅을 파서 엔딩을 봅니다. 이 과정에서 할 수 있는 돈 모으기, 광석 캐기, 광석 부수기, 삽질하기, 다이너마이트 쓰기 등을 충분히 행사합니다.

1회차 엔딩을 보고 나면 도전과제 습득 모드가 열리고, 1회차 때 달성 횟수가 충족되어 달성된 도전과제가 있다면 2회차를 시작하자마자 한꺼번에 과제가 습득됩니다.


2) 이제 2회차를 진행하며 여러가지 기믹 도전과제를 습득합니다.

▶ 무지개 (Rainbow) : 땅을 파다보면 무지개빛으로 빛나는 광석이 있는데 이걸 5개 수집합니다.

▶ 긴 추락 (Long fall) : 일단 최심부까지 일직선으로 땅을 팝니다. 중간에 걸림돌이 없다는 가정하에 마당에서 최심부까지 일직선으로 떨어지면 0.1초가 부족해서 도전과제를 습득할 수 없습니다. 때문에 구멍에서 부스터를 사용해 천장에 바짝 붙은 후, 아래로 살짝 내려가다가 부스터를 다시 사용해 오르는 탄성을 받았을 때 손을 뗍니다. 이렇게 부족한 0.1초는 오르는 탄성으로 채워지게 되고, 최심부에 떨어지는 순간 도전과제가 습득됩니다.
  
▶ 낡은 상자 (Old crate) : 업그레이드를 하는 창고 구석에 보면 열쇠가 2개 잠긴 상자가 있습니다. 이는 구멍을 파고 내려가는 도중 종종 보이는 바위를 다이너마이트로 부수면 등장합니다. 이 중 1개는 레이더에 걸렸고, 나머지 하나는 아무 바위나 부수다 나왔으므로 랜덤일 가능성도 있겠습니다.

▶ 스피드런 (The fastest) : 30분 안에 엔딩을 보는 스피드런 과제입니다. 최우선 목표는 삽을 최대한 빠르게 업그레이드하여 드릴로 바꾸는 것이고, 너무 깊히 내려갔다면 굳이 다시 등반하지 말고 살자를 하여 복귀하는 것이 시간을 아낄 수 있다는 점을 기억하시면 됩니다. 저는 정 가운데보다는 오히려 구석에서 공략을 했는데, 몇몇 바위를 제거하는 것 말고는 거침없이 내려갈 수 있었기 때문에 나중에는 전등도 붙이지 않고 드릴로 계속 아래만 파고 있었을 뿐이었습니다.

2회차만에 모든 과제를 따내고 싶다면 먼저 스피드런 과제부터 진행한 후에, 메인 메뉴에서 계속하기를 눌러 나머지 과제를 습득하시면 되겠습니다. 


※ 추신 : 전 어쩌다보니 3회차를 진행했는데, 드릴 가지고 놀다가 벽이 뚫리는 버그가 걸려서 궁금해서 그냥 날아서 내려가봤더니 엔딩존이 있어서 7분 만에 깨지는 어처구니 없는 사건이 터지고 말았습니다. 유튜브 영상을 보니 이걸 이용해 1분 만에 깨기도 하고 그러네요. 스피드런 도전과제가 힘드시다면 참고하시면 될 것 같습니다.

Listen up you absolute dirt merchants. I've spent 47 consecutive hours analyzing the quantum mechanics of this $4.99 masterpiece of hole creation, and I'm about to drop some knowledge that'll make your brain leak out of your ears.

CORE MECHANICS (FOR ABSOLUTE BEGINNERS WHO PROBABLY CRY AT NIGHT)
First thing you need to understand is that this isn't just about clicking your mouse like some kind of degenerate cookie clicker enjoyer.
You're literally excavating your way to enlightenment. Your starter shovel is basically a plastic spoon from a prison cafeteria, but that's part of the JURNEY.

ADVANCED STRATS (REAL ONES ONLY)
The jetpack isn't just for looking cool - it's literally the difference between being a beta ground-dweller and an alpha hole warrior.
Max that bad boy to 80 strength and you'll be bouncing around like a crackhead at a trampoline park.

Here's where the REAL min-maxing comes in:

THE ECONOMY (WAKE UP SHEEPLE)
You think those floating ore pieces are just random? WRONG. The game's internal economy is more complex than the Federal Reserve's money printer. When you find hollow spaces, that's basically free real estate.
The moles? They're basically the underground IRS, and you need to treat them as such.

BATTERY MANAGEMENT (FOR INTELLECTUAL WARRIORS ONLY)
Your battery isn't just some arbitrary number - it's a representation of your LIFE FORCE. Keep it between 800-1600 or you're literally throwing away potential.
I've done the calculations, and if you're not optimizing your battery-to-dig ratio, you might as well be playing Hello Kitty Island Adventure.

THE SPEED META
Want to get that sub-30 minute clear? You need to become one with the hole. I'm talking PURE FOCUS. No bathroom breaks.

No crying. No calling your mom. Just you, your shovel, and the sweet embrace of the void.

Remember: The game auto-saves every 30 minutes because it knows you're too busy optimizing your dig patterns to remember basic human functions.

FINAL THOUGHTS (FOR THE ENLIGHTENED)
At the end of the day, it's literally just a game about digging a hole.
But if you're not treating it like it's the most important thing in your life, are you even gaming?

Highly recommended quirky and a quite unexpectedly unique game that, for me, taps into that inner child desire to dig and explore with the hope of finding something awesome. This was a thoroughly fun 5 hours. Warning: This game will also tap into any OCD tendencies you may have (PowerWash Simulator players beware) to clear every last piece of dirt (which will (spoiler alert) not pay off, but may be satisfying regardless. With that I have a few suggestions for the game if anyone is listening.

---------------------
Spoiler Alert Below
---------------------
Upon finishing the game, honestly I felt a little let down. First of all., this game is supposed to be all about finding rare things below the surface. They give you two different gadgets that let you know when you're close to something to find., but that happens, I think maybe a total of 5 times in the game, two of which are identical. They tease you early on with finding a small mine with treasure.. but that's the only time you have an experience like this. Most of the other finds are just satchels filled with money. Also the end sequence is weird with these strange moles that are easy to outrun just to get to the ultimate treasure, then it's just over. Nothing fun or exciting. It only unlocks the ability to get achievements, which in my opinion should be available from the get go. I shouldn't have to finish the game to start completing achievements. Give me new better achievements on round 2, but don't prevent me from getting basic achievements while playing the game the first time.

------------------------------------------------------
A Few Suggestions to the Team (if they read this :)
------------------------------------------------------
- First and foremost, I think you have an incredible platform to create something absolutely and unexpectedly amazing. Something that on the surface seems like just a simple game about digging a hole could lead to tremendous adventure.. think about thinking you're just digging for treasure, but end up discovering a doorway to a buried lost city and the entire story changes into something more impactful and intriguing and takes on a possibly whole new focus/goal. Alternately, it could be fun to open up holes in the shaft walls that allow you to dig below neighbor's houses to find other treasures. If nothing else consider updating the finds underground to be possibly a 6th level enhancement to your gear, or new gear (think plasma drill, juggernaut jetpack (destroy any destructible objects on impact), etc.) you couldn't buy in the store. It's cool finding some money, but all that does is help you buy more stuff that you already have access to. I gathered most all of the ore in the game early on and I had around $60k on top of completing all my upgrades by the end. That's too unbalanced imo, or if you don't want users to be able to do that, find new mitigations to prevent them clearing the whole map, and getting all the ore.
- Left over particles: I would recommend setting a threshold on particle size of remaining dirt. Each shovel dig and drill has a potential to leave small chunks of dirt that still have full impact to the user. I did a nearly full clear of the shaft and many times on decent I landed on a left over dirt particle that was about 1/2" thick (or less) and I lost a bunch of health or I got stuck. It would be good that either particles clear themselves if they are smaller than a certain size., or just any particles that are not connected to anything else automatically get removed. Clearing these left overs would also greatly appeal to the OCD crowd :) If anyone is like me, I'm trying to get a perfectly clean shaft down to the bottom
- Reactive Physics: This might be a big lift, but I think any form of reactive physics would be a great addition., i.e. minerals and boulders falling when they no longer have a connection to anything. Floating rocks are weird, at least make sure all rocks have a connection (static) to the side wall for realism.
- It would be cool if the upgrade table could include upgrades to your armor/gear that could pad against fall damage and hear resistance against the fire rocks. This would give you more items for people to work towards and spend their money on.
- It would be great if the teleport to surface gadget is something you earn for the game. I don't understand why this is a one time use..
- It would be great to introduce bandages or healing packs that allow the user to heal while in the shaft (unless this was intentional to build suspense in later parts of the game where the lava rocks could mess you up.
- If you're introducing environmental obstacles such as the lava rock, it might be good to also include poison, explosive, steam vents, etc. that could make the decent even more treacherous, but again, as stated in my first bullet point, it might be cool if this coincides with new environmental discoveries. This might be good to do something similar to Subnautica where each level is more or less a new Biome with new environments and new environmental hazards.

Feedback:
- After you finish the game, it lets your start new game where you can unlock achievements, but I think these achievements should have been there from the start. Maybe some people find replay value in the act of digging for the sake of it, but for me I liked working towards the ending. Speaking of the ending, I liked it.
- The game could've benefited from better sound design, maybe some soundtracks to make the deeper layers more atmospheric. Also, I had to turn off the sound effects because the shoveling sound was too repetitive and I got tired of it. 
- I think there could've been a bit more content, maybe some more upgrades. I would have loved if there were collectible items scattered in the dirt, and when you pick them up they each tell a part of some story.
- When you dig, often time there's leftover spots of dirt floating midair, you get stuck on them and it makes the movement awkward because you can't see them too well. At this point, the Game-About-Digging-a-Hole genre is [i]crowded[/i]. Surely, we don’t need another entry. But [i]A Game About Digging a Hole[/i], pours dirt all over the dozens and dozens of other hole-digging games, and buries them in the holes they’ve dug for themselves.

Now, you might think you know exactly what sort of hole-digging game you're getting into with [i]A Game About Digging a Hole[/i], but I'm here to tell you: you do. It’s exactly that game. Undoubtedly, this is the most game about digging a hole ever made.

It is, without question, a game in which you dig a hole. But what kind of hole? The choice is yours. Sort of. Mostly. The hole-based mechanics have limits. Don't worry though, after just a few minutes, you’ll be grateful for the absolute lack of distractions like “gameplay variety.”

The hole grows, and with it, your sense of accomplishment—or existential dread. Yes, there’s a progression to your digging, but who needs that? Who needs anything more than the solemn, unrelenting reality of soil displacement? In an era of bloated mechanics, A Game About Digging a Hole dares to ask: What if we just dug a hole? And, critically: What if we kept digging?

The soundtrack? Whatever you bring with you—the rhythmic scrape of a shovel, the soft thud of dirt, the quiet realization that this is all there is. The ending? Inevitable.

This game doesn’t just simulate digging a hole; it becomes the hole. And by the time you’re done, you may find yourself staring into the void of your screen, wondering if the real hole was the friends you made along the way. Either that, or the hole was inside you all along—and for about 130 minutes, A Game About Digging a Hole lets you forget that.

First of all, do I think this game is worth it? 

- Yes

Now, everything else:

There is a lot of promise to this game with how everything is structured and developed. The concept and idea around this makes it easy on the brain and just enjoyable overall. While yes, the comments that talk about the game being limited in content are not wrong, I am sure there would be greater development to come, especially now as they are getting money and support from us players.

I managed to get all the achievements in around 3 hours (There are only 10 achievements at the moment though) but its a nice feeling completing all the achievements set for this)

I would like to see in the future:

More upgrades:
- Maybe a heat proof jacket/clothing, a mechanic where the deeper you go, the hotter it gets. Something else to watch out for and spend money on.

- As there is a jetpack, why not include a revers situation where you could upgrade the jetpack so much that when you fly high enough, you then have a secret/bonus area to start digging upwards.

- Multiple endings? By getting enough resources/special material it could unlock other endings, maybe you can dig further down and find more stuff and other entities.

- [spoiler]A way to defend/attack the creatures from below rather then just having to try and run around them[/spoiler]

-  A few bug fixes such as the lights staying up when you destroy the back of the surface it is set up on.

But other than a few tweaks and what not, I think this could go so much further with what they have for a baseline already. Keep up the good work Devs!

This game is pretty much perfect.

I discovered the game through a YouTube video and all I needed to watch was the first 14 seconds to be sold. I'm normally not crazy about AAA games or big budget studio $80 blockbusters so this game spoke to me instantly. I don't love games that are overly complicated or do more than they should, and thankfully this game doesn't do that.

The sort of Unity Engine game where you can work at your own pace with one mission in mind is a certain type of game that speaks to me in spades and I seriously have 0 complaints when it comes to "A Game About Digging A Hole". The experience is perfectly paced, perfectly explained, and perfectly priced. Players are going to want to dig a hole and I'm proud to say that you can start digging right out the gate.

I sincerely hope some DLC or some sort of expansion comes to this game, but I also find charm in it's minimalism. Either way this game was a very satisfying experience and seriously ticked each of my video game boxes perfectly. If you're thinking about playing this, please do!

땅을 파면서 들어가면 필연적으로 어두워진다. 이 어두움과 앞에 뭐가 있는지 모르는데서 오는 공포가 상당하다. 상점 페이지 홍보 영상에서 굴 같은 곳에서 괴물 소리가 들려오는 장면이 있지 않은가? 그래서 땅을 파다가 빈공간(어두움)이 갑자기 등장하면 시끄러운 삽질을 멈추고 구멍 너머에서 들려오는 소리에 집중하게 된다. 깊이가 깊어질 수록 무서운 소리가 들린다.

2회차 플레이 시, 새로운 공포를 느낄 수 있다.
그것은 배터리가 부족해서 느끼는 공포다. 올라가다가 몸 어딘가가 땅에 걸려서 배터리가 쭉쭉 다는 걸 보면 식은땀이 절로 난다.
구멍을 넓게 파자.(이건 1회차 때도 마찬가지) 상점 페이지 홍보 영상을 다시 봤는데, 한 번에 시원하게 다이빙 하는 거 어케 했ㄴ ?

평가에 이래저래 비판이 많지만, 나는 끝까지 손에 땀을 쥐고 플레이 했다. 공포 게임에 자신이 없고 망설임이 많은 사람이 플레이하기에 딱 좋은 게임이다. 애초에 귀신으로부터 닷지하고, 파피 플레이 타임을 즐기던 사람에게는 그 정도를 기대하라고는 말하기 어렵다.

이런 게임은 스포를 당하면 재미가 떨어지니 리뷰를 그만 훑어보고 당장 플레이하도록 하자. !!

플탐은 1시간으로 짧다. 
게임도 매우 직관적이다.

[olist]
[*]땅을 판다
[*]광물을 캐서 판다
[*]장비를 업그레이드 한다
[*]더 깊이 들어가서 더 귀한 광물을 캔다
[/olist]

그저 이뿐이다. 
이런 직관적인 구조는 이해하기 쉽고 빠르게 적응할 수 있으며 이는 노가다 게임으로서의 강점이다.
이러한 직관적인 구조와 함께 게임 자체도 나름 재미있었다. 광물을 찾고 보물상자를 발견하는 과정까지 시간가는 줄 모르고 플레이 했다.

문제는 엔딩이 너무 허무했다.
노가다 게임임에도 성취감을 느낄 수 없는 엔딩이었다.
또한 도전과제를 위해서는 엔딩을 본 후에 새게임을 해야하는 구조다.
다시말해 엔딩을 클리어하면 "업적모드"가 생기는 구조인 것이다.
업적모드는 뭐냐? 그냥 트로피 선반하나 생기는게 끝이다.
새게임임에도 전회차 계승같은건 없다.
업적이 그리 흥미로운 것도 아니다. 그저 땅을 얼마나 파기, 돈을 얼마나 얻기 정도의 보상이다.
노가다 게임을 좋아하고 플레이도 흥미로웠으며 재밌었지만 나는 이 게임을 하면서 성취감을 얻지는 못했다.
노가다 게임의 이유는 긴 노가다 이후에 얻는 성취감이라고 생각하는데 그 부분에서 내 기대치에 못 미쳤던 것 같다.

[h1]Worth $5 and a few hours to 100% if you like [i]Powerwash Simulator[/i] type games[/h1]

Sometimes, the appeal of a videogame is knowing that you'll experience the end of it. There's nothing groundbreaking (ironically) about AGADAH, it's just a charming, scrappy first-person-excavation game taking place entirely in and underneath some rando's backyard.

The presentation is quite basic; there's no music for the bulk of gameplay - I put on the Minecraft OST to listen to in the background. The terrain deformation mechanics are adequate but unimpressive  - bits of ground stay hovering in the air even with nothing anchoring them, and I had more than a few instances of small bits of terrain (only a few pixels thick!) inflicting fall damage, interrupting what should have been a freefall.

But you know what? I bought this game to dig a hole, and I dug a hole, and I enjoyed it. I enjoyed it so much that I fired up a new game to get the speedrun and other assorted achievements.

I 100%'d AGADAH in about three-and-a-half hours, and found it to be worth my time and my money. It's no GOTY, it might not even be the best game you play this month, but it's a fine palette cleanser, with a price point to match.

Recommended.

Overall, very fun if you want to live your childhood fantasy of digging a hole so deep you need a jetpack to fly out of it.

 - It is too short and shallow; You never actually get to do anything interesting with the mechanics and the upgrades are pretty basic.  - it does not respect the player; The entire game is just a long-winded setup for a troll ending.
 - it does not respect the classics it rips off. Otherwise you'd be able to blow the moles sky high just like Mr. Natas in the Motherload.

**Review: A Game About Digging a Hole**

If you're looking for a surprisingly delightful gaming experience, "A Game About Digging a Hole" might just be the ticket! What starts off as a simple concept—digging a hole—quickly draws you into a captivating journey where each layer reveals something new, both literally and metaphorically.

At its essence, the game is all about, you guessed it, digging a hole. Sounds easy, right? But as you dig deeper, the game-play unfolds in unexpected ways. What might seem like a laid-back activity soon evolves into an intriguing adventure, full of surprising twists. The mechanics are super accessible: you’ll dig through layers of soil, sand, and rock, gather resources, and uncover hidden treasures beneath the surface, and then pay to upgrade your tools!!

The art style is charmingly minimalist, with a nostalgic pixelated design that invites you to focus on your digging delights. The music and sound design beautifully complement the visuals, transitioning from soothing and serene to a gently intense vibe as you uncover more layers.

There’s a delightful mystery surrounding the hole you're digging, as every new layer introduces new surprises, quirky creatures, and odd artefacts. The further you go, the more intriguing—and slightly unsettling—it becomes, tapping into our natural curiosity about the unknown. Honestly I was a bit scared to find out, but I really enjoyed it when I did!! It leaves a lot to the imagination which honestly makes me happy, because now I can hypothesise the meaning to what I found!!

**Final Thoughts:**
"A Game About Digging a Hole" is a fun little game to pass the time, I really enjoyed the experience and the ending was pretty good too. If you want to be on edge for a good 2.5 hours only to laugh about it later, this is a great game for you. Simple and Rewarding.

A Game About Digging a Hole – A Surprisingly Addictive Journey

"A Game About Digging a Hole" is exactly what it sounds like—a hole-digging simulator. But don’t be fooled by its simplicity; there's something strangely satisfying about the experience.

You start off digging at a painfully slow pace, gradually collecting ores that you can sell for upgrades. These upgrades let you dig faster, carry more, stay underground longer, and even acquire a jetpack. Along the way, you'll uncover hidden treasures and secrets—trust me, it’s a long way down. This hole is massive, and reaching the bottom is no small feat.

Without giving away any spoilers, I will say this: the ending is absolutely worth the grind. My first playthrough took me about an hour, and after finishing the game, I unlocked the ability to chase achievements. I ended up spending another 2–3 hours collecting them all, and honestly, I enjoyed every minute of it.

This is the perfect game to unwind with after a long day. If you need something mindless yet engaging—something to help you shut your brain off and just relax—this is it. You might start off just digging a hole, but along the way, you'll find more than just treasure.

Happy digging!

a game about digging a hole isnt too terribly complex; you dig a hole to find treasure. however, the ending of this game has a very philosophical statement about greed and avarice. throughout the course of any playthrough, the player should certainly encounter thousands of dollars worth of ores and gems, which they shall certainly use to purchase better equipment in order to make the hole deeper to reach the treasure promised at the bottom of this back yard. keep in mind, the opening cutscene shows the house was purchased at $10,000. Ignoring any possible loan that may have been taken out for this and assuming a straight purchase, the player could easily recuperate the cost of the house and even make a significant profit without even making it to the diamond level, of which each diamond is worth $1,000 so only ten would be needed to break even an there are many more than ten. but as we all know, as gamers or simply as humans certainly driven by greed, that rather than make our profit on the easily tangible gems and ores in our sight we yearn for, seek out and claw our way to the treasure unseen. the tragedy of this game plays off of this innate human urge, as when you finally reach your promised treasure chest, it is empty. the moles, whom you had to avoid to get to the end, had planned for this from the very beginning. they hunger, and they understand hunger. they know that the easiest meal is not on that you claw for, fight tooth and nail for, but rather the one that walks itself into your maw. we are that meal. the moles understood that we are driven by a hunger not unlike their own, but that ours would lead us to great lengths to satisfy. the knew this, used it, and abused it. tens of men came before us and share our fate at the hands of the beasts that lay at the bottom of this game about digging a hole.

Este juego es la representación gráfica del placer, un lugar de descanso para los chino farmers que lo único que desean en esta dura vida es cavar libremente agujeros. Este perfil de jugador es un enfermito? Si, me incluyo en el, y con muchísimo orgullo. 
Nunca os ha pasado que vais dando un paseo por el campo, y os preguntáis que habrá debajo de toda esa tierra? Fósiles, auntigüedades, objetos perdidos, millones de años enterrados en KILOS y KILOS de tierra. Eso es esta juego. Nuestro personaje compra una casa muy barata, y por alguna razón decide que quiere cavar en el jardín, vamos lo típico que cualquiera haría. El caso es que una vez empiezas, no puedes parar, y ahora lo más importante de tu vida es cavar solo un poquito más, pero ese poquito se vuelve infinito de cojones. Probablemente tendrás ganas de seguir y seguir para saber que hay en lo más hondo.
Lo adictivo de todo esto es que empiezas a cavar con una pequeña palita, que hace una mierda de agujero que te desespera porque no avanzas nada. Y como se avanza? Bien, empiezas a vender estos materiales y con ese dinero empiezas a obtener mejoras, de la pala, hasta llegar a convertirla en un taladro como un demonio que no deja ni un gramo de tierra, y esto te hace sentir un progreso muy muy satisfactorio. Además el numero de materiales que puedes llevar en tu inventario es limitado, por lo que también nos interesa bastante mejorar nuestra mochila cada vez más para no tener que volver al almacen 1.000.000 de veces. A medida que vamos avanzando vamos encontrando minerales cada vez más caros, por lo que a más dinero, más mejoras.
Lo guapo es que además de todos estos minerales también encontraremos tesoros escondidos, que contienen dinero, objetos y cosas varías.
Se me ha olvidado mencionar que podemos comprar un JETPACK? UN PUTO JETCKPACK. Esto es practicamente obligatorio, ya que se nos puede ir la perola cavando hacia abajo y después como salimo eh amkina? HABER ESTUDIAO.
A cierta altura nos vamos a encontrar con unos cacho de pedrolos que no podremos romper con nuestro pico y nos bloquearan el paso, solución? DINAMITA. Podemos comprar dinamita para abrirnos camino y lamparas para poder iluminar nuestra maravillosa obra de arte.
Y ahora??? A ver chavales, el juego da para lo que da. Una vez tienes todo mejorado al máximo y has llegado hasta abajo…
El juego merece la pena? Yo diría que si, solo cuesta 5€ y es obstante adictivo, además, a quien no le gusta cavar? El juego es lo que es y esta claro que no es el típico al que le vas a meter 80 horas, pero estamos muy mal acostumbrados a pensar que juego corto es sinónimo de no merecer la pena, y no es así. Relación calidad precio para mi es un 9, asin que compratelo makina.

Ah, A Game About Digging a Hole, c'est un peu comme retrouver son âme d'enfant... mais sans le regard noir de maman et la menace de devoir tout reboucher à la petite pelle en plastique. Ici, pas de cris, pas de réprimandes, juste toi, une pelle et un sol qui ne demande qu'à être creusé jusqu'au centre de la Terre (ou jusqu'à ce que ton personnage se demande pourquoi il fait ça).  

Le jeu capture parfaitement cette joie pure et inexplicable de creuser *juste pour creuser*. Pas de quête épique, pas de dragons à affronter, juste un bon vieux trou qui s'approfondit avec une satisfaction presque hypnotique. Un retour en enfance, mais avec moins de terre sous les ongles et sans risquer d'écraser un pauvre ver de terre innocent.  

Bref, si tu as toujours rêvé d'aller au bout de ton trou sans que quelqu'un vienne gâcher la fête, ce jeu est fait pour toi. Simple, absurde et étrangement satisfaisant !

No graphics or control options. Game has no dead zone setting so if you play with a controller on PC or on Steam Deck it very slightly drifts constantly, even with just the Steam Deck controls. I tried two controllers that work fine on console and PC, no drifting, but with this game, drift. There's also no Steam Cloud sync, so you can't easily switch from Deck to PC. The actual game-play is decent, but the game needs an actual options menu. Playing with a mouse is a pain in the ass, because you have to click each time to dig. On controller you can just hold in R2 and it keeps digging for you, it needs accessibility options. Also jumping and jetpack are bound to the same key/button which leads to accidentally using the jet pack while trying to jump, which kills your character from battery drain and you lose all of your ore. An easy fix would be to have the jet pack turn on only on second key press with the second press being held or extending the activation delay. 

For $5 I still recommend it, but it needs some basic quality of life improvements. At least fix the dead zone issue and add auto-mining on left click hold.

Ця hole була створена для тебе. Вона голодна, відкрита, готова прийняти все, що ти можеш дати. Вона тремтить у передчутті, її вологі краї ваблять тебе всередину. Вона ще не знає, на що ти здатен, але скоро зрозуміє…

Ти починаєш повільно. Торкаєшся її, відчуваєш кожен вигин, кожну м’яку складку. Але це лише гра перед справжнім проникненням. Ти хапаєш її міцніше, входиш різко, змушуючи її затремтіти. Вона не була готова до такого, але вже не може зупинитися.

Ти копаєш глибше, жорсткіше, розширюючи її, змушуючи прийняти ще більше, ще сильніше. Ти нещадний. Ти безжальний. Hole змушена тремтіти під твоїм натиском, змушена відкритися для тебе повністю.

Кожен твій рух розриває її межі, кожен поштовх залишає слід глибоко всередині. Вона захлинається в своїй вологості, вона вже не в силах приховати, як сильно вона хоче ще і ще.

Ти вже на межі, але тобі цього недостатньо. Ти довбаєш її далі, ти вимотуєш її, ти змушуєш її підкоритися тобі повністю. Вона кричить, вона розпадається під твоїми руками… І ось момент кульмінації.

Глибокий, нестримний вибух. Земля розривається, усе навколо здригається, волога пробивається на поверхню. Ти досяг свого. Ти розкрив її по повній. Вона залишиться розширеною назавжди.

Але ти знаєш… Це ще не кінець. Бо поки існує хоча б одна hole – ти повернешся. І ти її проб’єш.

This game sucks my butt

so, about this "game". Let's start from the beginning - the menu. You can't go windowed, borderless etc. You can't go back from the options otherwise than saving options. After starting new game you can't skip  any cutscene. You can't get any achievements 'till u beat the game and start the new one. 
Gameplay... what can i say, arcade games from 80's had much more interesting and complicated gameplay. Dig to sell, sell to dig. You have very small inventory for the most time, and if your inventory is full, ore is just destroyed. Yeah, it won't just drop, like it should. U'll lose it. And to see how many slots you have free, there are no useful indicator in UI, you need to open your inventory and check there. Also, you can't drop ore from inventory and game is forcing you to run and sell it. 
Economy is as primitive as it can be. You just dig raw materials and sell them to restore HP/Energy and buy upgrades. You can also buy lamps and dynamite sticks. But lamps are very dark and dynamite sticks are weak and you can't but upgrade or a triple stick, pentastick etc. 
Light is terrible - it has it's own life. You can see everything clear from the surface, but see nothing after going down for a 10-15 meters, no matter that it was very bright from the surface and you can see the sky from the spot.
Storyline... well, there aren't one. I mean, it's like dev tried to do something similar to "Hello, Neighbour", but he/she was too lazy and just created a lazy intro and outro (boring, and remember, you can't skip it), that's all. And even here it's ridiculous - the same thing that trigger the outro isn't triggered by similar actions without the treasure...
Textures also are something - digging them with drill usually leads to seeing the gaps here and there. Also, sometimes your dynamite will just vanish after touching the ground - probably because of these gaps, but i'm not sure.
So, i'd say that it's not the full game (hate devs who mark early access as a full game), it's not Beta, It's not Alpha, it's not even pre-Alpha. It's just demo, pre-pre-Alpha, done in a day or two. But it has the price of a good indie game... Such a shame

If you've ever played Roblox before you know that this is a genre of game thats pretty popular for that platform, and is divided in to low-effort versions that are basically just a mining in a N x N square and then higher-effort versions that have pretty much been perfected in terms to the basic game play loop, interesting items, etc. This game is more like the former game play wise which is a shame, because people have been making this genre of game on Roblox for free and their versions are much more interesting than this (e.g. Espacio Mining before it got shut down which was this + leveling up a base, crafting weapons, buying gear, fighting bosses, fighting mobs, events, secrets + lore, etc.)

There are games that are much more thought out or have more in depth game design for the same price on steam, so that combined with the fact that people have made a superior version of this game for free on platforms like Roblox 5+ years ago makes any price for it hard to swallow.

Plays very well on SteamDeck, no issues and even shows the proper controls on the UI. Runs a consistent 60fps and is decently efficient on battery life to. Fun game to pass time, nothing crazy, but well worth the price IMO.

Good:
- Cool tech to have the ground dynamically deform as you dig into it.
- Initially fun progression after the first couple of upgrades.
- Neat to find the things that are buried under the ground the first time for each one.
- Final shovel upgrade fun to use.

Bad:
- It's really slow to get the first few upgrades because of how limited you are at that point.
- Once you have all the upgrades you probably have quite a ways to still dig to get to the ending, that becomes a bit of a slog.
- Fall damage is pretty harsh, get good at fluttering the jetpack to keep your descent speed down or you'll end up a pancake.
- You need to play through the game at least twice to do everything, but there's not anything new (aside from in-game achievements) to mix things up on the second play-through.

Ugly:
- You pretty much have to accidentally stumble into the treasures that the satellite dish helps you find, the range on that thing is way too small.
- The ending is nothing like the rest of the game: [spoiler]It's a forced stealth section in two phases, you can't use any of your tools as attacks or distractions, it's not obvious when the enemies can see you, their movement patterns are random so you can get screwed based on how they patrol, and the actual ending is a, "Congratulations, you lose!" kind of ending.[/spoiler]

Tips:
- Get each tier of shovel upgrade first before upgrading the other equipment to that tier, your shovel matters the most for how efficiently you can dig.
- Avoid using the jetpack until you find silver, before then it uses too much battery to be useful.
- Once your battery is low, get out of the hole and then use the rest of the meter to dig surface rocks until you fill your inventory, that way you won't run out of battery in a pit. (This matters less once you have a few battery upgrades).
- Don't let your battery run out, it does explode and kill you and you lose all the ores in your inventory when you respawn.

I was excited to play this because I'd watched two youtubers and it looked weirdly fun. However, while watching the videos was entertaining, the novelty of actually playing the game quickly wore off, and the repetitive clicking made the ulnar neuropathy in my arm, wrist, and hand flare up big time.

I was convinced there was some secret ending the youtubers had not discovered, but after my own playthrough, there does not appear to be any more to the game than what I'd already seen in the videos. There is an option to re-play the game to get several achievements, but given that there's no secret ending, and given the admittedly funny but deeply unsatisfying ending, I have no idea why the devs would assume someone would want to play again. 

PROS
- Love the art style
- Funny concept
- Funny ending

CONS
- Wrist strain from clicking mechanism
- Constant excavation sound effects started to grate on my nerves (eventually turned the SFX almost all the way off)
- When excavating, you can leave behind tiny little bits of dirt that you later cannot reach to remove. When jumping down, you can't see these tiny bits and can accrue fall damage by landing on these microscopic dirt particles, even if you're spamming the jetpack.
- While you can finish the game, you cannot win the game
- No ability to go into the house, neighborhood, or interact with anything other than dirt, minerals, your shovel, dynamite, lamps (which can break and can't be moved once placed), and the computer to sell minerals.
- Extremely limited upgrade tiers that cap out well before you reach the bottom, which initiates a boring grind mode to reach the end.
- While $5 is not a lot of money, it felt like too much to pay for a game you cannot win, whose re-playability is dubious, and whose total play time is a few hours at best. If this were free, or maybe 99 cents, I'd still mark it as not recommended, but perhaps less harshly.

I entirely expected to love this game, and while the first five minutes were fun, the rest made me wishing I'd requested a refund within the two hour return time frame.

"A Game About Digging A Hole" es un juego minimalista desarrollado por Cyberwave y lanzado el 7 de febrero de 2025 para PC. El objetivo principal es excavar un agujero en el jardín de una casa recién adquirida, recolectando recursos que se pueden vender para mejorar el equipo y profundizar aún más en la excavación. A medida que avanzas, descubres diferentes tipos de rocas y tesoros ocultos, lo que añade un elemento de sorpresa y recompensa al juego.

El juego ha sido bien recibido por su simplicidad y enfoque directo. Polygon destaca que, aunque la premisa es sencilla, el juego logra ser atractivo al combinar elementos de juegos de clics con la satisfacción de mejorar progresivamente las capacidades de excavación. Las mejoras incluyen palas eléctricas, mochilas más grandes e incluso un jetpack para facilitar la movilidad dentro del agujero.

Sin embargo, algunas críticas señalan que el juego puede carecer de profundidad a largo plazo. Movies Games and Tech menciona que, aunque es disfrutable en sesiones cortas, la falta de una narrativa sólida y la limitada variedad de mejoras pueden afectar su rejugabilidad y longevidad.

En resumen, "A Game About Digging A Hole" ofrece una experiencia sencilla y relajante que puede ser ideal para aquellos que buscan un juego casual sin complicaciones. Su precio asequible y su enfoque minimalista lo convierten en una opción interesante para pasar el tiempo, siempre que no se busque una experiencia de juego profunda o compleja.
