🕳️ [h1] Recenzja: A Game About Digging A Hole – czyli jak kopać i nie zwariować [/h1]
[h2] Wstęp [/h2]
Czy można stworzyć grę opartą wyłącznie na kopaniu dziury? 🤔 Oczywiście. Czy można ją sprzedać jako relaksacyjne doświadczenie? Jak najbardziej. Ale czy to oznacza, że jest to dobra gra? Tu zaczynają się schody… albo raczej – dołki. ⛏️

[h2] Rozgrywka [/h2]
A Game About Digging A Hole to produkcja, która dosłownie robi to, co obiecuje w tytule. Kopiesz dziurę. 🕳️ To wszystko. Nie ma żadnych wymyślnych mechanik 🎮, nie ma ekscytujących zwrotów akcji, nie ma też żadnej realnej progresji – poza coraz większą dziurą, która w pewnym momencie przestaje robić wrażenie.

Owszem, gra oferuje pewien rodzaj odprężenia. Można odpalić, posłuchać klimatycznej muzyki 🎵 i bezmyślnie kopać – brzmi jak świetna opcja dla tych, którzy chcą się „odmóżdżyć” po ciężkim dniu. 😌 Tylko czy warto tracić czas na coś, co można symulować w prawdziwym życiu, wychodząc do ogródka z łopatą? 🏡🪓

[h2] Grafika i oprawa dźwiękowa [/h2]
Graficznie A Game About Digging A Hole jest poprawna. 🎨 Nie ma tu wodotrysków, ale styl pasuje do koncepcji – prosto, czytelnie, bez zbędnych fajerwerków. Muzyka jest klimatyczna, ale po dłuższym czasie zaczyna się powtarzać i może stać się monotonna.

[h2] Fabuła i zakończenie [/h2]
Fabuła, o ile można ją tak nazwać, w pewnym momencie faktycznie wciąga, co jest największym zaskoczeniem tego tytułu. 😮 Samo zakończenie? Nie zdradzę szczegółów, ale jeśli ktoś spodziewał się po prostu „skończonej dziury”, to może się zdziwić.

[spoiler] Zakończenie: W finale okazuje się, że pod ziemią znajduje się tajemnicza struktura, która całkowicie zmienia kontekst gry. To nie tylko bezsensowne kopanie – jest w tym głębsze znaczenie! 😱 [/spoiler]

[h2] Podsumowanie [/h2]
🔹 Czy warto? Jeśli szukasz czegoś absolutnie minimalistycznego i relaksującego, to tak. ✔️ Jeśli jednak oczekujesz czegoś więcej niż symulator kopania, lepiej poszukać innej gry. ❌

Well first and foremost, the digging (core mechanic) is not satisfying. When digging, bits of dirt are left floating around in the air and you have to fly around and knock them out unless you're a psychopath and they don't bother you. The holes you dig look ugly as ♥♥♥♥ after you dig them so you can't even really admire the work you've done at any point; unless you try to clear out everything, which is frustrating in and of itself due to the aforementioned floating bits of dirt. 

The upgrades are as bare bones as can be. It feels rewarding at first when you are upgrading your shovel but then before you know it, your shovel/drill is fully upgraded and you are still left wanting more. And at that point all that's left to do is upgrade your battery, backpack and jetpack which are all just bleh. 

The end game is boring and underwhelming. The ending is so dumb and predictable. And then to top it all off, you have to replay the game from the beginning to get achievements..

I only hope that this game can inspire someone to make a better hole digging game.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - I Dug a Hole and My Life Will Never Be the Same

You ever just wake up and think, “Man, I need to dig a hole”? No? Well, neither did I—until I played this masterpiece.

This game is EXACTLY what it promises. You dig. A lot. At first, I thought, “Wow, this is dumb.” And then, two hours later, I was screaming at my monitor, “JUST ONE MORE SCOOP!”

The gameplay? Flawless. The story? There is none, it’s just a hole, and that’s beautiful. The soundtrack? It’s just the sound of me questioning my life choices as I dig deeper into the abyss.

I have ignored my responsibilities, my friends, and my family, all in pursuit of the perfect hole. My landlord knocked on my door asking for rent, and I told him, “I can’t, I’m busy digging.” My girlfriend left me, but that’s okay, because this hole would never abandon me.

In conclusion, this game is life-changing. Also, I spent my last dollars on it.

11/10 - I have become one with the dirt.

This is not just a game about digging a hole, this game is a story of the power greed has on the common man.

Here I was, buying a simple house for the sole purpose of making cash. Buried treasure, they said. They weren't wrong. Underneath the soils of my backyard was minerals galore. Iron, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and even Diamonds. Hell I even found some of DB Cooper's lost money suitcases. Yet that wasn't enough. I needed more.

So I kept digging. I tore my once lovely backyard to shreds in search of more minerals and lost conspiracy cash. I made thousands off selling those minerals, but it wasn't enough. There were more riches to be found after all. I needed more.

That's when I found out that my wife left me, she said she couldn't handle seeing the man she once loved covered in dirt and sweat digging in a giant hole all day. That and something about the ruined flowerbed but she just didn't understand that this was for US. I was going to bring us a life of wealth! Alas, she gave up to soon. More for me I suposse.

And so I kept digging, and digging, and digging, and digging. More minerals, more funds to my wallet, but my hunger for riches was never satiated. Even as I tore apart that backyard and made thousands I was never satisfied, so I just kept digging.

I lost myself in that hole. The man that once was is long gone, buried in the chunks of dirt and grime all in the fruitless chase for a box of treasure.

And even after finding that treasure, I just kept digging, because even with all the wealth and glory I had acquired, it was never enough.

I lost everything that was once me, but hey at least I got cash right? Right?

The digging itself was relatively enjoyable in a mindless way. I originally compared it to Powerwash Simulator in the sense that its semi-satisfying work and you can upgrade your tools to boost your efficiency. That was, however, until I got to the bottom. I was expecting some sort of treasure at the bottom (which was not as far down as I expected though still quite far) but I was met with a twist that felt somewhat out of place. To learn that all the work I had put in was... worthless? None of the upgrades that I had earned helped me, there was nothing I could do except hope I could evade the moles (I couldn't). It wasn't the worst $5 I've ever spent, but I think your money could be spent elsewhere where you can get more gameplay for your dollar.

This is somewhat novel, yet stripped-down digging game with a resource-based progression system and barely anything else.

PROS:
-no frills, easy to play
-intrinsically appealing premise
-well-implemented 3D digging
-compelling resource-collection loop
-cute ending
-no bugs or major jank encountered

CONS:
-very short
-ultimately, lacks mechanical depth
-digging area is somewhat small and has very few treasures to discover (which you will not know until you've spent an hour or two digging)
-almost all items you find just feed back into the economy loop, so gameplay doesn't evolve past dig/dynamite/lights/upgrade
-finale at the bottom of the hole is a little half-baked

SUMMARY:
This game is a good canvas for something incredible, and although it's quite fun for what it is, the game seems like more of an inspiration for a future game that truly explores 3D digging mechanics.

"A Game About Digging A Hole" to minimalistyczna gra, która w prostocie odnajduje swoją największą siłę. Wcielasz się w nowego właściciela domu, który postanawia zbadać tajemnice ukryte w ogrodzie poprzez kopanie dziury. Początkowo wyposażeni jedynie w łopatę, stopniowo odkrywasz różnorodne zasoby i skarby, które możesz sprzedawać, aby ulepszać sprzęt. Dzięki temu proces kopania staje się coraz bardziej efektywny i satysfakcjonujący.

Mechanika gry płynnie ewoluuje od prostego klikania do bardziej zaawansowanego symulatora, w którym tworzymy skomplikowane systemy tuneli w poszukiwaniu cennych kamieni. Każde ulepszenie, takie jak elektryczna wiertło, większy plecak czy jetpack, dodaje nową warstwę strategii i ekscytacji.

Jednym z najbardziej intrygujących aspektów jest ukryta głęboko pod ziemią tajemnica, która dodaje grze elementu niespodzianki i zachęca do dalszej eksploracji. Choć gra jest stosunkowo krótka, oferuje zakończenie, które satysfakcjonuje i pozostawia gracza z poczuciem osiągnięcia.

Mimo drobnych niedociągnięć, takich jak brak satysfakcjonujących efektów dźwiękowych podczas kopania, "A Game About Digging A Hole" dostarcza wciągającej i relaksującej rozgrywki, która potrafi pochłonąć na długie godziny. To doskonały przykład na to, jak prostota i dobrze przemyślana mechanika mogą stworzyć niezwykle angażujące doświadczenie.

The title of the game doesn't lie. You click to dig, you collect materials from the earth, you jetpack (!) back to the surface to sell your materials, upgrade your gear, and do it all over again. This feels like a spiritual successor to flash games you'd play on Newgrounds, only with a much higher level of polish. Each time I upgraded my shovel I was excited to get deeper and deeper.

Yes, it's shorter than I expected. Yes, I wish there was more to it; there's a solid core to this game that is ready to be explored! It does feel like fun was left on the table after putting in the work to make the core of the game. 

But have to respect and support a developer that put together a tight 60-120 minute experience, made it polished and fun to play, and published it. It won't knock your socks off, but it's worth the price of a cup of coffee for the afternoon of fun I got. YMMV depending how much you like digging.

My Honest opinion about this game:

I beat the main game in about 2.3 hours because i have ADHD and i get distracted by many things, and the more times i get distracted in a game, is what tells me the game is good. The way the leaves move, the way the grass moves, the way the dirt get dug, the giant hole in my backyard. I could dig forever if provided. I will proceed to play the entire game again in achievement mode, unlock all achievements and dig every last piece of dirt in my backyard until its the biggest hole i've ever seen.

CONS: Theres not enough content;
Its not that theres not enough content, its just that I WANT MORE!! More upgrades, more ores, more items, MORE BACKYARDS TO DIG! I find this game ended too quick for me. I wanted to keep playing it, hence why im going to replay on achievement mode. The game is too small. Its very well made and i assume if it does well (i hope) there will be a sequel or a bigger update that adds more. 

IDEAS:
More backyards to dig, different themes for different backyards.
Skins for the shovel, the stone, the house, the tnt, lamps, everything!
More upgrades; i feel like i was able to upgrade everything far to quickly, and it came to an end when i wish it didnt, I think there could be multiple levels of upgrades added to all the up-gradable components, and more, Maybe an upgradable house, garage that allows storage for trophies (the treasure in case you wanna display instead of selling). 

I know i'm simply trying to change a game that has released VERY well. Don't get me wrong, i would dig nonstop in this game even in its current state, and i will continue to dig until i've unlocked every achieve and dug ever last bit of dirt and ore. I YEARN FOR THE MINES!

The game is an absolute blast to play. The core gameplay loop is incredibly satisfying—you dig deeper and deeper into the ground, constantly upgrading your equipment to make the process faster, more efficient, and even more enjoyable. There's a real sense of progression as you fine-tune your tools and strategies, making every new layer you uncover feel rewarding.

However, without spoiling anything, the ending introduces a frustrating, unpredictable element that feels out of place. Instead of a fulfilling conclusion, it relies on randomness in a way that disrupts the carefully built momentum of the experience. It’s a disappointing twist that doesn’t respect the time and effort invested in upgrading and optimizing throughout the game. While the journey itself is fantastic, the final moments leave much to be desired.

Dieses Spiel, und dem Anschein nach die anderen des Entwicklers, sind meiner Meinung nach genau zwischen Mobile Games und PC Games. Bedeutet, es hat in etwa den Umfang eines Mobile Games, aber keine Mikrotransaktionen. Es ist aber auch kein Just Cause oder GTA mit hunderten Stunden Spass, dafür kostet es nur einen Zehntel so viel. Meiner Ansicht nach sollte es mehr solche Spiele geben.

Das zur Länge. Bezüglich des Inhalts muss ich eine schlechtere Bewertung abgeben. Es fängt an wie beworben - man gräbt ein Loch, findet Erze und benutzt diese, um das Loch schneller zu graben. Soweit so gut. Dann allerdings [spoiler]stösst man auf ein Dungeon[spoiler] und es wird plötzlich zu einem [spoiler]Stealth/Horror[/spoiler]-Spiel.

Warum die Entwickler das so gemacht haben kann ich mir nicht vorstellen - Wieso nicht bessere Upgrades? Andere Biome? Andere Werkzeuge? Andere Löcher? Das enttäuschendste ist dann, dass weder das alles im Spiel ist, noch die Story weitergeführt wird. Man kann einfach alles nochmal machen, dafür mit Achievements.

Tl;dr: Das Spiel fängt interessant an, aber ab etwa einer Stunde hört es auf, wird für 10 Minuten zu einem anderen Spiel und ist fertig. Danach gibt es nichts neues mehr zu machen, weder Story- noch Progressionsweise.

It's... okay. For five bucks, it's good. I like to dig. It's satisfying to make a big hole. Worth it for what it costs but disappointing.

As fun as digging is, the fact that the game likes to leave tiny fragments behind that are annoying.
Another annoyance in digging is if you clear around the rocks before blowing them up, it's really hard to hit them. The dynamite bounces a lot, which make precision a pain.
Going back to those little fragments for a moment. Landing on them sucks. If your plan is to activate the jetpack before landing, you'll end up landing on one of those and take damage. Grated health basically doesn't matter. Only enemy kills you in one shot. Running out of energy kills you. Dynamite and falling are the only ways you can take (just) damage instead of die. So, yeah. The only damage is self damage. Ah. Wait. I forgot about those random fire rocks. They can hurt you if you stand on them at the right angle.

Having to click until you get the drill upgrade is kind of annoying. But eh. I went past it. Not too terrible.

The fact the teleporter was a one time use threw me off. I thought it was a gift for exploring. Not a consumable.

Now, the worst part. The ending.

Others have brought it up before but you're suddenly dropped into a stealth segment where none of the abilities you've upgraded for the last however long matter. You have to sneak around some enemies that kill you on catch. so health amount doesn't matter and then the actual end just felt meh. Like, made it all feel more worthless than what I expected it to be.

I would also like, if at the end, when you reach the bottom or something, you somehow unlock even more powerful upgrades. Like a drill that can destroy rocks and a big range of dirt. It would give something to spend all that cash you're going to be making at the bottom and make the process of completely emptying the hole of dirt, like I wanted to do originally, easier.  Also, maybe give a purchasable permanent teleport. Maybe that could be a key item to a "good" ending? Idk. I just want to dig holes and not have it feel as meh.

Also. A day/night cycle would be kinda cool. Give more use for the lights you can buy early on.

The upgrade progression doesn’t make much sense and is poorly balanced, and exploration is practically nonexistent.

One thing that could have made the experience more interesting would have been the introduction of ladders instead of giving the jetpack right away, encouraging a more strategic approach to digging. But even that wouldn’t have fixed the exploration issues. Also, without spoiling anything, the final section is just really poorly designed.

Clocking in at a relatively short playtime—about 2 hours to beat—this game delivers a unique kind of zen that’s perfect for players looking for a low-stakes, chill experience. The price tag of just $5 makes it an easy pick-up if you're in the mood for something casual and fun.

At its core, Digging Holes is all about... well, digging holes. The gameplay loop involves clicking to dig deeper and uncover various treasures, gems, and secrets buried beneath the surface. It’s an oddly soothing activity, like digital fidgeting. There’s something satisfying about the repetitive motion, and the visuals, while simple, add to the peaceful atmosphere. The progression feels rewarding enough, though the mechanics don’t evolve significantly, so don't expect too much complexity or challenge.

If you're someone who likes to zone out and let your mind wander while clicking away, this is a great option. It’s not a game that demands your full attention, and its low-stakes nature means you can just dive in, do your thing, and turn off your brain for a while.

However, after around 2 hours, I was pretty much done. There’s not a whole lot of substance beyond the digging, and the game’s limited scope prevents it from offering any lasting appeal. It’s fun in the moment, but there’s little incentive to keep playing once you’ve hit the end.

In short, Digging Holes is great if you’re looking for something quick, low-effort, and easy to lose yourself in for a few hours. But don’t expect it to leave a lasting impression. For $5, though, it’s hard to argue that it isn’t worth a brief diversion.

Pros:

    Cheap price point ($5)
    Great for zoning out and relaxing
    Simple but satisfying gameplay loop

Cons:

    Short playtime (about 2 hours)
    Lack of depth or variety after a while
    Not much replay value

Verdict: Perfect for short, mindless fun, but don’t expect a groundbreaking experience.

It's a neat premise for a game, but I can't really say it was worth playing.

The actual digging mechanic is extremely simple. You dig, get ores, sell them, upgrade your gear, and repeat. And that's a good place for a game to start, but it doesn't get much more complicated than that. 

The decisions you make over what to upgrade are pretty obvious from the start. You only have 4 choices and it never branches out, so you're never really thinking very hard about what to pick next. I would have loved to see the ability to upgrade different stats or for you to acquire more tools. 

I thought I would eventually find more mechanics to play with or more challenges to overcome, but I didn't. You just keep digging, doing the same thing from start to finish, and then it ends.

The only thing left is the curiosity of what you might find, and that feeling was really the reason I bought the game. And unfortunately, after finishing the game, I can't really say it was worth it.

So is it a game about digging a hole? Yes, but that's all it is. Is it worth $5? Maybe, but I can't say it was worth my time.

The game has potential and I would love to see it developed further into a more rewarding experience!

The act of digging a hole seems, on the surface, a monument to futility.  We displace earth, creating a void, only to likely fill it again.  It’s a task often associated with manual labor, a symbol of the mundane, even the punitive. Yet, within this seemingly pointless endeavor, a surprising depth of meaning can be unearthed, layer by layer, like the very soil we excavate.  Digging a hole, when approached with intention, can become a meditation, a metaphor, and a surprisingly profound act of creation.

The physical act itself offers a connection to the earth, a grounding experience in a world increasingly disconnected from the tangible.  The feel of the shovel biting into the soil, the weight of the earth in our hands, the rhythm of the work – these sensations anchor us in the present moment.  The sweat, the strain, the gradual formation of the hole – all demand our complete focus, pushing aside the anxieties and distractions of daily life.  In this physical exertion, there is a primal satisfaction, a connection to the generations of humans who have toiled the land before us.  The hole becomes a testament to our effort, a tangible representation of our physical presence in the world.

Beyond the physical, digging a hole can be a powerful metaphor for personal growth and transformation.  The hole can represent the challenges we face, the obstacles we must overcome.  The act of digging becomes a symbolic journey through these difficulties.  Each shovelful of earth represents a step forward, a small victory in the face of adversity.  As the hole deepens, so too does our resilience, our determination.  We confront the “dirt” of our past, the difficult emotions and experiences that we bury deep within ourselves.  The act of digging them out, bringing them to the surface, can be a cathartic process, allowing us to confront and ultimately overcome them.

Furthermore, the emptiness of the hole itself can be a source of meaning.  It is a space of potential, a blank canvas upon which we can project our hopes and dreams.  The hole can represent the void we feel in our lives, the things that are missing.  But it is also a space for something new to grow, a foundation for future projects.  Perhaps the hole is dug for a tree, a symbol of life and growth.  Perhaps it is for a foundation, a symbol of stability and security.  Or perhaps it is simply a space for reflection, a place to contemplate the vastness of the universe and our place within it.  The emptiness, therefore, is not a void but a pregnant pause, a space teeming with possibility.

Finally, the act of digging a hole can be seen as a creative endeavor.  We are, in a sense, sculpting the earth, shaping it to our will.  We are creating something where there was nothing before.  The hole, though seemingly simple, is a testament to our ingenuity and our ability to transform the world around us.  We are not just digging a hole; we are creating a narrative, a story written in the earth itself.

In conclusion, the act of digging a hole, far from being a meaningless task, can be a profound and transformative experience.  It offers a connection to the earth, a metaphor for personal growth, a space for reflection, and an act of creation.  It reminds us that even in the most mundane of activities, we can find meaning, purpose, and a deeper understanding of ourselves and the world around us.  So, the next time you find yourself digging a hole, take a moment to appreciate the depth of the experience, both literally and figuratively. You might just unearth something unexpected.

有一个理论叫做“峰尾效应”，就是客户的体验大部分取决于开始和结束的时候。
那当我结束短暂的刚好够我退款（可能）的119分钟的旅程，我恰好在开头和结尾时感受最糟糕。
在开始时，铲子的挖掘能力非常差，我感觉像在玩一个clicker game，担心把鼠标给按废了。时不时的，空中悬浮的极小的尘土颗粒卡住了我的行动
但在挖出第一个矿洞之后，事情开始有趣了起来。这种感受在买到了钻头之后达到了巅峰——当钻头满级后，终于可以像我的世界那样垂直真男人挖矿了，我就一路向下，满载而归——

直到我落入了四个木条包围的隧道中。

我很好奇作者最后为什么要安排[spoiler] 连续三个洞穴的恐怖追逐战[/spoiler] 。你抛弃了之前搭建的所有系统，转而开始依赖虚幻五引擎自带的角色移动与加速功能。
更恶心的是，[spoiler] 最后得到的宝藏空无一物[/spoiler] 。我其实并不惊讶，毕竟，那个箱子和它周围偌大的，缺少装饰的房间一样虚无，一样毫无意义，就像我希望通过这个游戏感受一些整理，收获的快乐一样，毫无意义。
当玩家沉浸在你的游戏中时，用这种恶趣味来破坏体验是非常恶意的。我希望能被事前通知，如果我明知自己在玩soul-like游戏，我或许不会那么失望。

我不喜欢这样的结局设计，无论作者如何自圆其说。一个沙盒游戏应该重视并鼓励玩家的建构是有意义的，否则就是对玩家的蔑视。

A Game About Digging A Hole" ist ein minimalistisches, aber überraschend fesselndes Spiel, in dem du ein Loch im Garten deines neu gekauften Hauses gräbst. Was simpel klingt, entpuppt sich als kurzweiliges und unterhaltsames Erlebnis.

Gameplay:

Das Spielprinzip ist einfach: Du gräbst mit deiner Schaufel ein Loch, findest dabei Ressourcen, die du verkaufen kannst, um deine Ausrüstung zu verbessern. Je tiefer du gräbst, desto wertvoller werden die Ressourcen und desto mehr Geheimnisse entdeckst du.

Spielzeit und Umfang:

Die Spielzeit beträgt etwa 3 Stunden, wenn du alle Errungenschaften freischalten möchtest. Das Spiel ist nicht besonders umfangreich, aber es bietet genug Inhalt, um dich für diese Zeit zu unterhalten.

Grafik und Sound:

Die Grafik ist bewusst einfach gehalten, was dem Spiel einen gewissen Charme verleiht. Der Sound ist unaufdringlich und passt zum entspannten Spielgefühl.

Fazit:

"A Game About Digging A Hole" ist ein kleines, aber feines Spiel, das überraschend viel Spaß macht. Es ist perfekt für zwischendurch, wenn du einfach nur ein bisschen abschalten und ein simples Spiel genießen möchtest. Wenn du auf der Suche nach einem kurzweiligen und unterhaltsamen Spiel bist, dann solltest du "A Game About Digging A Hole" auf jeden Fall ausprobieren.

[h1] 在小小的花园挖呀挖呀挖，挖到亮闪闪的石头带回家[/h1]

掘地求财是一款小品级挖地寻宝游戏，游戏的内容很简单，在自己新买的家后院一路向下挖，挖出矿物和各种宝藏提升经济，接着购买各种升级提升挖地效率然后接着挖。游戏本身内容很少，一路向下挖到100m触发结局挑战就完成了，整体流程也基本上是打洞、喷气背包飞上去、卖货升级然后继续下来挖的重复，有这类玩法的模拟经营游戏有很多，不过本作更贴近波西亚时光的设计。游戏的升级项也比较少，等挖到有钻石的层的时候钱基本就开始溢出了，游戏的加点项很少，后期能溢出几万的钱没东西买，基本上1h冒头就能通关了（游戏甚至有一个成就是30min内完成游戏，可见流程并不长）。不过从一个小铲子一点一点挖坑到升级成钻头（跟吸尘器一样）发家致富挖出超级大坑的过程还是很有成就感的，而且游戏定价不到20元，确实物有所值，很适合休闲时买来图一乐休闲一下。

p.s.游戏比较推荐拿来休闲，不推荐像我一样上头搞成就。游戏本身一周目是不能解锁成就的，需要一周目通关拿了通关成就后去二周目解锁成就（不过会叠加一周目的数据），其实一直到二周目结束体验都还算好。结果我一周目二周目都完事加起来也就2h，为了除“30min内结束游戏成就”外的其他成就，在下面又无脑挖了3h，直接玩的冒肝火。尤其是最后两个“空中下降4s”“找两个钥匙打开宝箱”成就，玩的我直冒火。游戏里面挖地他的设计是把泥土这个物体清除一定体积，而不管是前期球体体积消除的铲子还是后面不断挖出球体的钻头，都会在本身立方体的泥土中留下一些“残渣”，这些残渣在你玩的过程中可能不会注意，本身也是漂浮在空中的一些小体积泥土，但在空降时可就致命了，因为这些都是带碰撞体积的，空降4s成就基本上需要从地表一路降到快100m的距离，这个时候空中的这些残渣会不断要了你的命，还贼难找到。。。至于那个钥匙更是蛋疼，游戏虽然能探测器探到但是识别范围很小，我基本在下面瞎猫碰死耗子挖了2h才挖出来，都快给下面清空了，还是推荐休闲玩别想着肝成就了。

You can't use any of your upgrades you've spent an hour or so getting.

The actual ending of the story is fine. Nothing crazy but not bad.
But the final area needs work. Make me use my upgrades. Throw dynamite for distractions, dig through blocked doorways. Jet pack over bottomless gaps or lava. You can also buy lights for the dark parts and dynamite to blow rock that is too hard for your drill/shovel. I was having a solid 6/10 time until I made it 100 meters deep, at that point having every upgrade possible. 

Upon reaching the bottom you find a drop down point where you suddenly are thrust from a relaxing grind game to a stealth mission with no clear direction in a dark cavern. You can't drill, cant use your jetpack, can't use lights, can't use dynamite, all of your upgrades are gone for the purpose of the stealth shift. It's a jarring genre shift and it instantly lost my interest after i snuck past the enemy only to find an even bigger chamber with more enemies i needed to sneak past. 

Overall a mid game thanks to the genre shift..

✅ RECOMMENDED

I began in my backyard. A small tool in hand. Just dirt, rocks… and the faint sense that this was the start of something bigger.

Hours turned into days. I harvested rocks. Sold them online. Upgraded my tools. Built machines I never thought I’d need. A shovel… a battery… even a jetpack. The hole grew. So did I.

Months passed. The backyard became a labyrinth. The dirt whispered secrets. Every layer felt purposeful, like there was a story hidden beneath the soil.

I dug. I dug. And somewhere, deep down, I sensed that the hole… had plans of its own.

This is more than a simple game about digging. It’s a journey into something absurd, mysterious, and oddly captivating.

Первые 30 минут игры - как по методичке "Как создать шедевр для кощунственного убийства собственного времени", потом.... Потом начинается боль. Я очень хотел поставить палец вверх, но понял, что игра не приносит удовольствие, а в моменте сильно раздражает, что не должно быть в подобном жанре в принципе.
Игра ОЧЕНЬ быстро схлопывается. За час вы прокачаете все вещи и деньги просто будут накапливаться как снежный ком. 
Есть визуальные баги. Заходя в гараж (место где вы покупаете прокачку/продаёте нарытое непосильным трудом) игра начинает фризить. Есть баги с моделью уничтожения камней динамитом, но это уже не столь критично.
При копании очень часто остаются висящие мелкие куски почвы, а так как у персонажа есть хп кажется, что будете постоянно умирать от земли, забывшей, что такое гравитация, но с этим всё в порядке, моя боль в другом. Она в моменте, когда я из-за камушка ты не можешь нормально управлять персонажем и мысли  "Почему я чёрт возьми не могу пройти дальше?!".

A primeira vez que eu vi esse jogo foi em um anuncio no Facebook (sim ele ainda existe) e eu coloquei na minha lista pensando que ia ser um dos diversos jogos que tem uma proposta legalzinha mas nunca sai, o que não foi o caso.

O jogo é extremamente simples e o looping de gameplay dele é exatamente o que você vê no trailer/primeiros 20 minutos de jogo. No começo a progressão é extremamente lenta mas conforme você cava mais fundo e tem acesso a minérios melhores você recebe mais dinheiro e em 1 hora já quase maximizou tudo (e pelo que percebo essa é a faixa de tempo média entre os jogadores que analisaram o jogo). 

Eu ainda não achei o tesouro escondido e nem fiz as conquistas mas chutando alto eu diria que o jogo não tem muito mais que 5 horas de conteúdo, e arrisco dizer que é um tanto enjoativo já que não tem  muito mais o que fazer nele, você vai e cava até sua mochila encher ou ficar sem bateria, você vende seus minérios, compra upgrades e repete.

O jogo te lembra caso você fique muito tempo sem salvar, o que deve ser feito manualmente e eu agradeço que esse lembrete exista já que estou mal acostumado com save automático em praticamente tudo, além de outras qualidades de vida como tradução PT-BR (que é feita por uma extensão de UNITY, tanto que ao salvar o jogo aparece "economizando..." o que é bem engraçado). 

Eu acho pouco provável que qualquer coisa nova venha ao jogo mas seria legal uma vez que  dinheiro pareça ficar inútil quando todos os upgrades forem comprados. Talvez algo cosmético como mobiliá pra casa que poderia ser um mini espaço pra você acessar, ou talvez um teleporte para chegar a superfície mais rápido que gasta uma quantidade alta de energia. Também senti falta de um menu de estatísticas, uma vez que algumas conquistas sejam do tipo "Colete X do Minério Y" e saber quantos você já coletou seria muito legal. 

Pelo que o jogo tem a oferecer eu achei o preço um pouco salgado, mas me sinto mal em dizer isso de uma empresa pequena então nem vou reembolsar pra ver se volto outra hora pelas conquistas mas de forma geral o jogo é exatamente o que ta no trailer e apesar de ser bem relaxante e de certa forma satisfatório da mesma forma que é assistir alguns reels de Instagram, não passa disso. Talvez vale uma chance pra jogar uma horinha ou duas sem pensar muito a respeito.

⭐ El verdadero GOTY ⭐

Olvídate de Elden Ring y su “profunda” exploración. ¿Para qué quieres un mundo enorme si puedes excavar tu propio destino? The Last of Us presume de su gran historia, pero este juego es literalmente más profundo. Skyrim dice que tiene libertad, pero ¿puedes cavar un agujero sin que un NPC te interrumpa con una misión irrelevante? No lo creo.

Aquí no hay cinemáticas innecesarias, diálogos cursis ni personajes que te obliguen a sentir emociones. Solo tú, una pala y un agujero que crece más rápido que la deuda externa. Los gráficos son revolucionarios: un agujero en constante evolución. La banda sonora es minimalista pero inolvidable: el crunch de la pala golpeando la tierra, un sonido más satisfactorio que cualquier OST de Final Fantasy.

La jugabilidad es impecable. Sin tutoriales, sin microtransacciones, sin lootboxes. Diablo IV debería tomar nota. Cada palada es un paso más hacia el vacío existencial que tanto temes enfrentar. ¿Tiene final? No lo sé, pero después de cavar durante horas, estoy demasiado comprometido como para dejar de intentarlo.

⛏️ 15/10, más atrapante que GTA VI (porque ese ni ha salido). Mi familia está preocupada, pero el agujero me comprende.

かなり面白いです。どれくらい面白いかと言うと、５８０円の値段で購入から既に３時間も経って居る位の面白さ。内容はひたすら掘るゲームです。掘って石や鉱石を採掘して売り、売った金でショベル・バッテリー・所持品数の増加・ジェットパックの購入及びアップグレードに使います。掘るとたまに宝物を見つけれる事もあります。プレイ開始時、庭にバツ印が書かれて居ますが、そこはあくまで目安な上、石や鉱石は比較的浅い地層でも取れるので、最初は庭をまんべんなく掘る事をオススメします。理由は所持品が一杯になったら、直ぐに売る事が出来るので。そしてアップグレードですが、まずは所持品の増加をアップグレードさせ、次にバッテリー、そしてショベルのアップグレードの方が効率が良いかも知れない。そしてジェットパックを購入する間では、あんまり深く掘らない方が良いです。戻る時に色々大変なので。そして所持品が一杯の状態で石・鉱石を取ろうとすると、破壊されます。ちなみに自分は、このレビューを書いて居る時点ですが、マントル地点まで掘りました（笑）。なおこのゲームの主人公は無敵では無いので、高い場所から落下したり、マントルに触れたらダメージを受けます。体力回復は、バッテリー充電もそうですが、金が掛かります。だからそれらの出費も計算しながらアップグレードする感じに、自分は感じました。

The good:
- It's 5 bucks
- I got 2 hours out of it, so it's like streaming a movie.
- If I cared enough I could probably get another hour out of it looking at achievements or trying to dig out the whole yard.
- I respect the opportunism or business sense at work here -- they are working on a game called Solarpunk (quietly, classily advertised in game) and this was basically just a gamejam/techdemo kind of thing they built along the way. Smart to get some revenue out of it.

The bad:
- This should probably be a little less than 5 dollars. I mean -- it's 5 bucks, whatever. But big picture, it's a thin experience, and it's very short. But maybe it will end up being a huge seller for 99c during steam sales, who knows.
- I was hoping for a little more meat on the bone - The game shows you it's loop early, and it never really changes. But like, at one point you just find... an empty room. You can't do anything there, you can't add anything. It just exists. I was expecting a new console to open up in the workshop that led me do ANYTHING with the room, but nope it's just a room.
- The ending is silly, but this is a very light criticism because we're all here for the hole digging and progression, not the ending.

So in conclusion I was like 90% happy with this, 10% disapointed. If 5 dollars doesn't matter to you, this is a fun 2 hours. If your budget is tight and the amount of entertainment time you get out of a game matters to you? This can be finished in 2 hours (after which achievements activate) so take that into consideration.

As I already mentioned, I'm not sure if I like this game. I have a hard time explaining why I like idle/clicking games in general, but this one is even more questionable because you can't idle at all, and all you'll see is your shed and the hole you're digging. However, I kept playing and kept giving the speedrun achievement a try, so clearly, something is still addictive. Is it just that the numbers go up? 

Some of the things that are questionable to me are that when playing with a mouse and keyboard (which I prefer over a gamepad in this specific game), you have to keep clicking until you unlock one of the last shovel upgrades, and then you have to hold the mouse button. While on a gamepad, you can already hold the right trigger from the start to keep digging. 

And the achievements will not unlock during your first playthrough is weird. It seems to be a designer choice, and if you finish the game and press "continue," you'll unlock those that you have gotten the required requirements retroactively, but why not just unlock them while you are on your first playthrough, as little rewards for that you keep going on? From what I read is that the speedrun achievement unlocks after finishing that run, and then press continue in the main menu, so be sure to get back into your save after giving it a try to see if you really didn't get it. 

While most of the achievements are earned naturally, the one for rainbow ores is only possible after finishing the first run and starting a new game in ächievement mode." As stated, there is a speedrun achievement that requires you to finish the game within 30 minutes. This is quite challenging. 

I give A Game About Digging A Hole 2,5 out of 5 stars.

Manchmal sind es die einfachsten Konzepte, die am meisten Spaß machen – genau das beweist A Game About Digging A Hole! Mit nichts weiter als einer Schaufel bewaffnet gräbt man sich immer tiefer in die Erde, auf der Suche nach einem geheimnisvollen Schatz. Unterwegs findet man wertvolle Ressourcen wie Kohle, Eisen und Gold, die man verkaufen kann, um bessere Ausrüstung zu kaufen. Das sorgt für eine schöne Gameplay-Schleife: graben, verkaufen, upgraden – und wieder von vorne.

Das Spiel ist eher kurz – wer es gemütlich angeht, braucht etwa 4-5 Stunden bis zum Ziel. Trotzdem fühlt sich die Reise dorthin lohnenswert an, und für den fairen Preis von rund 5€ bekommt man ein charmantes, unterhaltsames Erlebnis.

Hier noch ein Paar Ideen für mehr Content:
Vielleicht ein paar mehr Geheimnisse abseits des Hauptpfads oder die Möglichkeit, sich nicht nur nach unten, sondern auch zur Seite zu graben – wie wäre es, sich zum Beispiel bis zum Nachbargrundstück hochzugraben und dort ein verstecktes Item zu entdecken? Auch eine Art Autominer, der mit Kohle betrieben wird, könnte für noch mehr Spieltiefe sorgen.

----- Spoilerwarnung ab hier!) ------
Das Finale des Spiels ist nett, aber es wäre vielleicht spannend, wenn eine Art Meta-Progression eingebaut wäre. Zum Beispiel könnte das Öffnen der Truhe dem Spieler Erfahrung oder dauerhafte Upgrades verleihen, sodass man beim nächsten Durchgang mit besseren Startwerten beginnt. So würde ein erneutes Durchspielen noch motivierender werden.

[h2] Данная игра помогла мне закрыть один гештальт, проработать одну мою детскую травму... [/h2]


Когда я был совсем-совсем маленький, меня часто отправляли в деревню к бабушке и дедушке.

У них был довольно большой участок с домом, баней, сараем и, само собой, с огромным количеством свободного пространства, где ничего не стояло и не росло. Тогда я любил смотреть телеканал Нешенл Джеографик, на котором часто транслировались репортажи про полезные ископаемые, археологию, руды и прочие ништяки, которые обычно находятся под землёй. Под впечатлением от данных передач я решил, что выкопать шахту на частной собственности моих прародителей, найти там алмазы и разбогатеть будет отличной идеей. 

Я уведомил всех своих деревенских кентов о том, что с завтрашнего дня я начинаю раскопки, и они могут присоединятся ко мне, чтобы потом вместе делить прибыль. Я горел этой идеей, я был уверен в том, что этот план обречён на успех. Я копал утро, день и вечер, в рекламные перерывы, во время просмотра "Спокойной ночи, малыши". Я пропускал обед, договаривался с новыми и новыми людьми втянуться в мою темку...

Так проходила неделя за неделей, моя яма становилась всё глубже и глубже, находки становились только интереснее, от скелетов мелких животных до гильз. Если взглянуть на внутреннюю стенку, то можно было лицезреть градиент сменяющихся пород. Земля, грязь, глина, какая-то чёрная zaluра, потом темно-зелёная твёрдая масса... Когда мы доходили до грунтовых вод, мы останавливались, чтобы подождать пока они уйдут, и потом снова восстанавить работу.

Яма вышла славная. Метра 2-3. Воспоминания о самом процессе только положительные. 

Но вот настала пора возвращаться домой и отложить этот вопрос до следующего года. Я жму руку всем моим коллегам и, надевая свои колготки с человеком-пауком, фантазирую о том, как через год я вернусь сюда с новыми силами, и доведу начатое дело до конца.

Вот проходит год, я, с бесконечной мотивацией в этот раз всё-таки докопаться до несметных сокровищ, собираюсь к любимой бабушке в деревню. 250 км в вонючей буханке, 4 с половиной часа по грунтовке... и вот он я. Стою наперевес с лопатой напротив места где когда-то красовалась яма, которую я копал, копал, копал... Теперь там не было горы инструментов, грунтовых вод и красивого градиента... 

Всё, что было в том месте, так это EБYЧИЙ КУСТ EБYЧEГО КРЫЖОВНИКА, который дед посадил, как только я умчался в большой город. 

Морали нет. Я рот eбaл крыжовника.


[h1] Итог [/h1]
Игра смогла вернуть меня в тот самый момент, когда я без еды, воды и задней мысли находился в самом что ни на есть состоянии потока, которое ищу по сей день в какой-нибудь иной от копания ямы деятельности. Философствовать можно сколько угодно, поэтому, девочки, кидайте мне свои фотки в личку. :D

It's a simple game based on a fun concept with underbaked execution.

It starts easy enough: you get a shovel and a yard, and you need to dig a hole. As you dig you find minerals, which you can sell to earn money. That money is then used to buy upgrades which help you dig faster or stay down in the hole longer.

For a digging game it's a shame that the digging itself is rather weak. Your shovel digs out a divot in the mesh in front of you, and only digs when there is material directly in your crosshair. In theory that's fine - why waste energy digging if there's nothing to dig? But in practice it means that unless you're perfect with your digging, you will end up with tiny bits of soil stuck in midair that will block your progress and can't be removed unless you perfectly aim at them. You'll often find them by taking fall damage after jumping in the hole and "landing" in midair on a speck of dirt.

To dig you click the left mouse button. There are no options to rebind this input, and no accessibility options. Holding down the mouse button does not continue to dig, so you have to spam the mouse button endlessly until you get one of the late game digging upgrades. Needless to say, clicking like crazy to move tiny piles of dirt gets old quick.

Speaking of upgrades, you have four pieces of equipment (your drill, inventory, battery, and jet pack) each with five upgrade tiers. Most people will max out their upgrades about an hour into the game, which is about as much time as you should expect to enjoy the experience. It would have been nice to have a more flushed out upgrade tree, or at least something else to spend your hard-earned dig money on.

My biggest issue with the game was the ending. Frankly, the ending is outright terrible. In a game about taking your time to dig a hole, it suddenly shifts genres to stealth horror with enemies that are unpredictable and inconsistent.

Yes, you can dig a big hole. No, I wouldn't recommend it.

The gameplay itself was enjoyable enough, and almost got me to the 1:1 dollar-for-hour ratio, albeit that I did multiple playthroughs to grab all the achievements, including 2-3 attempts to get the sub-30 minute speedrun achievement.

However, the game is strong in its journey and not its destination, as the ending is completely disconnected from everything that came before it. The ending of [i]A Game About Digging A Hole[/i] does not feel like it belongs to this game. It is only related to this game in that this ending is how this game ends. [spoiler]All of the upgrades and items including the jetpack and dynamite are forcibly taken away from the player in the final gauntlet, which is unexpectedly a frustrating stealth section that sends the player back to the surface upon being caught.[/spoiler] And it's so darn puzzling to me why this was chosen to be the game's conclusion of the gameplay; the final test of the player's skill and choices, especially since the tools for a more appropriate ending were already there. [spoiler] The player has a jetpack; the player has bombs; the player has a health bar. The game could have ended with the player flying around throwing bombs at a boss enemy in a boss arena, testing their movement skills and their upgrades in order to defeat the boss before being defeated themselves. And I'm completely puzzled to why such an ending or something similar wasn't implemented: it's possible technical or time constraints forced the developer's hand to pivot to something simpler, because I'm too optimistic to believe that the current ending was willingly implemented with no grievances.[/spoiler] But instead, the game has the ending it has now, and while it does somewhat tie up the little narrative the game had, it in no way ties up the gameplay loop.

For those who remember [i]Motherload[/i], the ending of the game [spoiler]had the player fight mecha-Satan using the upgrades and items (such as explosives) the player had originally acquired to help them reach the quite-literal boss fight in the first place, and despite there being no combat in the gameplay up to that point, it felt like an appropriate final test of the player's accrued piloting skills and upgrade choices for their drilling unit, ending in a spectacular finale.[/spoiler] I only wished this game took notes from [i]Motherload[/i] as the two have a lot in common with their overall gameplay experiences.

Still, the main gameplay loop before the ending was enjoyable enough that I'm tentatively recommending the game. I doubt I will play any more as I've gotten my fill from the game, but it was an enjoyable afternoon digging a hole.

If you're diving into this game, the Open Sky Mine is the best strategy. Instead of just going deep, focus on clearing out all the earth around you. This way, you won't need the jetpack or the lamp at the start, but you'll want them later in the game.

Hold off on buying dynamite until you've cleared the earth above the big rock. Instead, save up your money for a better shovel, battery, and storage upgrades.

At first, you’ll encounter rocks that can be sold (though who’s actually buying them?), then move on to find coal, steel, copper, silver, gold, platinum, and diamonds. Along the way, you’ll also discover useful items like a wallet, two keys for the casket in your garage, and two money bags. Don't forget the two abandoned mines and, at the very bottom, a mysterious dungeon!

The downside? Once you've upgraded everything, there’s not much left to spend your money on, aside from light, dynamite, batteries, and health. Adding the option to enter the house and buy decorations would’ve been a great way to use your leftover cash.

I may not be legally allowed to do this in my backyard, but you can bet I'm digging the biggest hole I can here. Simple, but satisfying game loop, and I've already beaten the game but plan to explore some more - there's some "NG+" type stuff to do.

a generic take on the Motherload concept, tried and true, so no originality towards the developer

Application, however, is entirely in their purview - how much of a benefit each upgrade is, additional tools available, how much time investment is required for each tier, etc. The time required for each is as expected, but the return is suboptimal.

Furthermore, physics and the engine do the concept a disservice - floating crumbs of dirt that will prevent movement as well as bounce your character when touched, lack of gravity(personal opinion for improving the genre), input delay, etc.

 On top of that, there's no reason why a game as simple as Motherload, though 3D, should be making GPU and CPU run at 80+C, with parts that are rated 255% more effective than the recommended requirements for this game.

Feels neither like a refreshing take, or a homage to the classics, You can find 170 copies of this game on roblox that will save you a coffee and run for longer playtime

[h2]진짜 있을지도 몰라! 일단 파보는 게임[/h2]
헐값에 내놓은 집, 그 앞마당에 보물까지 묻혀있다는 정보에 덜컥 집을 사버린 한탕주의 주인공의 본격적인 보물찾기 게임입니다. 페이지 본문 소개처럼 '커피 한 잔 값 정도' 가격으로 즐기는 오직 땅파기만 존재하는 게임이지만, 이 컨셉에 끌린 사람들의 호기심과 모험심 정도는 만족시킬 만한 규모의 지하세계가 있고, 공략을 위해 빠르게 구매할 수 있는 저렴한 장비 및 업그레이드 시스템은 캐주얼한 게임성을 보장하면서도 발굴 전략에 집중할 수 있게끔 보조해 주는 친절함을 동반하기도 합니다.

장비는 심플하지만 핵심적인 것들로 채워져 있습니다. 다양한 활동량을 늘려주는 배터리, 한종류로 고정되지만 투자를 통해 업그레이드 되는 발굴 도구, 판매할 자원을 담는 가방(인벤토리) 칸 추가가 주요 업그레이드 대상이고, 빠른 복귀를 위한 성능 좋은 제트팩을 조기 판매하기도 합니다! 설치형 램프와 극소 위력의 다이너마이트는 발굴 테마에 어울리면서도 어두운 지하를 헤쳐나가는데 매우 유용한 아이템들로, 발굴 현장의 몰입감을 높이는 데에도 영향을 끼칩니다.

주인공의 미래가 걱정될 정도의 깊이와 넓이로 파놓은 정원 아래를 드나들며 여러 가능성들에 대한 기대감과 조우를 이어나가는 모든 과정은 1.5 ~ 3시간 정도이며, 꽤나 중독적이고 만족스러운 경험이었습니다.

[h2]기타[/h2]
+엔딩 이후, 조건 달성시마다 트로피를 하나씩 추가해 나가는 업적 모드가 개방됩니다. (1회차때의 값도 포함, 누적됩니다) 이는 절차적 생성 스테이지의 회차 요소에 진입해서 통계 수치를 채우고 업적을 달성하는 정도의 의미를 갖습니다.

+업그레이드가 지원되지 않고, 직접 선택 할 수도 없으며, 근처에 다다랐을 때에만 자동으로 사용되는 [spoiler]디텍터[/spoiler]의 경우, 모든 장비의 업그레이드와 엔딩 이후에도 해당 방법으로 찾는 아이템을 보기 힘든 경우가 있어 발견되는 아이템의 가치 상승쪽으로든, 장비 활용 가능성 쪽으로든, DLC에서의 활약 가능성 쪽으로든(?) 개선이 필요해보입니다.

[h2]대강의 만족, 그리고 더 많은 것을 원하게 되는 게임[/h2]
수많은 가능성이 보일 정도로 좋았던 아이디어는 고작 14일이라는 기간에 작은 게임으로 실현되었기 때문에, 훌륭함과 동시에 아쉬움이 클 수 밖에 없었습니다. 게임의 성공과 토론장의 피드백들이 아이디어를 확장하고 실현하는데 도움이 됐으면 합니다.

굳이 따지자면 '동심의 규모'로, 어두운 지하를 조금씩 밝혀나가며 미지의 비밀을 발굴해 나가는 테마가 취향이신 분들에게, 단순하고 가볍지만 즐거운 모험심과 소유욕이 올라올 수 있는 경험을 주말 오전 혹은 새벽 즈음 1.5~2.5시간 정도 파고 들만한 '커피 한잔 값'의 게임으로서 추천할 수 있겠습니다.

[h1]A Game About Digging A Hole[/h1]

[b]A Game About Digging A Hole[/b] by [b]Cyberwave[/b] achieves taking a simple concept or idea and making something unique and enjoyable out of it.
The mechanics of the game are intuitive, and each time a new mechanic is introduced, it is done in a clear and understandable manner.

The core component of gameplay involves digging a hole, collecting ores and selling them, buying upgrades for your equipment, and digging even more!
The game doesn't really show any increase in difficulty besides one specific section and one specific achievement, therefore it globally remains within a casual range.

The visual aesthetics of the game are clean, polished, and of good quality.

[b]A Game About Digging A Hole[/b] is overall a good quality, simple, unique, and enjoyable experience from [b]Cyberwave[/b], featuring a serious challenge for those who wish to unlock all achievements.

全部の実績を開放してみていろいろ分かったこと。
＜良いところ＞
・この価格で予想以上に遊べる
・一度クリアしても実績が解放されて何回も遊べて色々な試行錯誤ができて良かった
・日本語対応してくれている
＜悪かったところ＞
・日本語訳が機械のため分かりづらい
・何回もやっていると最初にチマチマやるのが面倒くさくなる
＜総評＞
低価格でこのボリュームはとても満足でき、まだ発売されて一日も経っていないため更なるアップデートや追加コンテンツなども期待でき買ってよかった。


少しわかりづらいとこや小ネタ
・最速の移動方法はバニホ
・途中で出てくる「up」と「down」が書かれている装置は同じ高度に近づくほど中心の円が光り、同じ高度でも遠くに離れていると反応しないこともある為注意が必要。
・実績にある「無駄」はバックパックが限界の時に鉱石を40個掘ると達成できます
・四秒間落ち続ける実績は私の場合ジェットパックで高度限界から一番下の層まで落ちて達成しました。検証してないので分からないのですが、恐らくジェットパックなしでも地表からでもいけるかも。

this is a charming game about digging a hole! it took me just over 2 hrs to complete it.. well kinda. there seems to be more to discover, and if nothing else there are some fun things at the end (wont spoil surprise) 
this is actually a nice throwback to games of old in how it rewards you too! (i think)
overall for a cup of coffee i spent 2 hrs of fun and enjoyment digging holes, upgrading gear, and discovering things... 
also, this is really well made, like its short of course, but there's literally animations/cut-scenes (start and end) and whatnot, that are just like... well i guess usually a game like this would be made by an indie dev, and in a way this one kinda was too, made by the art guy of the solar punk devs in their free/holiday time honestly i would say this is one of those rare gems of you get what you pay for and even if you play just for an hr or two the love that went into this is well worth it!

if you like digging holes, or mining, or discovering quirky things i think you may well enjoy this game!

its also inspiring to me that it was only made in two weeks, and that it looks and plays so well! 

i can definitely see potential for so much more, but again its a price of a coffee, and if anything its kind of inspiring me too! there's a whole market here.

finally, if you want more voxel digging madness after this one (i certainly regained the itch) perhaps consider checking out hydroneer afterwards!
(that one is far more complicated/in depth but its certainly more digging.) 
oh and one last thing, i want to say my experience personally, not only did i have fun but i also got a good laugh out of the ending, it was almost like a puzzle for me.. kind of. (well not really  a puzzle but a light exercise in "how do i overcome this challenge")
it just dawned on me upon entering new game plus what the two keys i found was for... alas im already in NG+ never mind... maybe ill find them again! XD and i really have no clue how to get that speed runners trophy, but i want it!

edit2: i have completed 3 runs, on the fence whether i try for a 4th as i was so close to the 30 min mark (36 mins) the speed run achievement is doable, i have seen people go as fast as 18 mins on youtube! i feel like this has speedrunner potential in general too!

run 1 was a casual 2hrs ish run, run 2 was a bit more drawn out because i wanted a couple achievements... and run 3 was my recent failed speed run attempt at 36 mins!

i also love how the trophy's kinda carry over between runs so you see a total of your stats overall between all your runs!
this is a charming game that you can play for a couple hrs to reach the end, or if an achievement hunter/completionist, will likely give you a couple more hours enjoyment on top!

A Game About Digging A Hole é um daqueles jogos com o loop de game play bem claro, cavar, coletar recursos, melhorar a escavação, com aquele começo de jogo massante onde cavar e muito chato, mas logo começa a ficar interessante com updates de equipamentos, o problema e que isso dura muito pouco, acredito que a base do jogo e solida para criar algo sobre isso, como novos equipamentos, novas formas de cavar e coisas do tipo, mas por hora o jogo parece focar so mais simples possível, sem variações de estrategia, nenhum mecânica adicionada posteriormente, é um jogo básico, realmente rapido, com um final definido, inesperado, mas não muito agradavel.

Mas vale a pena pelo preço? acredito que sim, tanto pelo jogo em si entregrar o que promete, quanto pelas possibilidade de se tornar algo realmente complexo no futuro, então se tiver 17$ sobrando ai, não vejo por que não gastar alguns minutos aqui.

Pontos negativos: 
- Extremamente limitado
- O jogo acaba quando vc esta começando a entrar na onda
- Sem desafios

Pontos Positivos:
- Jogo relaxante
- Mecânica base solida
- Boa exploração

At the time of writing this review I have "Beat the Game".

I would like to start by thanking the developer who chose to not take his break over the holidays and instead chose to create this in my opinion, great game. 

It is what it says it is, grab the shovel and dig, nothing more to it but there are a few things along the way. My hopes are that this game gets given some attention, the structure to a very deep and rich game is there and plenty to go off of with room for exploring the lore and further exploring just how deep this hole can go.

This next part I will start off by saying SPOILERS AHEAD, with that out of the way lets dive in to some of the things i think a game like this could really use..

Collectibles, it would be awesome to have items not only to sell, but to gather and keep around the garage we go back to so often. Lost shoe, artifacts, pieces of lore.. there's so much that can be used and preferably not hold our hand and simply let us discover it by chance. No radar indicating their direction or location. 

Physics, I feel like the developer already knows this, but the problem with digging in certain ways can leave small specks of dirt that get in your way, when using certain modes of transportation. I realise this is a one person team working on this.. and you are appreciated.

Difficulty, I chose to max out the shovel before progressing below 5 metres which is not a difficult task to do but then everything seemed very easy not that it was an issue, I think its something that should be stated as the cost for energy is cheap and the travel back n forth from the garage to the dig site is short there wasn't any need to upgrade the inventory, battery or jet pack until I wanted to dig deep and by that time you're making a ton of cash the upgrades fly by. I'd suggest scarcity to the ores, I don't know what the coding multiplier is but if upgrading your shovel nets you more spawns maybe lower that a tad for longevity. Or if there's simply that many ores just bring that down a bit.

Dynamite, the dynamite in-game worked great for rock clearing it did seem though if i tried I would be able to avoid all the "destroyable rocks" simply by digging around them. It would be nice to either have the ability to strap multiple together to have a bigger explosion or be able to upgrade the dynamite and increase its radius that way. 

Endgame, a lot could be done here with the excess of currency you can net yourself. Example.. You have 50k banked and have made it to the end, purchase another house with a tad different layout for the dig site, an increase in difficulty, new collectibles to be earned. Things like that..

I ask a lot out of a game that just came out but wow, did i ever have fun and that last part was super fun. I hope this game catches people attention because it is a great way to pass time and not ask much from a game. 

To the developer thank you again, easily an 8.5/10 for a game that is, what it says it is.

Reading this comments section reminds me why I hate listening to the wider gaming audience. Does this game last 1-2hrs? Sure, if you're trying to crush through it, and not taking advantage of the New Game+ mechanic. But is that the [b]point[/b] of this game? Kids, you're digging a hole. Digging a hole, and slowly upgrading your gear, making the digging easier, allowing you to use gadgets, to use explosives. It's a silly and fun l'il thing, and critically, [b]not made by a million dollar studio[/b]. I've seen reviews comparing this to [b]Fortnite[/b] and [b]Roblox[/b]. If you are comparing this game to those, you are not a serious person, your opinion could not be worth less. And speaking of worth, $5 for 2hrs (if you're in a rush) of silly fun? Made by an indie dev, who clearly made this for the joy of making a fun and simple game? [i]What else can you get for $5?[/i]

If the trailer for this game seems fun and the concept appeals to you? This game is [i]absolutely worth $5[/i]. If you want some 8hr adventure with significant depth, then go look at games by major publishers or larger studios. To argue the value of this game is utter clown shoe nonsense. It's fun. Buy it and have fun.

EDIT - I've now played for close to 3hrs, not min-maxing, not speedrunning, and I'm not done. I've unlocked the best digging equipment, and I'm 1 away from the best battery, but still plenty to dig and discover. So yeah, anyone talking about how it's a sub-1hr experience just rushed it, which runs entirely counter to what this game is about. Ignore the haters, this game is legit.

It was only $5 but when you consider that games with concepts nearly identical to this exist for free on Fortnite, Roblox, and probably other platforms that I'm not aware of, I would expect more out of this. For example, a game VERY similar to this on Roblox has way more tools to choose from, way more storage upgrade, pets that help you with mining, and is completely free to play. The only things that are paid in those games are some premium content that gives either infinite storage space or an OP drill/explosive that aren't even needed (and make the game finish too quickly).

I feel like if this game had a prestige option or something where you could keep playing and getting more and more powerful with each prestige it would provide at least a couple more hours or so of fun. Maybe I would challenge myself to 100% dig out every inch of the yard if the tools were upgraded to be powerful enough to justify the time it takes.

Still, 100% recommend to buy this game if you simply want to support the creator who made this game entirely during their free time. [b]Ну тут у нас однозначно претендент на игру года! Игра про копание ямы. И этим все сказано.[/b]

Название игры говорит само за себя: мы должны просто копать яму. Периодически, кроме камней, угля и прочих руд можно найти разные прикольные вещи. С локализацией сложности - "выход" это "отделка", "железо" это "утюг" и так далее. 
Есть некая "таинственная тайна", которую можно раскрыть (или же выкопать), что добавляет игре интереса.
Стоит ли игра 200 рублей? Если вы любитель таких нестандартных и проектов, то да. В противном случае - сомневаюсь. Однако, может быть, если зарыться глубже, то что-то интересное в ней и откроется, так как судя по трейлеру кто-то или что-то обитает в глубинах.

Für mich ist es ein Stück Nostalgie und die Erfüllung eines Kindheitstraums – ich wollte schon immer ein großes Loch im Garten buddeln. Nun kann ich es endlich in der virtuellen Realität umsetzen!  

Das Spiel lässt sich in weniger als einer Stunde durchspielen, wodurch eine Rückgabe theoretisch möglich wäre. Dennoch werde ich darauf verzichten, da ich die Entwickler mit diesen 5 € gerne unterstütze. Mit einem Koop-Modus und ein paar zusätzlichen Grafikoptionen wäre es für mich eine glatte 10/10!

PS: 
So nach nun 4,6 Stunden [Mit Toiletten pause] habe ich nun auch alle erfolge für Trophyhunter sind das einfache 10 erfolge für 5€ mit meiner Meinung Spaß verbunden.
